text:
After having used this piece of equipment for a week, I've concluded that this is a very cheaply-built, yet medium-high performing laptop. The key deck is plastic and flexes about .003" - .004" in the center under my keystroke pressure. I feel-out how much pressure is necessary to depress the keys. I typically apply this principle across the board in order to prevent undo wear and extend the life of my belongings. The keys are mushy but tactile enough to get the feel of how far they have to travel before registering. The keys are quieter than the ones on my Mid 2010 Apple MacBook Pro. The keyboard backlight is good. ASUS's TUF Aura Core app is required if you want to change the color and settings. There are only 3 brightness levels apart from "OFF." The brushed plastic finish is relatively easy to keep clean, but it's flimsy cheap as well. The machine performs well, but I'm mostly utilizing the i5-9300H processor and 8 GB of DDR4 RAM this has since I don't do intense gaming. It will accept up to 32 GB DDR4 2666 (PC4 21300) RAM. If gaming is what you're looking for, I would look up comparisons between 4 GB and 6 GB graphics cards. At this point, I think 6GB would be worth the difference. Use the function key and hit F5 to toggle between "silent, performance, and turbo." This corresponds to processors clock speed. Silent is about 1.8 GHz, performance is standard clock speed of 2.8 (?), And turbo around 4.0. Note that this has no internal optical drive, so you'll need to purchase a separate one if you want to run CDs/DVDs. The matte display is nice. I've had a glossy one for years. I think that the color reproduction is more realistic than most monitors I've seen.

Overall, I like it. I'll be babying it, but I think it will serve me well for a long time.

text:
My original magic mouse finally went on the fritz - not sure how many years I had it but I liked having a wireless mouse. I had also gotten used to the feel of the mouse, the gestured needed to switch screens, right and left click and so on. What I never got used to was the battery usage. It seemed every other week or so, I would get the screen notification that the mouse batteries were low and need to be changed soon. I keep my used batteries in a bag so that I can take them to recycling. I have a large bag full of batteries, many or which were used in the mouse.

The other problems with the original mouse were also battery-related: the door that enclosed the batteries was hard to fasten tightly with the result that it would fall off from time to time when I moved the mouse. The batteries also had to be snugly fit and if there was any looseness, which did happen from time to time, the mouse would lose blue-tooth connectivity periodically, connecting and reconnecting repeatedly. It took awhile for me to figure out this was a battery issue.

Still, I liked the mouse in spite of these annoyances and maybe I'm just a bit set in my ways. When the mouse finally died and no amount of jiggering could sustain the blue tooth connection and the battery compartment door just would not stay on, it was finally time. That is when I bought the Magic Mouse 2, a few weeks ago.

I am beyond happy with it. All of the battery-related problems have been eliminated. No more frequent changes, no more fiddling with the battery compartment door or batteries themselves. This mouse just works and I have had none of the other problems that other reviewers have reported. I don't find it uncomfortable, it's responsiveness is fine, and I don't have blue tooth connectivity problems. Every other night or so when I turn off my monitor, I hook the mouse up to its charger, which is connected to a USB hub, and I'm ready to go in the AM.

I would say that if you are a current or former magic mouse user looking to upgrade and get rid of the battery-eating model, this is a good choice for you. You will maintain continuity with the mouse gestures you've grown used to using and the feel of the mouse will be identical. I also recommend getting a Logitech wireless solar keyboard to free yourself from the cord completely while also not needing batteries or even recharging.

If, however, you are used to other mouse types with a larger body and defined keys for left and right clicking, you might find this mouse a bit uncomfortable and foreign and should look elsewhere.

text: The Garmin Edge 1000 is a great little gps/bicycle computer....most of the time. My biggest complaint is that every so often, it decides to do whatever it damn well pleases!  I had a long diatribe, but have decided to go the Ernest Hemingway route.  Sometimes screen buttons flash on, then off, too quickly to be pushed. Sometimes I push, they blink and come back- power not off, ride not saved (but at least not lost either; try again. And again.). Sometimes I push and...... nothing. Battery life is a mystery. 2 months of no riding, battery at 87%. One hour ride. Next day, battery at 0%. (Yes, I hit the POWER OFF bar on the screen. And yes, I have gotten all the firmware updates.) Odometer readings for the same route, ridden often, will vary by several hundredths of a mile.  The out and back of a turnaround course should be the same, and never are.  No comment on navigation, I've rarely used the gps function.  It pairs with sensors easily, no problem there, although there are occasional times it has trouble finding the cadence sensor at the start of a ride.  Battery life of 15 hours? Not even close, and I now leave it plugged in overnight. Every night.  I know it could do so much more than I ask of it, but all I ask is that it DO what I ask of it- turn on, stay on, don't freeze up; speed, distance, cadence, heart rate; have the screen actually react to a touch *every* time. Tonight I was going to ride, racing sunset. The Garmin decided to freeze up, and then it was too late to ride. Infuriating. It works well most of the time, but infrequently and sporadically (no pattern that I'm aware of, although I will start tracking malfunctions to see if there is one) it freezes up. Would I recommend it to a friend? I don't think so. And I wish I didn't have so much money tied up in peripherals, or I'd seriously consider getting something else. Who knows? Maybe I'll go back to my wired Cateye Astrale.
title: Every so often it decides not to cooperate

text:
I have owned a few different generations of Kindles in the past and have generally loved reading on them. I like the fact that it gives you great convenience of holding tons of books wherever you go in a very compact form factor, and the impressive battery life thanks to the e-paper technology.

The last Kindle I had was a 9th generation Oasis, which was an upgrade from a Paperwhite. I was very much disappointed with the 9th generation Oasis mainly due to issues with the screen backlight. The backlight on the device had uneven light distribution on the screen - so one side of the screen (where the buttons are placed) was very brightly lit when compared to the other side. And the issue was something which cannot be ignored since it was quite evident while reading in dark when you have to completely rely on the backlight to see the text. It was a bad experience for me since I had to pay a premium price for an ebook reader. I had got it replaced twice but the issue still persisted, indicating that the design of the product itself had the issue.

While I was struggling with the 9th generation Oasis, I saw that the 10th generation was out and apparently the backlight issues were no longer present in the new device. I waited for some time for the reviews to flow in to see if there were any major issues with it. And finally, I traded in my 9th generation Oasis with the 10th generation and I am so glad that I made the decision to upgrade to 10th generation.

All my complaints from the previous generations are solved, and the amber lighting on the screen is amazing and I now use it almost 100% of the time. It gives you the feeling like you are reading on a real paper book. The 300 ppi resolution of the screen is very crisp for daily reading and the battery life is good enough but it could have been better. I feel that this is a Kindle that I can finally keep for a longer time to read my books and I am happy that Amazon made this small incremental update to fix an issue they had with the previous generation. I would have appreciated even more if they had acknowledged the screen issue they had but anyway, I am happy with this upgrade.
title: Finally a Kindle that I can keep for long term

text:
I wanted to use the Si5351A in a design and thought it would be worthwhile to test it's programming and capability with this breakout board. I connected to a Raspberry Pi4 I2C. The easiest way to get the required values for any frequency is the ClockBuilder Pro program from Silicon Labs and have it generate all the register settings. I manually asked for 40 frequencies (500KHz to 20MHz in 500KHz increments) and put them into a CSV file then wrote a program that will read the CSV file, find and set the requested frequency. Worked so well I decided to take an older Raspberry Pi2B , bought female 40pin socket and small plated perf board and made a clock generator for my work bench. I can VNC from my laptop to set the frequency I want.
NOTE: The SiLab spec sheet says the part's range is 2.5kHz to 200MHz. I verified 2.5kHz and 100MHz (my digital scope's limit).
title: Verified capability

text:
This mouse is available on Amazon in two different colors - black or blue. Some of the photos don't do justice for this small dark blue mouse. The top side of the mouse is a dark shade of blue, while the underside (which you don't see when using the mouse) is an aqua light blue. The scroll wheel matches the underside.

The blue mouse looks good when used with a navy blue or royal blue laptop (like the ASUS Zenbook UX370).

This mouse is smaller than a normal desktop mouse, but not as tiny as some travel mice. Will fit most hands comfortably. I'm 6'2" with large hands and enjoy using the mouse when sitting at the couch, while my 5'1" daughter with small hands can use the mouse anywhere for many hours doing school work without issue.

The mouse has a small blue light that flashes when in Bluetooth pairing mode.

Ordered this mouse from Amazon, received the next day, pulled the mouse from its package, opened the battery door and removed the pull-tape from the battery, closed the battery door, and while the blue light was flashing on the mouse, turned on a Bluetooth-equipped Windows laptop, went into the Control Panel, Devices, Bluetooth, Add Device, and Windows immediately paired with the mouse. No special software install necessary for Windows 10. Easy setup!

Logitech states this mouse will work with Mac and Windows computers, Android mobile devices and Chromebooks.

The mouse has an on/off switch adjacent to the battery door. It was "on" when received new, but there is a pull-tape for shipping to avoid the mouse running until you unpack it. I believe the mouse automatically sleeps when not in use, but this doesn't present a challenge to wake-up when you're ready to use again. The small blue light on the mouse only flashes when in pairing mode, and doesn't appear to turn on at any other time, effectively hidden.

The optic under this mouse works on many different surface types without issue, to include wood tables, white plastic tables, leather armrests, cloth armrests, blue plastic and gray plastic surfaces of laptop palmrests, jeans, etc. I haven't tested this mouse on a clear glass table, which may give it a challenge. If you absolutely need a mouse that will work on _any_ surface, the "Logitech MX Anywhere 2S" model uses darkfield technology which reportedly will work on clear glass (and costs significantly more than this M535 model).

When shipped, the mouse will arrive in clear plastic packaging. The backside of the plastic is perforated, making it very easy to open, _without_ having to cut into the plastic with scissors or other tools.

The primary benefit of using a Bluetooth mouse versus a wireless USB mouse is that operating in native Bluetooth mode with a PC or Android device that supports Bluetooth allows you to use the mouse without having to deal with a small USB dongle necessary in other wireless models. This is an especially important feature for newer model thin laptops that don't have many USB ports, and/or you may not want an extruding dongle connected to the laptop.

In daily operation, I've not encountered any challenges with this mouse. Works well in Windows 10 with default settings. No problems with accuracy, lag or jitter. Responds well during light gaming sessions.

Overall, thumbs up, and would buy again! No complaints.
title: Bought navy blue, works great!

text: Well, I did not do my research and bought this HD radio thinking I could pick up AM reception without fading and static. I live 100 miles east of NY city, and yes, I get 1010 WINS and 880 WCBS during the day., both are which are 50,000 watts. At night I get 1/2 dozen more in HD. I have a CCrane internet radio and thought the reception is the same. It's not. I guess not enough AM/FM HD yet. At night the radio is great at picking up AM stations hundreds of miles away in standard mode.  The radio is well built, excellent sound and very good stereo separation on FM. On FM, the HD has about 1/2 dozen stations, so far. text:
I got these for my perfectly healthy kids, ages 2, 4 and 7. I worry that they could get separated, lost or kidnapped. I also bought several different accessories from the jiobit website for attaching these on my kids.
After using this for about a week, this is my impression:
- The battery doesn't last very long after kid is separated from caretakers. We were at Grandma's, and kids, with my permission, left with their aunts for an hour or 2. By the time they returned, their batteries were down to 20% or so, and the devices ran out of juice pretty soon after. 2 hours are hopefully enough to find a missing kid, but you can't send kid with a caretaker who doesn't have the app installed, without risking battery drain.
- The devices are waterproof, and by that, I mean, laundry proof. A device got accidentally left on an outfit my kid discarded, and survived the entire wash routine with no trouble.
- The many ways to attach the device to kids are all useful. My 2 year old, I need to use the pin pouch to attach it to her, otherwise, she will manage to get rid of it, somehow. My older 2, one prefers it in his pocket, and the other prefers it on a belt clip hidden under his shirt.
- They work well, overseas.
- You can't talk to kids through them, or hear the kids.
- They can be very frustrating in apartment buildings or malls, where you can see that the kid is somewhere in the gigantic building, but not where.
- You can make the jiobit ring, which is useful for finding it, but also for letting kids know that they need to turn up.

Overall, these are very lightweight, and the only usable trackers in the market, but could still do with substantial improvement!

For those who are concerned about bubbles, I suggest that you carefully read every instruction before beginning your installation. Then get yourself situated with everything you need. Put all the supplies on the table in front of you as if you were about to perform surgery. Choose an area with good lighting, and no dust. Minimize dust potential by turning off fans or closing windows. Consider removing sweaters or other articles of clothing that could drop lint in your workspace. Finally, wash your hands and don’t hesitate to let them air dry. When you are ready to begin your installation, read the instructions again. If after all of these efforts you spot a piece of dust under the shield, gently life the protector by the corner closest to the speck, and use the edge of a plastic spoon to gently scrape the speck of dust toward the edge until it can fall away. Do not touch the underside of the shield with your fingers. Once the speck is removed, let the corner make contact with the screen again and smooth out any bubbles. The protector should be invisible if it is installed correctly. I hope this helps. Good luck!

text:
I have had this little dude for about a year now. I have it running in-between my PC and AMP (4x splitter). I bought this unit for the price and the fact that it has Bass, Treble, and Volume on the unit so I could tune it to my liking and balance the sound to my amp.

Overall, it produced a "pretty good" sound and I was quite pleased especially at the price point.

Over the past year, I have become a bit of a "mid-level audiophile" and have added a couple of DAC's to my iPad and phone (one cabled and one Bluetooth) with various adapters, balanced headphones, etc... to get the sound I wanted from my (as you all know) quite expensive portable devices. They now sound fantastic, especially with balanced headphones.

So, when that was completed, I turned my attention back to my desktop setup. I went through my devices, one at a time, and found after adding the Beyerdynamic DT 880 Premium 250ohm headphones to the PC setup I could hear I needed to do something about the sound.

After some connecting and disconnecting and playing around with the wiring setup for the amp, PC, and pre-amp I determined the pre-amp was the issue. I was going to get a more "top of the line" one but then came across a post about how the tubes make a HUGE difference. Okay. I can see that.

So, instead of ordering a new unit I purchased an upgraded set of tubes for this particular tube amp. I went with the Riverstone Audio (just search for 6j1 tube here on Amazon). I installed them last night and this morning thought "eh... let's give this setup one more shot." Holy-Cow! Everyone was right! Tubes make a HUGE difference! It's like I have a new pre-amp! The soundstage is incredible. The separation and soundstage are magnificent from my desktop Bose speakers. WOW! Truly blown away with how this little 180.00 dollar setup sounds now (Nobsound NS-10P Mini Vacuum Tube Preamp + Riverstone Audio Tube Upgrade + ART HeadAMP4 Eight Output Stereo Headphone Amplifier = all available here on Amazon).

Folks, for a PC setup... I'm good now. Really. Games sound better. Music just fills the room. I'm pretty blown away how this setup now sounds. I recommend this unit (with the tube upgrade) wholeheartedly.

text:
The cameras are average, we've been with this company for over 3 years now and have only stuck around in hopes that the updates over the years would bring more functionality AND reliability. Well the only credit I will give the developer is that they finally delivered on functionality at a mediocre level. Reliability is still lurking somewhere between the bottom of the dumpster and the oily, grimy asphalt below it.

The good:
-The cameras (we use 2 orbs as baby monitor cams, WARNING: these rarely stay on longer than 30 minutes, so it's not a set it and fall asleep camera) have great night vision, like super detailed night vision
-The resolution/quality is a 8/10 (they offer UltraHD, HD, and Standard in the app settings, but it's not truly UltraHD. Probably 1080p I think)
-The mics are super sensitive so you can hear baby's softest whimpers or cries.

The bad (I'll abridge this list for the sake of time):
-Alexa compatibility is awful. If you can get it to work on FireTV sticks and/or FireTV Cube (we have both), it's decent. There's a timeout (not sure if it's intentional or a software flaw as it's never a set amount of time) where it just closes the camera after 10-35 minutes. This also happens on the iPhone app (I'll talk about that in a second), but at least does you the service of warning you with a 15-20 second countdown so you can push to keep it going.
-The FireTV app does not offer ANY interactive features. You can only tell the Alexa to show the camera by name. You also cannot just switch to another camera with your voice. It will freeze the app. You must go home, wait 5-10 seconds, then tell it to show a different camera.
-The iPhone app (also on the iPad as a shrunken iPhone version) is decent, like 6/10 decent. It has been updated over a dozen times since we started and it now offers what you'd expect in 2020: split screen for multi-camera view (not available on FireTV apps, just mobile/tablets), various settings, controls to move your camera around the room, FaceID/TouchID, etc. The auto-record motion detection is garbage, fills up your cloud, and the cloud itself is the most confusing thing in the world to setup. You get a free month trial but if you try to stop it/extend it, etc it just doesn't confirm you've done anything and always says it's active
-The Alexa Skill is pure garbage, with limited functionality and hit or miss everytime you try to login. I'm actually writing this review right now because for the umpteenth time the skill has stopped working on my FireTV Cube and I tried the usual disable, re-enable and re-login. Usually works but now the site to login just won't load, via the app or the web browser.

Good luck if you already bought into this company and are stuck. If you're considering it, DON'T!! Spend the money and get something more reliable.
title: Great if you just want to check on the camera occasionally and are ok with unreliability

text:
Short version: great customer service and would buy again.

Long version:
My wife wanted a new stereo for her birthday.

I took a risk on buying this because of the custom fit for our Kia Forte5 SX. I didn’t like the “chin” on the dash kits that were available and was getting quotes of $800 for a factory looking faceplate for the stereo, taking it to $2,000 for everything at a local shop.

There are not a lot of reviews and not a ton of info on the listing, but for the cost difference I thought I would risk it and it payed off. Definitely worth it.

When I got the unit they had already wired the connectors for the car and it was done well.

However, there was a problem. There are a couple different stereos and wiring setups for this car and ours had a different on than standard.

I contacted the seller and got a response in an hour. They responded to numerous questions about setup, wiring, steering wheel controls, connections etc. I sent them the wiring diagram and even the weird factory USB connector on my model that nobody makes an adapter for. They just sent me an email that the adapter is on its way.

The steering wheel controls worked great, no adapter needed, but you will need to program them which is easy.

The radio works well, still figuring it all out. There is a manual that goes over some stuff, but a lot more there than the manual can cover.

You can see the pic, I replaced one of the cigarette lighters with a dual USB that connected to the ones from the stereo. The third USB will be the factory one once the adapter gets here.

For the factory backup camera, you will need a voltage step down converter, fairly easy to install. I set it up so camera is always on.

There are some slight differences in gaps, which slightly bug me, but I’m not ocd so I am able to mostly ignore.

Also, the only mounting is the front bezel/faceplate. It seems plenty strong, but I wish it had side brackets like the factory.

A few things still working on.
Mic could be louder when I call people they have trouble hearing. . Right now it’s on steering column, will try and move to headliner.

Volume control, some things need more volume and switching from phone back to music can be a problem. Looking for an app from the Play store.

I may add some more accessories down the road like the front camera

Definitely Worked our well and my wife really likes it. Wireless Apple Carplay works great, but can be a little slow to reconnect.

Connected as my secondary mesh router. It works very well to extend my network out to my detached garage. My main router is installed in the front of my house (living room) and this is set up in the back of my house (kitchen) and the 2.4 Ghz and 5ghz networks connect my devices seamlessly wherever I am on my property. My single router could not do this while maintaining a strong signal. Very pleased with the Asus brand of Wifi routers.

It was easy to set up the mesh network, but it did take a couple of attempts before it worked. The Android app lets you see what devices are connected and you can see what router they are currently connected to. FireStick and Samsung TV devices are able to connect to this 5 Ghz network, but my previous Apple Airport Extreme somehow did not put out a 5 Ghz signal that those devices could "see." So, that is a nice network speed upgrade for a lot of my devices.

I approve and would would recommend it to create a mesh network along with your main Asus router. I don't know about mixing brands.

We recently bought a whole new TV setup (TV, sound bar, TV mount and sound bar mount) and I wanted white cables to connect everything (so that the cables would be somewhat hidden in the white cabinet that we were installing everything in). The local store where I'd normally buy an ethernet cable only had either blue or black cables. Thankfully it was easy enough to order these Amazon Basics ones and they seem great!

One little nitpick I have with ethernet cables is the little tab that you press to disconnect them. Most manufacturers put some kind of protective cap around that part of the cable. Sometimes they make that protective layer either really fat (which can make plugging the cable into a tight spot tricky) or somewhat rigid which can make pressing the tab to unplug it tricky. These still have that coating, but it's nice and slim and flexes easily.

I'm currently using this cable to connect a Sonos Beam and I've had zero issues so far.
title: Thank goodness for Amazon Basics

text:
This seems like a pretty decent camera, though its no GoPro for the price you really can't beat it, so I bought 2 of them to give one to a friend. I've had it a couple days now and have been using it on my bike rides to test it out, the real test will come next week when I head out to Colorado to do some skiing.

First thing is this camera comes with a ton of accessory mounts and a remote control to start and stop video and take photos. Give yourself a good hour to unpack it and to get use to how to access the menu to set up the camera and charge the batteries. The one thing Im not really happy about is that it comes with a real vague start up guide and you have to download the user manual online. I know most manufacturers do this now, but there seems to be about 3 or 4 different manuals for the EK7000 out there, so make sure you fine the correct one.

The small back screen is nice and clear, and once you figure out how the menu and settings work, its actually pretty easy to use, I set my video setting at 1080p 30 fps using a 64gb micro SD card, and could get about a hour or so of video on one battery charge and it used almost 2GB on the card. Im going to try out and see how 720p 60fps works out as far as battery life goes. The video playback on my PC looked really good at 1080p and though the stabilization was pretty good it wasn't and clean and smooth as a GoPro in my opinion, but definitely wasn't a deal breaker. The camera seems really good too, but I've only got a couple pictures of my cat so far.

They have a App for viewing photos and video playback that works decent, but for some reason after viewing a video it would lose WiFi connection every time when you went back to "camera preview" for some reason. Not a real big deal, but you just have to reconnect and it will work, and whats nice about the "camera preview" is that you can adjust the camera angle when the camera is mounted on your helmet and get the angle you want without guessing.
title: Great Sports Camera For The Price

text:
Truly wireless earbuds are game changing. Being able to listen to music so easily without fear to getting snagged is wonderful.

These earbuds do not have the best sound or ANC but the complete package is magical for iOS users. Sound is decently well rounded. These do well across a wide range of music genres, audiobooks and movies/shows. ANC is surprisingly strong but will not compare to larger over ear models. Transparency mode keeps you engaged with your surroundings. The integration with iOS is what really sets these apart from competitors. Seamless pairing across all your Apple devices and Siri features.

If you’re on Android, look elsewhere unless ANC is top priority. There are many other options that perform close or better for cheaper. For iOS users, the regular AirPods provide 90% of this experience for a much more reasonable price. If ANC is a must and you’re living that blue bubble life, it’s hard to beat this set of earbuds for battery life, performance, and portability.

text:
Overall, this camera is great for the money and does exactly what is advertised. I'm glad I waited for a month to write a review because some of the areas that I felt were lacking turned out to be supported. The camera setup was easy for me. It quickly connected to my wifi and began to work.

The Netvue app is good too. It shows live feeds and stores still shots of any motion detected. At first, I couldn't figure out how to replay the video for the still shots but I figured it out. It is actually very cool because it appears that the camera is always recording to the local memory card so you can easily go back to the point in time that the motion was detected and play the video before/after. That was something that I had to figure out but has been working flawlessly ever since. I highly recommend buying the max memory card with the unit. You won't need to use Cloud storage if you have sufficient storage in the camera.

One of the best features is the ability to interface with Alexa. We have a Fire TV and I can simply say "Alexa, show the front door" and I will immediately see the live feed on my TV. That is so cool!!

There are a few minor complaints that I have but they really are minimal compared to the great features:
-There are three cords that come out of the back of the camera. Not a big deal if you plan to mount on a wall and tuck the cords behind it. However, if you mount direct to a surface like I did, the cords will hang out. I had to wrap them in a plastic bag and rubber band them to the top of the camera. It doesn't look pretty but it works.
-The motion detection isn't perfect. Most of the alerts come from headlights as cars go by. There were a few times that it didn't catch a package delivery but the majority of the time, I get an instant notification when cars are going up and down the driveway.
-The live playback is a little choppy but still very good.

Again, this camera is definitely worth it for the money. The features will definitely outweigh any minor inconveniences. Definitely recommended!!
title: Great outdoor camera for the money

I buy and use a lot of wall-mount racks. While I'd prefer to sell high end equipment to my clients, budget often requires some value engineering. For several years I've used Navepoint racks and drawers and I am very satisfied with the product.

This is a quality rack for the money. Other lower cost racks have very poor hinge designs, sag with only a little weight in them, and generally look cheap. This looks like an expensive pro rack, at a "pro-sumer" price. I routinely load these up with about 60 pounds of gear, and they don't sag.

The hinge is strong. The door is quality perforated steel- not a cheap piece of acrylic. 3 locks are included, though I generally use only one and keep the others as spares. Important to note is that Navepoint knows how to box a rack, whereas many others ship their cheap rack in a crummy box and they arrive damaged. I've not had a damaged Navepoint rack, and I've used at least 100 of the 6, 9, and 12U models.

You really can't go wrong for the money. If you spend 3x on the rack, you may get a better product- but there is no guarantee. Highly recommended.

text:
This is my first pair of truly wireless earbuds. Other devices I have include a Plantronics Voyager Focus, which is my primary go-to at work, Powerbeats 3, and a pair of soundpeats magnetic bluetooth workout earbuds (similar to Powerbeats). These TrueCapsules are my favorite, hands-down. (The Powerbeats are my least favorite)

Pros:
While the Focus is pretty tough to beat in terms of battery life and noise cancellation (for both mic and speakers), the TrueCapsules are the most comfortable buds I've ever owned. I'm usually not a fan of ear buds. I have an oddly shaped right ear canal, and because of that I can never seem to find a earbud diaphragm that works properly. Especially when working out, they always tend to wiggle loose and fall out. Historically, the only earbuds that have stayed put for me have been the standard Apple earphones, which don't really "suction" into place, but simply rest in your ear. Until now! SoundPeats nailed it; their diaphragm is the perfect size and texture for my weird ear. They are very comfortable for me, unlike my Powerbeats, which start hurting my ears after a half-hour or so (and doesn't sit properly in my right ear, anyways). And they fit better.

I am not an audiophile. I listen to a lot of music and I have my own ideas of when music sounds good and when it sounds lousy. These earbuds, in my opinion, outperform my Powerbeats, in regard to audio quality. Hard to believe the Soundpeats device is going to produce better audio than Beats hardware, but they sound better, to me. If I had to guess why, I'd say it's because they sit more flush in my ear, which lets me hear a wider range of sound and deeper bass. I don't think the battery life is quite as good as the Powerbeats, but I'm still VERY happy with this purchase.

Cons:
I'm still trying to get used to the touch controls; I think you can do everything you might need to do with different variations of tap and touch, but I try to keep the manual nearby. I'm also always accidentally pausing music and turning them on when I don't want to. Turning the volume up/down is a pretty slow endeavor, but these are minor gripes that shouldn't dissuade anyone from trying these guys out.

UPDATE - Three Years Later
My beloved SoundPEATS earbuds fell apart recently when I was trying to find a more optimal-fitting ear cushion. The glue holding the two plastic pieces together gave way and ... bam. i could see the innards of the left earbud. Immediately I thought to myself: well, i can either try to get creative with a little superglue, or I could drop $150 bones on a higher quality set of buds. Superglue did the trick. We're back in business.
title: Nothin' Defeats SoundPEATS

I was very excited to get this product and that emotion lasted all of about 3 minutes. The most glaring problem was the backdrop stands were only 7’ tall, not the advertised 8.5’. This was a deal breaker so I sent the unit back. However, I will provide some insight into the items that I did unpack and look at. (Which weren’t many.)

For starters, the backdrop stands were a bit flimsy for my taste. This is certainly not a heavy duty unit but I suspect the stands actually would do the trick, provided they weren’t challenged to hold much more than the backdrops that came with the unit and weren’t moved around much. The stand legs don’t click into a set configuration — this may be good, or bad, depending on your needs. If you like the hassle of trying to get the two stands the same height then this may work in your favor. If you don’t enjoy that task, you might want to keep looking. This feature could be useful if you are working on uneven ground, but that had better be inside because I doubt these units will work very well outdoors. Sandbags might help and would definitely be worth trying for stability. I did not assemble the crossbar after discovering the stands were too short. The stands and crossbar came in a pretty nice case that flips open to allow access to three pouches that hold the stands and bar. The case wasn’t super strong (I didn’t expect it to be for this price) but it seemed more than adequate for its purpose.

I also assembled one of the softbox units and I was pleasantly surprised. Although it was a tad cumbersome to click together, it was sturdy enough and seemed like it would last a long while, given proper care and handling. The umbrellas were, well, umbrellas and not much can go wrong there, though not suggested for outdoors with any kind of wind.

All in all, had the stands been tall enough I would probably have kept the product and just lived with it. I believe the lighting portion of this setup was its strength, though I expect the light stands would have been the same quality as the backdrop stands and therefore a bit disappointing.

Be wary of build quality. Leaving this backdrop unit set up in a studio would probably be its best use case. In any case, limiting the number of setup/teardown is suggested. I didn’t fully assemble the lights but expect similar build quality.

In summary, if your needs are for a lightweight all-in-one kit, and you don’t mind the aggravation of adjusting both light stand feet and poles to get identical height, then perhaps you’ve come across an item to put on. the short list. It was a good price for a lot of gear, especially as a starter set! Just be sure to set your expectations accordingly!

text: Received my echo 3rd Gen unit over the holidays due to an ongoing promotion. It has great sound over the Dot version hands down - good base and highs. It takes a bit of investment of your time to learn all the nuances of what Alexa can do for you. With the app, you can set up your Echo to be an alarm clock, timer, grocery list, teach it a routine for each day (like giving the weather forecast, the latest news from a specific news source, turn on/turn off lights, thermostat control, play specific music (classical, rock, pop) etc.). But beware, the instructions for all this are not included with your Echo. You have to dig around (through e-books, YouTube, etc.) to become familiar with the commands and required outcomes. For example, my unit began to display a pulsating yellow light that became annoying at night in my bedroom. I couldn’t turn it off except by disconnecting the power. Of course, this could’ve become a deal breaker if I had to disconnect every nite (I kept all the shipping package just in case I needed to return it). Well, it turned out that this was one way the Echo communicates with you. It was trying to tell me It had a notification for me to listen to. Until I asked, “Alexa, do I have any notification?” the yellow pulsating light would’ve continued. Immediately after delivering all notifications, the yellow pulsating light stopped. By the way, the notifications were about shipping/delivery of packages coming from, wait for it...Amazon. Of course, other types of notifications are possible pending how you program your Echo. Like I said, this simple issue would’ve been a deal breaker for me if I hadn’t decided to invest some of my time in trying to resolve this simple problem. It wasn’t until I learned how to communicate with my Echo that the problem wouldn’t go away. But again, the answer was not included with this product. My feedback to Amazon would be to include a list of commands and a trouble shooting section for the buyer. By employing this one simple act, I’m sure these products would be in far more demand by their customers once they learn the how to’s of communicating with these aliens. Beginning to love my Echo!
title: Great sound but be prepared for a learning curve on how to command your Echo!

text:
This case is beautiful, it is easy to fit a decent amount of components inside and leaves room for a clean build.
Managing the plethora of cables that make this case shine the it does is a hard task, I've put together countless rigs in the past, and this one does take some time to put together if you want to do a nice cable management job. Speaking of cables, fans and LEDs, the fans that actually come with this case are not the fans shown on the pictures. I have a friend who bought this case a few months ago, and his came with the nice fans shown on the pictures which are much brighter due to the fact that they have mode leds, the newer cases come with fans that only have fans on the center hub instead of all around the outer frame, apparently by cutting down a few leds from the fans, made a huge difference in the production costs, so they decided to change the design.
Also, the fan(s) speed cannot be controlled by the remote controller that controls the LEDs, make sure that your motherboard has a good working PWM fan heather, or the fans will run at full speed all the time and the nice case will turn into a bright jet engine. The LED controller box instructions mention something about being able to control the fan speed manually via the remote controller (when the speed sensor cable is not attached to any PWM heather on the motherboard). But this is not accurate. If you can't control the fans via motherboard heather, the LED controller box will supply full power all the time to all six fans.
Wrapping things up, this case looks beautiful, and the glass on the front and side window is very neat and clean, scratch free. I would have lkved if the fans i received were the same depicted on the listing and the ones that used to come with this case model. But they just changed them. I would not pay a penny more or this case because as beautiful as it is, it does seem to be over priced.

This review is for the SGEYR HDMI 2.0 4K 60Hz YUV444 audio extractor. I write all of this because this page has 4 different products and Amazon allows lumping together all questions and reviews in the same place. This is not user-friendly as a prospective purchaser wants information on the particular product.

I would have given this 5 stars if the documentation was any good at all. The "manual" is a short leaflet that is poorly written. You can't download anything from the SEGYR website. I ended up using screenshots from the Amazon listing and making a PDF binder. Attached is the fairly confusing, poorlywritten description of the ARC switch that is in the product description, so you get the idea.

So, the hardware has good specs, comes in a metal case, and seems to do what it is supposed to. It has multiple audio digital and analog outputs (optical, coax, 1/8" stereo). It is better than the cheaper low-spec plastic units and is worth the small extra cost. Some might find the large number of bright LED's irritating in some environments.

Not sure why there is an ARC (Audio Return Channel) on-off switch. It is not a power switch. The ARC switch seems to turn digital audio extraction on and off. You basically buy this switch for that function in the first place, so it seems it should just be on all the time like most of these switches. The EDID (Extended Display Identification Data) label is a bit technical. How about "Audio Format"?

text:
I selected this system out of a dozen based on what its attributes were and a good price. This is my first venture into this kind of system and the learning curve was pretty steep for this old man.

My application was to monitor the carport parking area in a detached carport 30' wide that has 3 enclosed storage areas 4' deep that the tenants in a two story triplex use. It is 30' from the triplex and a wired system was not an option unless some major work was done. Both the triplex and carport have aluminum siding so I knew that might be an issue.

When I ordered it I also ordered some power extension cords and two power splitter setups, plus a large hard drive. Upon arrival I formatted the hard drive and assembled the system inside on the ground level to test the camera's using a TV for a display screen. I then moved the cameras outside and things looked good. The next test was to place the camera's under the planed position on each end of the carport and the signals were blocked by three walls and lots of storage items. Placing the camera's outside the carport didn't help because the Network Video Recorder (NVR) was positioned roughly in the middle of the carport under the TV so the position change did nothing.

Next I moved the NVR upstairs and on a wall that was about inline with one end of the carport. Once again I positioned the camera's on the ground on both ends of the carport and had only one show up on an old computer monitor. Because camera's were on ground level the items in the storage area were suspect as well as walls.

I decided to install two cameras In the carports wooden ceiling where I planned they would go which should eliminate the storage area's items and possibly one wall given the angle. This helped but signal strength was weak so I contacted the support team via email and explained my situation.

This support team has vastly different working hours than I do so answers to a question often took a day to get to me but these guys were willing to help and kept in contact. Frankly, if they weren't for them I might have gave up. They ended up sending me a signal booster (IPC Router) and this was the start of a steep learning curve for me. The booster manual (quick guide) needs to be read 'carefully' so not to miss details and the pictures were not so clear to me so I missed some important points. This is where the support guys really helped. My first impression of how this booster worked was wrong and after many attempts to get it right, I finally got it. All four cameras now show good videos on screen and the the time stamps in each is within a couple seconds of each other.

If you have a line of sight that is not hindered much this system should meet ones needs and the time stamp should be close to each of the other in a multi-camera setup. If line of sight has interference of one kind or another, you may see larger variances in the time stamp if they show up at all. In that situatin you may need a booster to improve the signal. Should you go that route be sure to read the manual "carefully" and "completely" and don't be afraid to ask the support team for help.

The support team is there to help and I appreciate how they helped me.

text:
So, for starters, this kit does exactly what it claims to do. It’s great at it actually.

This comes with a BIG HOWEVER

Not the fault of Inteset, but NEWER gen Firesticks have issues. I have both an older gen Firestick and a newer gen that has volume control on the remote. The older one works PERFECTLY with this kit, but the newer one has issues. It will accept a few commands then if you watch the light on the receiver, it basically locks up. It’s not the fault of the receiver. I’ve figured out that a lot of data passes through the Firesticks usb bus even when not in use. This causes the bus to run at max capacity whenever you do anything with the Firestick. Not an issues with the original remote because it’s not usb, but with this design flaw, it makes it hard to use a usb ir receiver.

Again, this isn’t a problem on older gen Firesticks. Works perfectly. It’s only an issues with the newer gen Firestick. Idk if this is on purpose from amazon or just a design flaw but it severely hampers usb performance.

Pros: I've owned the LG Tone Ultra series beginning with the HBS-810, HBS-820s, and now these. The size of this LG Tone series is preferable for me. Flexible, not clunky and stiff, and I typically don't feel neck fatigue because of its humble footprint. Also, I carry 2 phones, so the multipoint feature is welcome. Overall, the performance in audio and voice quality has improved tremendously. Older models didn't perform as well in voice quality during voice calls -- many clients of mine were complaining of background noise or spotty voice quality -- it didn't make for a good professional Bluetooth headset. I struggled to use the older models during my work day, which translated to less reasons to use them altogether. But with this new series, I hope was delivered. Improved Bluetooth 5.0 technology along with dual mems, quad layer speaker technology delivers both great balanced audio sound with good level of highs and bass, while allowing me to take much clearer voice calls. Multipoint connection is great for someone like me who carries 2 phones simultaneously able to connect this headset to both phones. The LG smartphone app helps me control these headsets from either phones, added features, control and monitoring. Lastly, the best feature of these headsets is the voice feedback, but also the haptic feedback. The haptic feedback is the best feature of these headsets and unique to it from any other Bluetooth headsets I've owned. If I get a call, I like that it vibrates around my neck. I love that. Also, battery life is exceptional. They last me 2 days if needed.
Cons: Only a few but they are quite disruptive to my ability to really enjoy them. First, I must say the Bluetooth connectivity is spotty. It doesn't automatically connect to my devices. With the updated Bluetooth 5.0 connectivity, I had hoped for a much smoother flawless experience, but it just doesn't deliver. I find myself having to search and connect to these headsets many times manually. I had other multipoint headsets that automatically connect to both phones simultaneously, which spoiled me. I had hoped that these LG HBS-835s series would do just that. Instead, I feel like the Bluetooth connectivity is a step down even from the LG HBS820s. Secondly, maybe it's the one I received, but the power plug in seems a bit jenki. I have to jiggle it a little in order to make sure the microUSB connection is getting power therefore properly charging the unit. Lastly, that's just it, I said microUSB -- by now, I was hoping we would already be on USB-c.
Summary: The HBS-835s almost delivers on a near perfect richly featured headset experience. It does deliver on the items that count, voice and audio quality. But the lack of reliable and consistent Bluetooth connectivity draws it down, and unfortunately disrupts the overall experience enough, considering Bluetooth 5.0 technology promises that didn't deliver. So close and yet so far away -- hoping that an update in firmware can solve these simply issues.

text:
I'm on the hunt for a perfect outdoor home security camera. It must have the following features:
- Solar powered, so I don't have to run electrical to it.
- Wireless, so I don't have to run communications cabling to it.
- Record video on motion, according to user schedule and according to user-defined screen area(s).
- Night vision.
- Block out certain areas to avoid whiteouts from street lights and other bright sources.
- Local storage.
- FTP or other means to copy captured video / photos to local network NAS.
- Documentation and applications written in well developed English, not broken English or English as a second language.
- Product development and improvements (firmware updates, feature improvements, etc.). Automatic firmware updates.

This system has been impressive from the very beginning, with extremely good, attractive packaging. The documentation is pretty good, with the major flaw being that it is spotty. This should not be a problem for people who are used to putting together and installing things, but is missing some details that would be helpful for less experienced folks.

This system hits on all my requirements except one or two. While it records video to a local microSD card, I cannot find a way to have video and/or images automatically transfer to a storage device (NAS) on my network. Also, I can't find a way to limit motion detection to just certain areas on the video image.

There are applications available for both smartphone and PC/MAC. I'm using Android phone and Windows laptop which are both adequate but lacking in full functionality. There are some operations you have to use a smartphone, and which are not available in the Windows client.

Videos come through very clear and reasonably accurate,

But my overall experience is that I'm impressed this is as robust and well put together for the cost. You really get a pretty good product for your money. This is not a cheaply made device someone is selling with bare functionality.
title: Really nice system for the cost

I spent an entire afternoon shopping for a new monitor. I decided on this one, having had no prior experience with Sceptre brand before. text:
I purchased this Motherboard during the Black Friday sales, and received an incredible deal. (Thank You Amazon.).

I am using this with a Ryzen 7 3800X and 16 Gb of GSkill "Neo" RAM at 3600 speed, 16-19-19 timings.
To be clear, I had absolutely NO issues with this Motherboard. Mine was not set up with the latest BIOS, so I used the BIOS flashback to be able to run the most up to date BIOS in support of Ryzen 3000. Worked like a charm. I am getting peak CPU speeds of over 4500, and everything is working great.

A couple of caveats that I did discover: 1. The Ryzen 7 3800X idles hot, (47 Degrees C.), and at 1.47 Volts on auto settings. It is actually fine there, and in stress testing with AIDA 64, I did not go over 72 Degrees C.
Also, if you want to use the X4 direct PCIe 3.0 lanes direct to the CPU for NVME storage, use the BOTTOM M.2 slot, and not the top one by the CPU Socket. Using the top one by the CPU socket will cut your PCIe slot 1, (Main Graphics Card) to a 8X lane bandwidth rather than the 16X bandwidth.
So far, ASUS has issued 2 BIOS updates for the Crosshair VII in support of Ryzen 3000, so ASUS is continuing to support this Platform. From all the things I have been reading about the X570 Motherboards, I am kind of glad to be on X470 for now.

Also know that you will not get peak performance out of the Ryzen 3800X CPU with the Wraith Prism cooler. It will be functional, and be fine, but you will get better performance out of a more robust cooler, whether air or water.

Not sure what else to add. Everything that was supposed to be in the box, was in the box. It just seems like a great Motherboard, so I am happy with this purchase.
title: Terrific Motherboard for Ryzen 7 3800X and GSkill 3600 Memory

text:
Overall this is a good mount, but there are some caveats to be aware of. I'm happy with the mount, but setting it up was a bit of a pain. One thing to note as far as space goes, This mount requires some clearance to adjust position. I had two monitors with an average size of 30 inches sitting towards the back of my desk, and to get them mounted in a similar position over my desk, I had to move my desk away from the wall by 6 inches. If I didn't do that, my options would be to raise the monitors to full height, leave them several inches away from each other, or move them over the front of my desk, losing the extra desk space I would have gained by using this mount.
The GOOD: The mount feels sturdy and well made. After appropriate adjustment, the springs are strong enough to hold any monitor under about 20 lbs in place, but they still allow you to move the monitor freely.
The BAD: Some of the bolts need to be cranked down really tight to get things to stay put. I have a monitor that is well within the weight limit, and I really had to crank the tilt bolt to get it not to slip to where it is facing down toward my desk.

text:
Tecsun PL-880 Review

First impressions: Solid, well made, heavier than expected, clear display with smart or switchable backlight, smooth controls, stainless steel telescoping antenna - not plated brass, very nice padded case, charging cord, ear buds, wire antenna, single removable Li-Ion 18650 cell that charges in radio, good English user manual, high fidelity speaker.
It covers Long Wave 100 kHz to 519 kHz , Medium Wave (broadcast AM) 520 kHz to 1710 kHz and several Short Wave bands going from 1711 mHz to 29,999 mHz with SSB upper and lower on all. It does FM (stereo through headphone jack) 64 mHz to 108 mHz.

Here's what impressed me: It has a quality feel, and is easy to operate and learn all the functions. It has a nice scan feature where you can scan in one band or all bands. It will scan stations and automatically put them into memory. It has 3050 total memories with memory pages. It is easy to delete memories with one key press. You can enter a frequency in directly with the key pad or tune with the tuning knobs. It locks on to active frequencies when you tune to them. It has a "kickstand" on the back so you can lay it down at an angle without as much risk of tipping it over. It has rubber feet on the bottom. It has a "line out" jack. It has a clock with alarm function and sleep timer. The tuning and volume knobs are very smooth and solid with a viscous sort of resistance. Not sloppy or lose. The display shows signal strength in DB and signal to noise ratio in DB.

It is sensitive. I picked up a couple of 40 meters LSB QSOs using only the telescoping antenna. I picked up several SW stations using only the telescoping antenna. My location is not good for broadcast FM but I picked up several of those as well. One complaint is that the audio is quite bass heavy even though there is a tone switch on the side. If you are within range of a good FM station it will sound much bigger than it's small size.

It's an expensive radio and it shows, but I think it's worth the money. I paid $100 years back for a Grundig S350DL and this beats it in every way.
title: Small, full featured and sensitive world-band radio

text:
i've had these cord clips up and running for a couple months now and they have been great once installed:

i have them installed to clip an ethernet cable that's basically running through my entire house. they are sturdy enough that if someone accidentally hits them, they do not budge. however, if you need to take them out, it's as simple as just pulling/twisting them off the surface with your fingers - won't hurt your wrist and hasn't done any damage to the paint or wooden floors that i've pried them out of (your mileage may vary though depending on what surface you're using).

they can be clip cables both from the left and from the right, so they're pretty versatile as well. i have them running all sorts of shapes across the edges of my floor.

OK! so why the minus one star? installation...specifically installing with tape instead of screws. i figured out a good way to do this so don't worry, but it took some trial and error. let me explain:

the package gives you a bunch of double-sided tape if you want to install this via tape as opposed to screws. the tape itself is clear colored but the covers on both sides are read. it's really really hard to peel off one side of the tape cover. like i destroyed several of these double-sided tapes in an effort to peel the cover off the second side of the tape. what i eventually started doing is as follows:

1) peel the tape cover off the side of the tape that's easy to peel, and stick that peeled side onto the cord clip.
2) take a knife and cut that tape (the one already taped to the cord clip) in half. now, the tape is already stuck to the cord clip so the tape isn't going anywhere. the plastic of the cord clip is sturdy so it should be easy to cut just the tape and not the the cord clip.
3) use the knife (or your fingers) to find the newly formed edge(s) that you just made on the tape cover by cutting it, and peel the second side of the tape cover from there.

it wasn't so bad after i discovered this... but it would have been nice if i didn't have to cut the tape cover for every clip installed.

on a final note, i'd definitely recommend these for home use. i'm comparing this to the Command Round Cord Clips, which i actually replaced these with. the Command Rounds cost a ton more and didn't last a whole day, whereas these are still going strong.
title: nearly perfect - sturdy, great price, but had to figure out install

text:
verifying what another reviewer wrote about putting this product into boiling (not just warm) water.

in my case, i heated water to boiling and emptied that boiling water into a large, non-heated pot which i let this cord cover soak in for several minutes. when this cord cover starts matching the temp of boiling water, it becomes flexible and you can bend it to whatever shape you need. the shape that the cord cover is in when it cools will be the shape that it stays in (unless you heat it up again).

product has been installed for a few weeks and no flaws yet! subtracting the star because it took work with the whole boiling thing... but i guess that's why this is few dollars cheaper than competitors. up to you whether that's worth the cheaper price.
title: works after you straighten it out via boiling water

I love bass and I rarely turn it up more than halfway. if there was any reason you wanted these headphones it would be because there was a convenient way to immediately turn the bass up and down without having to open an equalizer in your phone. the bass slider only affects some of the lowest frequencies so when you turn it up you're not turning all of the bass frequencies up just the lowest ones. I prefer at least another frequency higher to be affected. I think they left out the next higher frequency on purpose because with that much power you could damage your ears. The frequencies it affects are more of a very low vibration that probably wouldn't hurt your ears at any volume. Turning it all the way up certainly pounds your brain but more with movement then sound the frequencies are so low.

The sound quality is good but I'll agree that the mid-range is lacking and think an equalizer could correct that. side by side comparison to the Sony's I'll say the Sony's have better sound. Better clarity in all ranges and decent enough base.

I got the white color so when I accidentally leave it in the sun it won't explode the lithium battery as easily.

The band over the top is a bit had heavy maybe the batteries up there I don't know. It kind of has some leverage to slide forwards or rear words. I don't think I'd go running in these.

If you put them on but leave the music off they do not muffle the outside sound as much as a pair of earmuffs would. Like the kind of ear muffs you would wear for ear protection.

They don't have any active noise cancelling so whatever noise makes it through the ear muffs will not get electronically canceled by opposing speaker movements but that's okay because they're not priced to do such. I've seen off-brand versions in this price range that do have ANC active noise-cancelling though but I've never tried them, some even have good reviews.

I've been using them for a few hours here and there over the past 3 weeks and haven't had to charge them yet.

Hey maybe next model they'll put a full range equalizer with sliders for each frequency on the face of the left ear! Lol

text:
The most important thing to know here is that the user manual has little to no use. I consider myself to be moderately tech savvy and was able to figure this thing out, if you're not, don't waste your time. Tech support is fast but equally useless. For example, the camera is supposed to give you a WiFi ID and password when put in WiFi mode which you can use to control the camera in it's app: mine did not. Interestingly, my phone was able to identify the WiFi ID, so the camera was transmitting it, but the screen did not show the ID or password. So, I sent a message to the seller stating that the WiFi ID and password were not being shown in WiFi mode and the answer was "Did you set the camera to WiFi mode？You need set the camera to WiFi mode." This issue remains unresolved.
If you're thinking, no problem, I won't need WiFi mode, think again, because the touch screen is not very sensitive and navigating with it, especially playback is very difficult. It would be so much easier to use your phone to view the videos.
I used it to make about twenty short videos. The quality and sound seem pretty good when viewed on the camera, but I haven't seen them on my computer yet, so take that for what it's worth. By the way, I took 6 or 7 videos before I realized the external mic needed to be turned on because it has it's own switch.
The most important thing here is setting up and operating this camera is not point and shoot by any stretch of the imagination, and a lot of detective work is required to make full use of it. This is evident by the number of questions people need to ask like "how do I install the microphone?" (this took me some time to figure out, I confess"), and "how do I format the memory card?" (I got around this somehow. maybe because the card was new). You see these in the public questions but remember most people ask these kinds of questions directly to the seller after the sale, such as my WiFi question, so they are not publicly posted.
One last thing, I have only used mine on a tripod so this isn't yet a factor for me, but I noticed in a demo video that was posted that the anti shake function didn't work very well. But it is an inexpensive camera, so you shouldn't expect too much from it.

i've had yammy receivers for well over 25 years now. they all have been flawless. i bought this a780 for all the wrong reasons as i already had 3, 2 of which were the hi-end adventage receivers. with this refurbished box, all are now of the adventage variety. truth be told, i can't can't hear the distinction between the adventage models and the lesser ones - the a1000 is the exception.

so why am i so happy? the ui (user interface) on this box is much improved over previous models. in fact, it's a damn joy! while i am not an audiophile, i can tell u, it really delivers. it has about 10% less power than my rx-a1000 but it's not even noticeable when cranked.

many folks are interested in atmos and 9.1 (presence spkrs). well, i can tell u, my very antiquated 5.1 and 7.1 sets, put out and it's unlikely that i'll do anything more than 5.1 in the future. i judge the audio in this manner:
1) movies: the dark knight and avatar 3d
2) antenna/live and streamed tv.
4) audio (music) from a local (home) server
that said (written), all my yammies perform quite well. the rx-a1000 is king when cranked and the entire 3200sq ft 2 floor house shakes with only one 15" subwoofer at < 50%. this rx-a780 is also impressive even with less power and smaller speakers - again, the entire house shakes (12" sub) but the highs are crisp and the sub is not in a corner.

i feel like i got lucky with this purchase, as it was so cheap, i consider it a STEAL! so yes, very happy. you may ask, why not 5 stars? there is one somewhat insignificant issue with 5.1 on normal broadcasts. with this receiver, i have to change a setting to enjoy 5.1 on those braodcasts that are not 5.1. again, very insignificant. if you can find one, this is a no-brainer! i've had at least 3 refurbs over a decade or so, and none ever failed. when i upgrade, i sell them and for those bought by friends, they're still pumping. i'm talking boxes without-hdmi-ports old, k. so yes, i'm a fan!

COMMENTARY: with today's technology, it's ez to get caught up on the latest dolby and atmos. few of us will put speakers on the ceiling (atmos), most with intelligence will not fall for the latest hype - speakers that project sound off the ceiling. in my opinion, it's pure marketing but not very practical in a home or home theater environ. with the appropriate and somewhat antiquated 5.1 dolby, one can have an amazing audio experience without all the bluster. don't be fooled by the best buy / magnolia sound rooms - it's just a stage. most of us live this other reality with kids and interruptions. you just can't beat 5.1 for the $$ and audio separation. for me, i cannot differentiate between my 5.1 and 7.1 systems. still, the dark knight is king for me with audio - i almost never re-watch a movie but knight audio puts all the star wars flicks to shame. just an opinion, k. don't get it twisted.

text: Needs to be formatted in GPT format to have Windows recognize the full hard disk drive size above 2TB. But even if you copy a formatted NTFS over to the 6TB drive you will not end up with a true system reserved partition. You need to create a 2TB partition (or less) and have the remaining partitions within reach of the 2TB for backward compatibility with the Master Boot Record (MBR).The specs should have included a information on how to create minimal legacy bootstrap-partitions at the beginning of the disk where the MBR could easily point. This would be "dummy" partitions whose purpose is nothing except to contain a bootmgr, which would in turn point into the actual full size of the remaining  ( > 2TB ) partitions and HDD.There is no easy BIOS fix. I ended up returning to my 2TB HDD and used this larger drive as a storage HDD with GPT format. I moved iCloud and DropBox links there too to start saving actual primary HDD space with 2TB on it. You might be better getting an external USB drive or again just use this drive for additional storage with the GPT formatting.
title: System Reserved NTFS Partitions Not Be Copied in Windows 7/10 For Full Drive Use

text: I have had a few connectivity problems both with WiFi and Cellular service.  The most troubling problem was with a contact sensor.  It went offline without any warning.  This keeps the system from arming without extra steps to bypass this sensor.  Upon investigation I found that the battery was dead after 3 months.  I spoke to technical support and they helped me confirm that the battery was the problem by swapping the battery from a working sensor into the troubled one.  I asked them how long the battery should last and they said "Up to a year" - I have read on their web site that batteries can last "up to three years".  They don't cover batteries even in this case were it seems that there was a problem that was either related to manufacture of the battery or sensor.  Either that or I should start stocking up on batteries.  Also more troubling was that the system did not alert me ahead of time that the battery needed changing.  I'm not sure if when a battery fails in a more expected way if I would get an alert.  Also not sure how the system responds to a sensor suddenly going offline while armed.  Overall I would say that this experience leads me to the conclusion that the alarm doesn't provide the level of trouble-free operation as I would have expected or hoped for.  You should plan on keeping some batteries on hand to replace them when they fail.  They use a CR123A battery which I found at big box hardware stores for $2-$2.50 depending on the quantity you buy them in.

text:
I needed a new sound bar that would pass through HDR and support some of the newer audio formats. I have an older CT660 Sony soundbar and it has been rock solid and sounds great. This Sony is actually smaller and you can feel some of the cost savings in the physical bar itself, but then what counts is the sound processing and sound quality. The Sony does not disappoint in sound clarity and quality, but where it literally falls flat is in the sub. The sub is weak and flat and lacks any real punch. I cranked the Sub level to its max of +6db and it barely made a difference.The low end bass and sub on my older CT660 was leaps better although a little muddy. Part of it may be the fact that this sub is front firing ported where the CT660 is seals and down firing. When I find some time I will see if I can get the old CT660 sub paired to this bar and hope it helps. The sub has inline video based menus for the setup which is nice, but every time it powers up it puts up the selection menu on the screen for a few seconds then drops. I did look around for other options, but those that passed HDR and DV lacked support for other than PCM and Dolby Surround. Considering I got this Sony on sale for $399 it is a good deal, I just wish they would upgrade the sub.

Update:
After 3 months I updated my rating as the bass is weak and the sub just plain old sucks. When you get any decent bass out of this thing it distorts and bottoms the sub. The older 660 I had had better bass, while not as crisp as this unit it overall sounded better. I will wait for a good sale later this year and replace this. Sony needs to offer the option to pair with another sub, even my old 660 sub would be a better match for this system.
title: Sony quality and good overall sound, but where's the bass?

text:
I am somewhat hesitant to give this a 1 star review because I got the cable a year ago and never went through customer service (so, for all I know, the customer service would've sent me a new one and it would've been fine). But here was my experience:

I got this cable about a year or maybe even 2 years ago. Connected it to my Acer 1440p 144hz freesync monitor, no dice. "No signal." Decided to ignore it and just use HDMI. A few days ago I decided, screw it, I want 144hz and freesync - so I decided to stop being a lazy idiot. Plugged it in again. No signal. Okay, turned off PC. Turned off monitor. Unplugged everything, replugged everything in, turned it on - you know, the solution that comes up when you google "display port no signal." Nope, doesn't work. Second idea: plug the side I have been putting into the computer into the monitor and vice versa. Result? this time it says nothing is plugged in. Bizzare! So (I have an RX480) I just go down using every possible configuration on all 3-4 DP slots on the card. No dice.

Finally I just drive over to BestBuy and get a new cord, and it is what I am using on my monitor now as I type this. 144hz and freesync - it all works. So the cord was just a dud. text:
Well before computers existed, I learned to type on a typewriter. Years later,I was using tower computers with full sized mechanical keyboards. The last few years it has been laptops with the more compact keyboards. I've never gotten used to the compact keyboard of a laptop, (nice when traveling, but a pain at home), so I finally decided to go full sized and I selected this one. Good choice!

I love just the fact that it is full sized. With the included built in trackball, this thing is a monster compared to my laptop keyboard. Good! On the laptop my old arthritic fingers were always tapping wrong keys causing me to cuss and swear in frustration. I find and press the keys on this keyboard with ease and I love the long travel mechanical feel. No guesswork whether I've pressed a key. I can again type without constantly glancing down at the keyboard.

I am often on the computer at night so the back lit keyboard is a definite plus. Press Fn and the number 8 key to turn on the light. A second time makes it brighter. A third time makes the light irritatingly fade in and out. (I won't be using that fade in and out feature.) If you have reached the fade in and out mode and press Fn and the number 2 key, the fading stops and the keyboard is one step BRIGHTER. After that, multiple presses of Fn and 2 dim and eventually turn the light off. Learning to type on a full sized mechanical keyboard again is taking some getting used to after the laptops keyboard, but I know it will not take long to become second nature. With my laptop keyboard I accidentally pressed the num lock key about a million times when intending to press the backspace key to correct a typing error. Then I press the delete key and get a period. Now I have to backspace, hit the num lock key and hit the delete key. All just to correct one miss-typed letter. That's doesn't happen with this keyboard. Note that because this is mechanical that there is a lot of clacking noise while you are typing. I like the feel and the sound, but no doubt it will drive anyone else in the room crazy. Not my problem. It's my house.

The trackball has a slightly bigger learning curve for me as I was used to using a wireless ergonomic trackball. But with that thing my twitchy fingers were always unintentionally pressing the buttons. That doesn't happen here because my fingers don't rest on the buttons. Having those buttons below the ball rather than above it takes some getting used to, but it seems to work for me. The scroll wheel works fine for me too and includes the press button function. If you're used to a scroll button that you can push left and right as well then you're out of luck here. My other trackball didn't do that so I don't miss the function. I've experienced more learning curve by having to maneuver this trackball with my fingers rather than my thumb. Not a problem. Just different. I did have to go in and adjust my mouse settings as once I hooked this keyboard and trackball up, the mouse cursor was moving a hundred miles per hour. It was slower on my previous trackball. I just slowed the cursor down and I increased the number of lines the scroll wheel would scroll up or down as scrolling was kind of slow. That was all I needed to change. I've had no issues with the trackball not cooperating and have been able to float my cursor all around the screen with no issues. There is a review that points out an issue with the trackball, but I've had no such problem. That review is over three years old so maybe there has been a design improvement since then. I don't know, but it works fine for me. Something I didn't see in the listing for this keyboard is that the trackball glows when you use it. It's light is off when you aren't using it, but as soon as you start to roll it around it glows like a dimly smoldering coal. Pretty cool!

I just got and installed this keyboard, but am so far very satisfied. If I were to complain about anything it would be that the space bar is kind of small. It's actually slightly smaller than the space bar on my laptop. This is due to that 'menu' key to the right of it. No worries though. It works fine for me, I haven't had any issues hitting it and I think I like that 'menu' key and will be using it.

The only other thing I might wish for is that the keyboard would have some USB ports. My laptop has two ports. My laptop sits on a cooler which plugs into one of those USB ports. The cooler has two USB ports but one is used to connect it to the laptop. That leaves me with two USB ports. One on the laptop and one on the cooler. This keyboard/trackball used those two USB ports so I have none left. I'll have to purchase a USB hub to get more ports to use for external drives, USB sticks and charging things.

As stated above, this keyboard connects to two of your computers USB ports. A nice design feature is that there is only one cable coming out of the keyboard. Near the end it splits into two short pieces each with it's own USB plug. Nice to not have two different cables snaking around getting tangled.

So, other than a slightly small space bar and no USB ports, this keyboard is perfect for me.

On more update:
I did have an issue with the trackball not functioning after my laptop resumed from hibernation mode. I solved this by going into device settings and changing power settings for USB root hub. I unchecked the box that allowed the computer to turn it off to save power. Problem solved. The keyboard did not suffer this issue as the power option was already unchecked for that port.
title: Just a little bit of a learning curve
