text:
I actually found the original recommendation for this antenna model on nocable.org where you put in your zip code and it shows the indoor antenna that might be best for your area and the recommendation worked pretty good for me. with full description below. If you aren't from my area I suggest you try your zip code here and see what it recommends.

I live in Bucks County PA outside of Philadelphia. I was only interested in getting the main local channels from the antenna (3,6,10,17,29,57 - ABC/NBC/CBS/FOX/etc) but this antenna was actually able to find 33 channels for me! I even tested it on my basement TV thinking this would be the hardest place to find a signal. I'm not sure what all the other ones are but it is definitely working. I've only been using it for a few days so far but the picture quality for HD is really good too, doesn't look much visibly different than picture from a Fios box.

The only obvious tip to give is to read the instructions with the antenna. Simply plugging in the antenna and going to channel doesn't work. I tried this first and got nervous when nothing was found. The instructions indicate that you must connect the antenna and run a channel scan from the TV in order to find the channels. After doing this, the 33 channels were found.

As for this model itself, it is very small and light. The flat panel antenna is paper thin, literally, to the point where I questioned if there was actually anything in there. It comes with one side black and other white to give options for color match on a wall mount. The antenna connects to the TV thru a provided coax cable, about 8-10 feet I'd estimate. The amplifier connects to the antenna thru coax cable (provided) and is also pretty small, about the size of a travel tissue package. The amplifier needs a power connection which is provided for plug in to outlet or you can connect to a USB port on the TV for power which is what I did and works well. The amplifier and all provided coax in my set were white.
title: Works great for me near Philadelphia PA (Bucks County)

Compared to more expensive Rotel amps, I find the Marantz to be more full, warm, and musical, perhaps at the slight loss of detailed transparency.

So there it is, this is a great little amp that hangs with competitors 2-3x the price, but very rightfully so doesn’t hang with competitors 10x the price.

text:
Solid product. I wish I could say that I love it.
The idea of having multiple outlets in one place is fantastic and I need it. Don't we all? In today's society, we require more of these ideas. Unfortunately it lost a star because like all things similar, the plastic prongs for the empty outlet don't line up properly and I had to break them off in order to get the metal prongs to fit into the wall properly. This creates a loss of stability, so only lighter plugs can be used in the ac outlets, or it isn't secure into the original outlet. Another star lost because if you have a wider than normal plug, you lose an outlet, as it overlaps the others. So the only thing you actually gain is USB outlets.
Overall it's not bad, but the design flaws should be corrected to be considered good. Possibly swivel the outlets? Place them on the sides? Measure the standard outlet for a secure fit?

text:
This was my first Echo/ Alexa Device (I now have this, 4 Dots, and a handful of 'Alexa Built-In' SmartHome devices), and for the price its pretty nifty. When I bought this, I wasn't expecting much given it's steep price cut from the Echo Show, but It really is a good little device. Once you fiddle through the settings, you can turn off the full-page Alexa recommendations, but it doesn't look like you can turn off the little 'Try, Alexa...' phrases at the bottom of the screen. I don't really mind those, as its honestly usually something that I can use.

What I like:
- Screen that rotates my calendar events, weather and photos
- Screen automatically switches to night mode in low/no light
- Impressive sound (all things considered)
- Ring Camera & Security System Integration (video is kinda slow, but still works fine)
- All of the Routines you can make to automate you life
- Speaker groups that are perfectly synced across my whole house

What could be improved:
- It seems to have a real hard time understanding me. I can sit there and tell it the same command over and over again and it will chime back with the "hmm I don't know that one". I walk over to one of the dots, say the same command in the same way and it gets it instantly.
- It also seems to have a hard time hearing me. Often times, I can be standing 3' in front of it, and it won't hear me, but one of the dots in another room, or even my Ecobee 4 on the other side of the house, will hear me and respond back. Usually it starts listening, then stops when it sees that one of the other devices can hear me better. I only have this issue when speaking to the show 5. I have tried re-positioning it, with no luck. Perhaps a mic is bad in my unit.
title: Looks Good, Hard at Hearing

text:
I decided on the 13.5 Surface Book 2 with built in NVidia card for several reasons. I needed something that I could take hand-written notes on for work, and I also wanted something that I could do some light gaming on from the couch.
As for handwriting, this really is a great tool when paired with the Surface Pen. I am able to rapidly take handwritten notes and share across devices, insert pdfs to quickly fill out or take notes on, and the fact that it separates into a separate tablet means that if I need more mobility, or want to do a little drawing, I have that option as well. Compared to my girlfriend's new iPad, I think that it is on par, or juuuust a tiny smidge short of the precision level, but as a cursive writer, I wanted something ultra precise and this device certainly is.
It also does a great job running the types of games I like in my leisure time. The tall aspect ratio means I get more screen than with my old 13.5 inch Asus Zenbook. It has not issue running RTS and TBS games like Total War, Panzer IV, or Civ VI. Even more graphics heavy games like Tropico 6 run very smoothly at the 3000x2000 resolution. HOWEVER, I had to tinker with the battery settings quite a bit to get good life when doing heavy gaming. I basically had to set the battery settings, even when plugged in, to "best battery life" (as opposed to "best performance"), and you also want to make sure that the game is running on the NVidia graphics card, and not the on-board intel. One thing that is both a benefit and a hindrance to this device, is that there are two graphics "cards" in the NVidia version I purchased: the NVidia card and battery in the screen half, and the Intel parts and battery in the keyboard half. The computer defaults to running down the battery in the screen first, which means that when I am gaming I am getting 2-2.5 hours battery life before the screen batter falls below 5% and it crashes the game. This isn't a HUGE deal, as I dont get as many opportunities to play that long without interruption, but I thought it might be helpful to some others considering this device. I can say that it charges very fast, and even a short break of 30 minutes can get me to at least a third, almost half battery.
I only have two other complaints about this device: first, the power cord seems really flimsy to me. It connects on the RH side with a magnet, and can connect both ways, but it falls out ALOT when I am sitting with this in my lap. More annoying than anything, except the cord is having a tendency to kink at the connection, and it has gotten VERY hot once or twice. Not sure if this is a regular product issue, or if this is because I purchased a refurbished item. Speaking of refurbished, my volume button is a little wonky - the volume up side rests lower than the volume down side. Again, not sure if this is a regular product issue or a refurbished issue, but I am guessing the latter because the aesthetics of it drives me crazy. Buuuuut, not a big enough complaint to raise a stink over, just my OCD going off.
I definitely am loving this device. The handwriting part alone has eliminated a hundred legal pads and sticky notes in my office, and syncing OneNote to my phone means that I have my notes anywhere I go. Would entirely recommend.

Several years ago I purchased a 9.7 iPad Pro, only to discover there were few choices of covers which fit that model. I settled on a Fintie, and never looked back. It had all the features I wanted - protection, deep grooves to keep the tablet upright, a good fit with all the buttons and speakers assessable, easy rotation of tablet, and an automatic on/off feature.
However, after years of continuous hard use, being shoved in a purse, thrown in a car, used in the kitchen following recipes, reading in bed, going on vacations, and just general use and abuse, it dared to actually look worn! To be clear, the functionality of this cover remained completely in tact. It has been perfect. Only because the cover began to look worn, did I choose to replace it. It was a “choice,” not a “need.” Of course, I searched out another Fintie, which arrived a couple of day’s ago. I was so happy to see that the quality of the product has remained the same. The grooves are nice and deep, and all the features I wanted and loved remained the same. The only “con” of this cover are, 1. The upper left little corner piece, after so much use, began to weaken and bend back. It has to be there for corner protection, but because of speakers and buttons, it has to be very small. I used a small piece of tape from the back of the case to the screen, to support it, which has worked fine. I don’t know if there is any way to build it stronger. 2. I wish there were more pattern and color choices, but I understand that this iPad is an old model. My final assessment, this case is unbeatable for design, ease of use, and durability. It’s a perfect choice!

text:
I'm in an apartment that I need to move out of soon, and I do almost all of my listening these days with
headphones in any case. If I find headphones fatiguing, I never listen to them: they end up gathering dust.
Or, if I find their overall performance crap, or the sound dull. Goodbye.

Having said that, I'm not really a huge fan of Sony's headphones these days. I do own a 2008 Sony
home theater in a box set, which is decent but not outstanding (not top end), and a small Sony 2011
bookshelf system with Ipod dock--which sounds good for basic apt. background listening and radio),
so I do own some basic Sony audio stuff which is good for certain things. I feel like their headphones
are hit or miss though lately, with quality, build, and performance. I don't really love Bluetooth because I like
being able to control the ampage and EQ as much as possible with wired setups, and the still-iffy quality of
wireless audio.

I wanted cans that offer much better bass response than most of the other quite excellent headphones I've bought the past five years or so. Some have tons of bass, like Koss PortaPros or the wonderful Linsoul Pro ZS10 IEMs. The PortaPros are great but a bit flimsy
and delicate, though totally portable, and the IEMs are great when I want the IEM sound and portability,
but sometimes I don't want to feel isolated as IEMs can sometimes make you feel like.

I also recently invested in a pair of Audio-Technica MH20xs, good budget studio monitor cans, but, they aren't really super bass-cannons, and they are a bit analytical and "dry," and this is not what I want from a pair of totally "fun", warm, bass-heavy headphones for sheer music listening. If you want that, put on the ATs, or my Fostex RP40s, which will give you detail but not massive bass. I find the ATs are better for classical, jazz, and watching streaming
stuff online or movies and such. They're just not super musical, since they're intended as pro monitors.
They are excellent though for $55 studio cans. However.... I'm difficult to please.

I still wanted more serious sized, bass-heavy but not distorted etc. headphones that were light and comfortable. I heard the MDRX10s were exemplary in that mode. You cannot find them retail in NY or LI where I'm at these days,
since Sony seems to be pushing their very basic BT headphones and sports buds and such, and nothing
"limited edition" like the X10s, which is very bloody annoying, so I ordered them up on Amazon from
my man BigBanana (sic) from out there in sunny Alameda, California. He shipped these big bassy bastards
Priority Mail and they showed up fast. I opened the package and held my breath, expecting to hear cheap
sounding sludgey cans that made Beats actually sound good. Oh, how the mighty have risen.

I received mine today, 12/30/19, and thus far, they absolutely deliver what they promise. In my experience this is a rarity for Sony these days, and a rarity for headphones in general. I don't like Beats, don't think their quality is good enough to warrant the price, bass or not. I've previewed Bose and they generally sound good, but kind of boring
and lifeless to my ears, with pleasant bass, but nothing truly outstanding, minus the high prices and
maybe noise-canceling if you absolutely need that. I own Hifiman HE400I planar magnetics, which are the best open back headphones I own, they have nice solid tight bass, but not Deep DELICIOUS brain-eating bass. Overall quality and detail, and high end, they beat these Sonys, but, on the other hand, the MDRX10s are stupendous for some decent clarity, they don't sound muddy at all, and, they pack a MASSIVE wallop in terms of bass response, impact, and bass clarity. I would differentiate this way: The Hifiman HE400Is have a warmish, clear, detailed darkish signature with
tight, clean bass, and super detailed sparkling high end, but require a lot of amp power, whereas the MDRX10s offer high efficiency, super warm, muscular powerful bass response, with more of a sound signature that reminds me of great powered DJ monitors like KRK, JBL, or Pioneers with a good subwoofer added in. You can also drive
the X10s with a phone or media player or tablet, without necessarily having to add a separate head. amp.
For really good quality 50mm bass-heavy headphones, that is a true accomplishment, without their losing
a lot of detail and quality in the mids and highs in the process. Also, the bass on the X10s doesn't get
muddy or buzzy like those ghastly bass-adjustable Skullcandy Krushers that have a sliding bass switch on 'em.
Stay far away from those unless you like distorted bass in your drum and bass music.

I need only turn these bad boys up to maybe 10-12 on my PC Creative Labs amp setup, with some EQ,
to get a gorgeous loud but listenable level overall, with truly ass kicking bass for rock, dance music, etc. After
about eight hours of testing, with a pair that was sent to me new, or open-box new, these headphones still
felt comfortable due to the soft on-ear pads, I wasn't expecting that, and, they deliver some serious performance,
easily 10x what I'd expected from them from reviews here or on YouTube. I feel like Sony still makes quality stuff,
but mainly at their higher end, top shelf, but the X10s at roughly $90 that I paid for mine, easily punch way above their price point. They seem to be well-made and are definitely comfortable, and even offer two removable
cables, and a nice vinyl metallic case. They're quite lightweight, and look stylish and attractive without being
too garish. They're spectacularly efficient headphones, even though they actually seem to offer a pretty
powerful, bass-emphasized signature, but still with some good clear mids and highs, and, the highs aren't
shrill or overbearing in any way. This is highly important as I CANNOT STAND shrill, metallic, sibilant,
annoying unpleasant highs. But I love me some good solid bass where the kick drum in say, the average
HD recording of The Police, (Voices Inside My Head) sounds like I'm putting my head about three feet or less
from the kick drum riser. It doesn't sound like someone kicking the pedal against a rug, it sounds like
Stewart Copeland actually kicking that bloody pedal on that bloody kick drum.

Yes, these are better than Beats, by far, and they cost less, and they have more bass than many higher-end
headphones I could name (Grado? Beyer? AKG? All great headphones that lack heavy bass). That's about
all you need to know. If you want budget-priced headphones with some unbelievable deep yet tight bass,
and clarity otherwise, and comfort, I can't recommend too many other headphones that fit the bill in a DJ
type design, that deliver all of the points I've mentioned. I even own new PIoneer X7 DJ pro headphones,
and, honestly, I like the sound of the MDRX10s better, because, the Pioneers A. don't have as much good
bass as these do and B. they were a lot more money and C. they are spectacularly heavy, and not very
comfortable and D. the overall sound signature is a bit muddy, total V shape, murkier bass and highs
and not much good midrange at all. They distort a lot more easily at higher volumes than the X10s.

So, Sony has redeemed themselves a bit this time out. I figured I'd laugh at how awful they sounded,
and send them right back to Amazon, but, instead, I lucked out with a really bracing sounding pair
of headphones with 50mm drivers and bass that truly devastates. I mainly listen to rock, pop, dance music,
goth, 80s, folk rock, power pop, etc., and metal. The X10s are the perfect headphones for these genres.
If you want to listen to nothing but classical and jazz, I recommend the Hifimans, BeyerDynamics,
AKGs, Grados, etc. As for the Sony MDRX10 "Simon Cowell but you needn't like him or his silly show to buy these": I recommend putting these through the best amplifier you own, EQing them to cut the regular bass down a tad and up the sub-bass a bit, and playing The Sisters Of Mercy's "Dominion/Mother Russia" at about volume 14, and be prepared for the retro nightclub playing in your head. You have been warned for bass masturbation ecstasy dead ahead.

text:
We've had our Circle for four months now. If I had it to do over again, I'd still spend the money, but I wish it were better. Note that Apple and Amazon parental controls are superior -- we block YouTube and the web browser on our children's phones and tablets.

Circle Pros:
- Fairly good at managing DNS & time limits
- Circle gives parents a targeted Internet “kill switch” for managed devices.
- Auto-enables Google Safe Search
- Good looking app
- Supports having unmanaged devices, thank goodness

Circle Cons:
- Abominable VPN. The invasive mobile-client VPN isn’t nearly configurable enough. It completely blocks use of WiFi at church and at school, because those networks don’t allow VPN and their networks are already locked-down. So we don't use it, which means our children can hop on a neighbor's network and get unfettered access to the Internet... but we use Apple and Amazon parental controls to block YouTube and the web browser, so we'ere in a good spot.
- Sometimes circle blocks unmanaged devices, such as when it blocked iTunes on my wife's laptop from downloading a device update. I had to turn of Circle, then it worked.
- The app logs me out unpredictably. When I logged in, it said that I authenticated successfully, then sent me back to the login page. I tried several times, with several failures, over a couple of days. So I turned Circle off.
- No desktop management option. Especially for initial configuration, I very much dislike being forced to use a tiny iPhone screen. I’d much rather have a large monitor, a mouse and a keyboard.
- Auto-device naming stinks, and there's no search-by-MAC-address option. We have a lot of devices -- kindle fires, kindle paper whites, iPhones, desktop computers, a smart TV, and so on. When they all show up at once, and they're named unhelpfully "Amazon device", "Motorola device", and "Apple device", or even more obscure things, it makes it hard to figure out which device belongs in what profile. It'd be so useful to be able to type in a partial MAC address to find the device and add it to a profile, but they don't offer that option. Workaround: Change the WiFi password, and don't tell the children what it is for at least a few days. Add devices to WiFi one or two at a time, then it's easier to figure out what they are, name them correctly, and assign them to the correct profile.
- Adding individual websites (rather than using preselected categories) is a pain, and it doesn’t always work.
- If you forget to unblock a profile, the child won't be able to use the internet. It'd be super nice if blocking of a profile only lasted until the next morning -- then I wouldn't have to remember to unblock.
- Circle’s EULA is long, and not my favorite, but it's pretty much what I expect of the industry.
- Functions by doing DNS poisoning of the local network, so yes, there can be problems from time to time.

When something isn't working, turn off CIrcle, reboot the main router, and see if it starts working again.
title: Pros & Cons -- a net win

I’m so excited about these headphones. I’ve worn them twice to go running this winter, and it keeps my ears warm and gives me wires-free music.

The pluses: The headband is very comfortable and it stays on while I run (in spite of a small head that headbands typically slip off). It’s easy to connect to an MP3 player and stays connected. The sound quality is fine for the purpose. The material is thick enough that it also acts as an ear warmer for outdoor jogging. The material is also dark enough that it blocks most light if you want to use it as an eye cover while sleeping. The speakers are thin enough that you could comfortably sleep lying on them.

The minuses: The speakers will be a bit of a process to remove to wash the headband. The thickness of the material may make it too hot to wear for summer workouts. The speakers aren’t in the ear, so for those who want to listen to their music a little louder, the people next to you will also likely hear it. If you want to use the headband for sleeping, there will be a space near the bridge of your nose that light can get in.

Overall: Perfect for me, especially for the price. Might not be ideal for everyone.

I just upgraded my motherboard to a new one with WiFi6 so I thought if I got a WiFi6 router I could get better speed connecting to my Synology NAS Plex server for uploading files. Testing with the router in the same room literally inches away from my computer antenna and with no other devices on the network the wifi speed never topped 650 mbps. I did an identical test with my existing Netgear Nighthawk. Same WiFi speeds and the Netgear actually outran the AX6000 by at least 15% using a wired ethernet connection.
This next part I was aware of when I bought it and was not a factor in the decision to buy. I'm just stating it for those who may not be aware.
The AX6000 boasts a 2.5Gbs speed WAN port. That's your internet connection. Who needs that even if it were true? My CenturyLink DSL connection runs at a measly 30 Mbps. Even a Cable One connection only runs at 100 Mbps.
Bottom line: If you already have an AC router don't waste your money on this. If you're upgrading from an N class-- don't waste your money on this. There are plenty of AC class routers available that are just as fast and less expensive.
And for Pete's sake don't fall for the special "gaming router" crap with the Star Trek design and a dozen antennas. Might as well flush your dollars down the toilet. I imagine the hard core pajama-boy gamers will disagree. Don't care. I'm addressing normal people.

text: I love the look and simplicity of this bag. A real leather product that seems designed to accept the scuffs and scrapes of regular use, and wears the added imperfections and battle scars with honor. The leather is stiff and thick which  would seem to offer added protection and the stitching seems durable. When closed there's a single zippered storage area with what seems like a good quality zipper. The front covering flap has a single magnetic fastener which when mated correctly offers good hold.  Open the flap and you'll find one open pocket on the front for papers or a magazine or two. The main storage area has a pocket suitable for holding even a very large cellphone and a looser pocket that will hold say bluetooth earbuds. The computer area holds my 13 inch MacBook Pro though a bit snuggly.  That main storage area is lined but with a basic fabric though nothing soft or plush. I imagine I might opt for a very basic sleeve to hold the laptop before sliding it in there to avoid scratches, though that might pose a size challenge. I put a generous Thule soft case in there and , well, it just doesn't work. With just the MacBook in there it barely closes and needs to be stretched for the flap to extend enough to connect securely with the magnetic closure. Also since there is no additional padding or protection at the base of the bag, I'm afraid if I set the bag down less than softly on, say a cement or tile floor, it could easily send an unfortunate shock to the frame of the computer potentially doing damage. The strap is adjustable and is made of the same leather with a fabric backing. I'd have loved to have seen an additional pad on the strap for more stability if you're wearing it over your shoulder but that can be found perhaps online hopefully with a similar finish. I was torn between a 3 or 4 star rating and decided for now to give it the benefit of the doubt since I haven't given it enough field use. But I'll revisit the review in a few weeks. In review, I love the look, the fact that it contains the most essential storage areas yet keeping it at a minimal size, the seemingly quality stitching and the leather finish what will only look more battle scarred and better with use. I will investigate some kind of water proofing but am aware that most of those sprays will definitely darken the leather and change the appearance. I will probably opt to experiment on the underside that will remain unseen if it dramatically alters the appearance and vibe. On the negative side is the minimal bottom side padding or protection as well at the slightly too snug fit that forces you to pull down to assure the magnetic closure aligns. If only the interior was slightly more generous, the lining a bit softer and the base offered even minimal padding for protection.

text:
Spend a little more and buy a name brand watch!

I have had this watch for 9 months now, and feel that is sufficient time to have given it a fair shake.

Right out of the gate I had issues with watch integration. Initially, they wanted me to have two apps on my phone- one to connect and one to track and display data. The two apps, from the same company, didn’t work well with each other, let alone with iHealth or MyFitnessPal. After some constructive feedback and some patience it seemed like they had fixed that. At least with step and heart rate data, not sure about workout data. But, that is fine, right? I don’t my looking at cycling info with the Amazfit app- whatever.

So, merrily we roll along. At some point I either stop caring or stop paying too close attention. Every once in a while the watch needs rebooted. Doesn’t all tech? A good sign when it’s time to reboot is when you stop getting notifications.

Everything is fine. My steps are being counted, my heart rate is monitored, I get text and email notifications, and I know when I’ve hit goal or I’ve been idle too long.

Then my charger breaks. It didn’t stop charging, but one of the plastic wings broke off so I had to hold my watch to it with a rubber band until I could order a new charger. No big deal, just another $10 to some other junk peddler.

I replaced my watch band also. It seems that if you actually wear your watch, the watch band will wear- as will other wearable wares (ha ha, words).

Well, as luck would have it, today I start paying attention again. I go to the Amazfit app, and find out that no data has been tracked since October! Okay, maybe I just need to sync. Syncing happens unusually fast this time. Normally it takes a while. Syncing complete and not only is two months of data not there, but the few steps this morning that are visible on the watch face are not there!

Alright alright. I get that technology isn’t perfect. I am close to this kind of thing in my work. Unpair & pair the watch. Of course, my steps from this morning are lost and unpairing almost acts like a factory reset (I say almost because I don’t exactly understand what it did, but it does allow restoration of settings from your account), but now my steps are syncing again.

Anyway, the moral of the story is that technology is sometimes more of a hindrance than a help...no, that can’t be right. The moral is, don’t buy an off-brand device and expect it to work like a more expensive one. (Tbh, my wife’s name brand watch was on sale and only slightly more expensive than this.) Another moral is, don’t fool yourself into buying some substandard product because you are envious of what someone else has, or you have otherwise convinced yourself you need a trinket.
title: Save Bucks and Buy a Watch That Sucks

text:
I had high hopes for this, but I'm somewhat disappointed. It works adequately for finding my keys or my phone, both of which I lose frequently. But the ring feature works spottily at best. I usually realize my phone/keys are gone when I'm late, so I'm panicking and pressing the button and ... nothing. The response is quite slow, and only works in (short) bluetooth range, so I have to slowly walk around my house, double click and wait. My house is 2032 sq ft and my taotronics headphones go clear across the house, but this tile only works within the same room. Sometimes it doesnt work when I'm standing right next to my keys.
Another disappointment is that the location history only works with your phone. Or at least mine does. I put my tile on the outside of my car as i drove around town, marking it as lost in the am and asking for community locating help. Without my phone also in the car, the tile doesnt ping at all. I find it hard to believe that in the Tampa metro area there are no Tile users. No location history showed up until I returned home, and brought it inside, and the only location was my house. This is while paying for the premium subscription, by the way.
TL;DR: This is ok for basic "ring my keys inside my house,so long as you never lose both keys and phone at the same time" functionality. Otherwise, a true gps tracker might be required.

text: I've purchased the Eufy Cam E wire free-HD Security Camera and am extremely happy with it. The installation process was seamless. I had some questions, so I called Keven at the customer service department and he was amazing to work with.  Here are a few questions I had.  One of the camera's night-time recordings were very dark compared with the other cameras.  He asked me if it was underneath the overhang of my house and I said it was.  Keven told me that it was very possible that I was getting a reflection that was influencing the camera.  Anything, like being next to light or picking up light reflections from the siding, can make a difference.  I changed the camera and sure enough, it made the difference.  Another question I had is that when I put the camera about 8 feet high and pointed down, I was getting more of the top of the head of anyone coming into camera view.  It was not much good for recognizing a face from that angle.  I dropped the camera down to more eye level and now it will have great value of facial recognition. Very pleased with the customer service department and love the EufyCam E-Security Camera. I definitely would recommend it.

text:
The biggest issue:
------------------

After about 3 months of continuous wearing, I started to get red, puffy, itchy welts on my wrist under the watch band, like two circumferential stripes coincident with the edges of the band. They are pretty significant and it takes a week or more for the skin to heal up when it happens. After some online searches, it turns out that this is a not uncommon problem. I solved it by getting one of the metal link band replacements offered here on Amazon: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B07KJYMZFM.

What I don't like:
------------------

Phone integration for text and call notifications is spotty. Sometimes they work and sometimes they don't. It's a nice feature when it works.

The phone downloads slowly but reliably to my Moto G7 Power. But getting the data from the phone to the Garmin servers then back to the phone too frequently gets delayed and makes the data unavailable to view in the Garmin app on the phone. When it works it's fine, but I do wish there was a simple way to extract the data to common format local disk files.

What I don't use:
-----------------

The other fitness features, like steps and move warnings. I don't find them all that useful.

The sleep tracking feature doesn't appear to be very accurate. Reading on the couch looks like sleep for example. It was interesting to look at for a few nights but not very actionable.

What I like:
------------

GPS and heart rate tracking during bike rides. These features are solid. I can go 4 or more days tracking 100 minutes of bike riding per day on a single charge. This feature is worth the price of admission.

24x7 heart rate monitoring. It's pretty handy for training to monitor one's resting heart rate to look for signs over over-training.

Alarms are nice. Unobtrusive for an office setting yet hard to miss. I wake with them too, but now after 6+ months of use, on occasion when I'm very tired I'll sleep through the watch alarm.

The weather information. I commute to work by bike. It's pretty handy to take a quick peek at the weather on the wrist before layering up (or down) for the ride home.

text:
The positive reviews on these that sound like advertising are 100% legitimate because these absolutely deserve the attention.
Sound quality is easily comparable to headphones 3x the price of these. The highs are crisp and clear and get better after a week of use once you get through the burn-in period. The emphasis on the mids is amazing and something you can really have trouble finding on headphones these days. The bass is full and heavy and definitely there without being too much and drowning the highs and mids. Vocals are 11/10 if you ask me, and I listen to a lot of folk and other genres where vocals are the focal point.
So far comfort has been exceptional and I'm someone who often has trouble with headphones aching after only an hour. I also ordered some aftermarket memory foam tips that improved comfort a lot but even with silicone, the fit is great.
I gave the sound cancelation a 4/5 only because they aren't active noise canceling and rely on the tips for sound cancelation. Even without active cancelation, these are great at eliminating outside sounds.
Connection has been easy, although I have had trouble with the headphones automatically connecting out of the case. This is pretty much a non-issue though as they connect quickly when you press the button on one of the two. I've had no issues with range and can easily walk around the kitchen or room and listen seamlessly.
Overall, these are the best headphones in this price range for the value. I'll update this review after I've used them for a few months.

EDIT: I'm still impressed with the audio quality but I've been having fairly severe connection issues. I've consistently had issues from the getgo but they've been tolerable until recently. As of today, especially (Feb 11, I bought these late December) the right headphone has been very glitchy and while watching youtube, consistently has a spotty connection and certain frequencies keep glitching in and out. It was happening with music too. If these headphones had reliable connectivity, they'd dominate the $100 range true wireless market. Additionally, I've had plenty of issues with the headphones changing EQ and volume without warning. It doesn't feel like an issue with my phone equalizer as these are the only headphones that do it. They'll suddenly go from rich, deep, bassy sound and wonderful clarity to flat and bland mid-song. I don't know what causes this. As another top review stated, they seem to have better connectivity when the left headphone is connected to your source device. I believe this is due to the left technically being the lead and so it does better with range and connection.

Honestly, I still recommend these and it may just be I got unlucky with mine. Hoping Lypertek reads this review and decides to help me out because I'm frankly really frustrated with the connectivity problems as it really ruins what I'm listening to.

EDIT- DECEMBER 2020 (ONE YEAR LATER)
I still love these suckers and Lypertek has released firmware updates since my initial review that seem to have solved many connectivity issues. (Additionally I had an issue where the left case slot quit working a couple months ago and Lypertek was very quick to resolve the issue, +10 respect.) Their app is still clunky but they're still pretty new to the headphone game so it's fine. I still recommend these to anyone who's picky with sound and on a budget. :)
title: Still Impressed- One Year Later (Edit)

text:
Hey all, this router is awesome for the price. I've recently outgrown the stock Comcast / Xfinity router, I'm using this router with a Plex server, a couple home hosted pc game servers with usually 5-10 people constantly logged in (from in and outside the local network) and it has seemed to improve performance and latency 10 folds over.

Also the user interface is great! Comcast would constantly reset my router causing me to loose all my port forwarding setup with no notice. Going 7 days strong with this new router. Set up took all of 45 minutes tops (including resetting up ports etc).

Also a huge PRO: comes with an easy setup configuration ( and built in) to run open-vpn. This is great for vpn'ing into the home network to be able to watch Hulu/Netflix while at work or school lol.

Only CON I can think of is wifi is decent, but somehow I got a stronger connection on my Comcast router, not a game changer because I hardly notice the difference.

Overall I DEF recommend this over using the limited and (control by Comcast) Comcast router. Would I buy it again, yes, but I might splurge and get like the Nighthawk R8000 instead.

Around 20 years ago when my parents got their first laptop, it actually came with fan for it. It wasn’t nearly as cool as this one, but as soon as I got a laptop myself I wanted one. Unfortunately, back when that happened I couldn’t find anything. I figured I’d look to see if they had them available now and found this one!
I was originally worried because it only had one fan, but fan inside this is really powerful, at least for what it’s trying to accomplish. My laptop used to sit on my lap or the bed and it would get pretty hot because of the lack of ventilation. However this one fan is so powerful that even when the laptop has been on for hours, it’s still cool to the touch on the bottom.

The lights are rather cool, but I was incredibly glad that they came with an off button because they are really bright. It would have been nicer if it had come with dimmer switch because I would have liked to be able to keep the lights on. However the only adjuster it came with was a speed dial for the fan. I pretty much keep it on full speed anyway so there was no point in having that on it, at least for my use. Though I’m absolutely certain it would be a good thing for other users.

I also wish the prop system had better staying power. If you move the laptop and fan up even minutely, whatever height you had set, automatically comes undone because there is nothing besides the large notch in the legs to grip onto. Essentially, the only thing that keeps it on the notch you have it on is the weight of the laptop on top of it holding it down. However, if you decide to move it or adjust where it’s sitting, you have to realign what level you had it propped at.

Overall, due mostly to the effectiveness and productivity of the fan, I do recommend this product.

-My unit came with a bit of backlight bleed in the bottom left corner, it seems like most users are getting this issue, which is very unfortunate. -I wish it came with integrated speakers, monitors around this price and even cheaper come with speakers like the viewsonic elite(check this monitor out)

Conclusion:
If your unit doesn’t have backlight bleed, then this monitor is perfect. If you don’t want to take the risk then you’re better off buying other monitors like viewsonic, LG, asus. Aside from the small backlight bleed the monitor is amazing(my unit at least)

This thing isn't perfect, I got 2 dvd discs from the 3rd season of the wire that for unknown reasons my computer cant detect in the drive. text:
I bought this card to replace my RX 570 graphics card hoping I would get a major boost in performance. That hasn't been the case so far.
I have Windows 10 up to date, the right graphics card drivers, the right power supply, everything. Everything is right in MSI Afterburner and power limit is set to +20. But still this card performs worse than my RX 570 at times, I'll be playing and my Core Clock frequencies will be all over the place, dropping to as low as 300mhz for no reason then spiking back up to 1750mhz, then up and down over and over again. No matter what I lock the frequency to, it still will go all over the place. This makes the frames rates range from 10-165 FPS and it creates massive stutters. I've done everything I can to get this card working properly it still, nothing. Definitely wouldn't recommend as of now.

(Edit)
I bought a replacement card and got the same result. I think I found the problem and I'm pretty sure it has to do with the VRM's (Voltage Regulator Modules) and a bad cooling configuration. Every time I start up a game, it seems to do fine, only for a minute or so. It starts off by running at it's intended frequency and proper power supply voltage, then GPU frequencies and power supply usage will drop drastically, then go back up and down again. These issues can be caused by overheating of the VRM's, which explains why my GPU's back plate gets unreasonably hot after only a few minutes of gaming. I guess I shouldn't be surprised though since the RX 5700's older brother (RX 5700 XT) from XFX got bad reviews from critiques because of bad cooling, and both cards look similar when it comes to the heating configuration.
title: Random Frequency Drops - Hinders Performance Massively.

text:
Initial review (only used for about 24 hours):

It’s better then I expected!

It’s sleek looks nice picture quality is good. No noticeable latency.

It’s smart enough to know what’s hooked up and actually displaying video. If I hook up 4 hdmi cords and only 2 are actually hooked up to a device it only allows you to cycle through the two active inputs. Aka if you have a ps4, PS3, Xbox 360, and Nintendo switch. If only the ps4 and Switch are on it will only cycle between the two of you press the “switch button.”
Just a nice little thing that keeps you from pressing button 4 times.
Im still playing with this though I’m not sure this feature works perfectly all the time.

Button feel on device is “meh” feels cheap but looks good so no big deal. And remote feels cheap, but I’m probably just going to throw remote out. Button on unit works just fine.

LED brightness isn’t excessive. So not intruding if you leave it directly under tv like I am.

Overall I am happy and would recommend.

Update: (couple weeks later)

That feature I said I would play with works perfect so far. As long as only one device of 4 is outputting video it will automatically switch.

So only issue with it is items that output video even though they are “off” or in “sleep” an example of this is an amazon fire stick which sends a signal of a blank screen to the tv instead of stopping the signal like most devices. So with a fire stick (or something that doesn’t turn off output) it won’t automatically switch.

Still happy with it! Would recommend.

Pros:
+ Hood for shading from sunlight or strong ambient light
+ 80W USB-C charging.
+ Height adjustable w/ Pivot, Tilt, Swivel
+ Blue light control & Flicker free
+ Picture in Picture and Picture by Picture
+ 3yr warranty
+ Reasonable price on Black Friday ($570)

Cons:
- Monitor goes blank periodically for 1-2 seconds making it unusable. I had this problem with Surface Pro 6 using Display Port 1.2 cable when the same computer/cable worked fine with a ASUS 4K monitor.
- Turning off power (using either the power switch or button or both) doesn't revert display back to monitor if connected using Display Port. It works as expected (i.e. display reverts to computer) if connected using USB-C.
- 2 power buttons w/ purpose not explained in manual. One would hope that if you had the switch on and button off then USB-C charging would still work but No, turning either off turns of USB-C charging.

For the problems listed under Cons I reached out to Amazon Tech Support thrice and ended up connecting with 7 folks who were totally clueless. I contacted Acer twice directly and the best they could offer was to send the monitor for repair or use power reset. The power reset stopped the display dropping for a few days but then the problem returned. I also tried latest Windows 10 Pro updates, Surface Pro 6 drivers, updated Dock drivers, Surface Diagnostics & all steps in Microsoft's article for troubleshooting connection to a second display (including clearing display cache) but they didn't help fix the display going blank issue.
title: Problems with Display Port support

text:
I purchased the Crucial MX500 500GB 3D NAND SATA M.2 Type 2280SS Internal SSD - CT500MX500SSD4 in order to increase my already maxed-out 256GB SSD.

I first installed the MX500 in this external M.2 USB adapter, then loaded the FREE Acronis True Image software on my laptop via the provided Weblink – surprisingly, this FREE software is included with the MX500. Using the “Clone Disk” option, it took about 15 minutes for the contents of my 256GB SSD to be copied to the new drive.

I installed the MX500 in my laptop and started it and the laptop ran as before, but now I had 500GB (well really ~475GB) of total space. It couldn’t be simpler.

I used this adapter for the initial transfer – it is very well made and worked perfectly. In addition, I now have a great 256GB SSD external drive (using the new external adapter).

My configuration:
Dell Latitude E7270
16GB RAM
Updated with MX500 = 500GB SSD (Original SSD = 256GB)
title: Excellent Product

text:
Let me dispel some of the negative comments here and hopefully provide a level of confidence in even the most novice of techies. I purchased the Crucial MX500 500GB 3D NAND SATA M.2 Type 2280SS Internal SSD - CT500MX500SSD4 in order to increase my already maxed-out 256GB SSD.

I first installed the MX500 in the external M.2 USB adapter (info below), then loaded the FREE Acronis True Image software via the provided Weblink – surprisingly, this FREE software is included with the MX500. Using the “Clone Disk” option, it took about 15 minutes for the contents of my 256GB SSD to be copied to the new drive, after which, a message from the True Image software stated, “Now Install the Drive in Your Computer and it will Run as Before.” Sure enough, I installed the MX500 in my laptop and started it and the laptop ran as before, but now I had 500GB (well really ~475GB) of total space. It couldn’t be simpler. I was planning to purchase the Acronis True Image software in preparation for the Disk Cloning, but I read in a review that it was included with the drive, and it certainly was; the software alone would have cost ~$50, so a great savings – THANK YOU Crucial!

I used this adapter for the initial transfer – it is very well made and worked perfectly:
https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B07PHFC4FP/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o07_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1

In addition, I now have a great 256GB SSD external drive (using the new external adapter).

Dell Latitude E7270
16GB RAM
Updated with MX500 = 500GB SSD (Original SSD = 256GB)

Comparing these to Sony WH-1000XM3. I prefer the Sony for everything except phone call quality. Music sound quality, bass response, noise cancelling, phone software, ease of use, fit and finish, material quality... all are better on the Sony. The only reason I purchased these Bose headphones was because of the improved microphone for voice calls. I can say the Bose do excel at this and phone calls are clear on the other end even in a noisy area such as an airport.

The iPhone software is horrible. I use these headphones on an airplane and the app is basically non-functional when in airplane mode or even just turning off cellular service. So you are left with only being able to adjust noise cancelling levels via the button on the headphones. Also, you are forced to create a Bose account just to use the app. Lastly, performing a firmware update took almost 45 minutes which seems excessive compared to any other typical firmware upgrade process.

If not for the voice call quality I would never use these headphones.
title: Terrible software and mediocre headphones

text:
My use case for this drive was to 1) watch Blu Ray discs I own on my computer, and 2) copy those movies to my computer as personal backups, in case the discs should become unusable in the future. At the time of writing this review, that usage is legal to do where I live. I have several different programs that I use to make personal backups of movies that I own.

So far, I have tried five Blu Ray discs, and this drive has been incapable of reading three of those five. Based on the inconsistency, I assume it has something to do with different types of copy protection. With the three failures, the computer does not even see that there is a disc in the drive, so none of my disc backup software can assess the copy protection to begin with. Had I known this would be an issue, I would not have purchased this item, as I already owned a DVD drive.

I ordered an LG WP50NB40 model to replace this purchase, and it has read every BD this item failed to read except for one - that one is a 4K UltraHD disc, which my computer isn't powerful enough to read anyway.
title: Struggles to read Blu Ray

text:
The case is pretty and sturdy enough. But it has a very disappointing design error that the manufacturer could have easily avoided and which makes this purchase one I regret. There is a notch carved into the inside cover flap that is meant to keep the page turn buttons from being hit when you close the cover. However, the notch is too small. It is barely big enough to cover the buttons, and will only do so if it is lowered in precisely the right position. The hinge has enough give that landing in exactly the right place is almost impossible to do. The result is that when I close the cover, the page will frequently turn in the instant before autosleep kicks in. Consequently, when I reopen the cover, the Kindle will be displaying the wrong page. Sometimes it's the previous page, sometimes the next page, sometimes it's off by more. On one occasion it was a good ten pages off!

Is it the end of the world that I can't use the autosleep feature and have to manually turn off the Kindle before closing the cover? No, it isn't. But one of the features I wanted in a cover was the ability to use the autosleep feature, and this cover was supposed to have it but doesn't.
title: Severe Design Defect Makes Autosleep A Problem

I compared these with my Apple AirPods and I can say these stack up pretty good against apple AirPods. For the price, you cant go wrong! Heres some of the things I liked.

-Noise Cancelling: These have noise cancelling which is a plus for me at the gym. This helps block some of the gym noises coming from machines and other people.

- Charging Case: The feel of the case and buds is nice, does not feel cheap at all. The case has a nice battery indicator that i thought was awesome! Not even apple does that. The indicator gives you a clear indicator of how much juice you have left (on the case). The charging case uses a USB-C for charging. The cable is included although it is super duper short. No power adapter is included but you can use your cell phone adapter.

- Battery Life: for me these have worked perfectly. I use these for the gym and was able to finish my 1hr workouts without having to charge.

- Pairing: was a breeze. Connected them in less than 1 minute (iPhone 11). Also after the initial pair, anytime you lift the buds from the case, by the time you put them in your ear, the buds have already paired with your phone.

- Sound Quality: not as clean/clear as apple. These sound really good! Great bass, but the mids and highs felt a little short for my taste. Nonetheless, not a cheap audio experience; however, audiophiles these will probably not make the cut.

- Buds Controls: the buds are comfortable and stay in place. They also have touch sensors and you can use this to tap to control play/pause music, skip/replay songs. During calls you also use this to hangup. I found this feature useful, although they are very sensitive, if you adjust the buds in your ear you may accidentally hangup or skip to the next track.

- Phone Calls: sound is clear on both sides. Compared to AirPods, my caller was not able to notice a significant difference on their side. On my side, things sounded good. If compared with apple, volume was a tad lower, but the quality was still really good.

text:
Starting with Pros/Cons

Pros:
+Name recognition. Bose makes good headphones. These earbuds deliver music as crisp as you'd expect from Bose.
+Cheaper than paying for hearing aides if you are borderline on needing them.
+Noise cancelling/amplification. It works. But settings are limited.

Cons:
- Short battery life. On full charge I got only around 2.5 to 3 hours of maximum use before having to take them off and recharge.
-Bulky and cumbersome. The collar ring is not flexible in any way to ergonomically lay flat to your neck.
- Earbud wires are too short. Every time I turned my head the wires would pull the earbuds out of place. Either look straight ahead or get used to readjusting the fit in each ear.
- Constantly opening the control app. The app has to be fully open to adjust any settings. Having to change settings constantly for varying volumes was a huge hassle.
- Documentation. It is sorely lacking any detail.

Why I rated as I did:

I bought a pair of Bose Hearphones to try and combat a very specific sort of noisy environment: attending competitive Irish dance events.

When hundreds of dancers are all performing hard shoe routines on 8+ wooden stages inside a gym/arena with live musicians (fiddle or accordion) accompanying them, the cacophony of sounds is often deafening and painful to me. But my daughter dances and loves it, so I needed to try something.

Do the Hearphones work? Technically, yes. The ability to set input between 360 degree, 180 degree (front) or 70 degree (direct front) focal areas is a nice feature. However - to amplify voices the Hearphones also amplify all surrounding sounds. To cancel out excess sound, voices are also cancelled out. The middle ground setting was no better than going without them. This was not clearly explained anywhere. I learned through a long day of trial and error.

Further the audio app needed to control the settings has to be open for every adjustment. There is no lock screen option for quick adjustments. While watching my daughter dance - with excess sound dialed out - I had to look down and adjust the settings to hear my wife or friends talking. And at the level I could easily hear them, the hearphones were again passing all sounds through in an amplified state making a loud environment worse.

By the end of the day I had a migraine and was left frustrated at how limiting the settings were.

The ability to selectively cancel (some/all) excess sound while still passing voices through is what I was looking for. In the situation I need these to help me, they do not.
title: They work. More or less.

text:
If you have an older Silverado (2003 vintage) with door tweeters, these will work if you have a 2" hole saw. The stock tweeters are mounted in a oval shaped bracket held with two metal nuts. Pull out the bracket, carefully break out the stock tweeter, then drill a 2" hole right where the stock tweeter was. Use the included saw-tooth ring to slightly increase the diameter of the new tweeter. Apply super glue around the perimeter of the new tweeter, place it in the new hole, and clamp or weight it down until the glue dries.
I then cut the plug off of the old tweeter leaving about 3" of wire and soldered it to the new tweeter wire, also cut to about 3". As I recall, the blue wire of the stock tweeters is positive. Put the bracket back in place, plug in the electrical, and you are done.
title: Older Silverado door tweeters

text:
I bought this for 170ish on sale, and I have to say that I am impressed with what I got for that price point. I purchased this to be a word processing/on the go browsing machine, and it is fully capable of that. I had a surface 3 for about 4 or 5 years, but that caught fire a couple months ago due to an issue with the fan. I decided that I could downgrade since I don't do digital illustration any longer. I had no problem downloading Chrome (you just have to switch it out of S mode, and it gives you prompts to do that).

By any means, don't expect a gaming computer or a computer that could run PS (with four tabs of chrome open, 61% of the ram is occupied and 15-45% of the CPU is too), but if you want something to use on the go, this is it. It's light, it's small, and it works for what it needs to. Nice little computer. Seems like the battery is lasting pretty well, too.

Some other thoughts:
- The screen is really bottom of the barrel. Turn up the brightness a lot and use it somewhere with very little glare. That kind of helps. I am pretty sure it's the same ones they were putting in think pads a decade ago.
-Came with really minimal bloat ware, but most of it uninstalled pretty easy.
-Pairs easily with my Bluetooth headphones.
-Knock-off macbook aesthetic. Not a positive or a negative, just is.

text:
Let me preface this by saying I was an early adopter of FireTv. I have been on board since the beginning and have owned at least 1 of every version of FireTV device (except the new Gen 2 Cube). For the most part I have loved these devices, especially my 2 FireTV Cubes. That is, until October of 2019, about the time Amazon started making major changes to FireTV OS. Until that time, these were definitely 5 star devices.

My issues started in October (I think). It also has affected my FireTv 4k stick, FireTv 4k pendant, etc. These devices have become very buggy since Amazon started upgrading FireTv OS. Cubes randomly freeze or close apps. Very slow response (sometimes). CEC stopped working on 4k stick. I have to restart the devices regularly. None of these issues existed prior to the OS "upgrades". I'm really shocked at how badly these upgrades have been managed. What was a great device (devices) has become a crap-shoot of sorts. When will the device freeze? When will I have to power cycle it? Because I know it will happen. If I had only 1 FireTv device, I would have definitely thought I was having hardware issues. But no, ALL my Fire TV devices have been affected, but none more than the FireTV cubes.

I don't want to completely change my electronics ecosystem. I love being able to turn lights on/off via voice. Or playing music. My grandkids thought it was so cool Alexa could turn on the Christmas tree lights. But right now the main function as an audio/video controller is severely compromised.

Oh, and while you are busy fixing FireTV OS, please add FandangoNow and VUDU to the appstore. I have a large online video library and unfortunately it is impossible to have one app contain all of my movies due to movie studio rights. So do us devoted Amazon users a solid and make life easier by adding these apps.
title: Amazon, Please Fix FireTV OS

text:
After doing a lot of research, I decided to build myself a new computer. I have built several PC's in the past, so I had an idea of what I wanted in a new one. After comparing several different motherboards, I settled on this one since it checked most of the boxes I was looking for like x570 chipset, 2 M.2 NVME slots, and support for the newer Ryzen processors. Cost was also a factor in my decision, I had a target budget in mind and for the price, this seems to have the most features. I thoroughly checked compatibility with all of the components I was planning to use on ASRock's website. Most motherboards are particular about the brand and type of RAM that is being used. I built the computer with casual gaming in mind, so paired this motherboard with the Ryzen 3600x processor, corsair memory, Nvidia graphics card and a Samsung M.2 NVMe drive for fast loading of games and operating system. These components proved to work well with this motherboard and I have had no trouble with the system so far.

The motherboard does have some lighting on it and looks clean if you plan to install it in a case with a glass window. I opted to install this in an existing case of mine that did not have a window, so the aesthetics was not a concern of mine.

text:
Pros:
-Seems good quality construction
-Super Easy to setup, connect and go
-No apparent compression
-It works great for movies, presentations, pictures and other stuff with a low frame rate.
-When it gets hot it disconnects till it gets cool, this is good in the sense that it just doesn't burn or melts, they have a failsafe so it's something.
-Can be used with something with highish framerate if you strap it to a fan

Cons:
-Gets hot when you push it, I was using it for Zwift (kind of a video game) and it would get hot and disconnect leaving you stranded for minutes.
-There is signal degradation with high bit rate movies (when there is too much going on on the screen, like a car chase)
-Doesn't activate Samsung Dex or desktop mode on android phones, just does screen mirroring.

Conclusion, it works, but is not meant for heavy duty usage, has poor heavy heat management, but at least it has overheat protections in place which prevent it from burning, and you can ducttape it, to a cooling fan and it works great that way.

The signal degradation issues are inherent to this kind of devices, even if the signal is totally uncompressed is a digital signal and data is lost along the way, specially with obstructions or electrical/static noise (which we all have with so many wireless crap around us) or if the frame rate is high, there is only so much data that makes it thru and you start seeing artifacts and pixelation all over the place.

Don't get me wrong, is very usable, I'm very picky so this whole thing is very very subjective, for movies is only in some parts where you can see issues, but for the most part, it looks like your regular Netflix stream, for games it craps out a bit, but hey at least I don't have to run a 5meter/15ft cable across my room and into the drywall so there is that. If you want to show pictures, movies or a presentation and you have a direct line of sight between the transmitter and receiver this thing is great I tested it to 10 meters/30ft (ran out of room) and still worked flawlessly.

So again, the whole thing is very subjective depending on what is good picture quality for you.

I'm still debating whether to keep it, mostly cause I hate having to cool it down, the fan is just an extra thing I have to connect to another usb port which I hate. If it didn't had that issue I wouldn't mind the slight picture degradation that it gives while gaming or when Michael Bay is blowing too much stuff up and trying to get you dizzy by spinning and shaking the camera all over the place.
title: Manage your expectations.

text:
Today's mice try to do it all, and thus have many buttons and settings. That makes sense if you use a mouse for "real work" as well as gaming, but for those of us who are minimalist and need a wireless mouse to simply BE a get-it-done mouse, those do-it-all mice are overkill (and overly expensive). If this describes your need--a mouse that does the simple mouse functions--this mouse is perfect. It has only two buttons and a scroll wheel (which is a third button). No extraneous buttons in the thumb-rest, no choices to make. It is very comfortable with a very "grippy" textured rubber surface that gives it a very secure feel in the fingers, especially for finer movements. (The arch might be a little low and not sit right in your palm if you have larger hands.) And, as the name implies, the buttons are very quiet when depressed; just a soft tap sound.

Another blessing (for minimalists like me) is that it is NOT a Bluetooth mouse. It uses a very small USB dongle and the wireless connection is very solid. Unlike with Bluetooth (BT), there is no lag in transmission (which sometimes occurs), or interference with other BT devices or weirdness getting the BT to connect. Absolutely, some people need BT, particularly if they want to use the device on more than one device. And, it is true you tie up a USB port, but often a good keyboard will have an extra one or two USB slots, and/or there are USB hubs. (The major drawback would be if you used this with a computer such as the newer MacBooks that only have type C ports. Then, you would need an adapter for the USB A style dongle, which becomes unwieldy. In that scenario, a BT wireless mouse is better.)

LogiTech claims a batter life of two years. If by chance I'm still around and remember, I'll update this post in two years and let you know! But at the low price of this mouse (less than twenty at time of purchase in 2019) even if the entire device only lasts two years, it's a bargain.

In sum, if you need a wireless right-handed USB (not BT) mouse with nothing more than basic functions that feels great, is very quiet, and is at a bargain price, look no further.
title: Perfect for those who just want a solid, reliable, quiet and simple mouse

I have never used the camera of my MacBook Pro (13" mid 2012 model) and to prevent anyone from snooping in on me, I had covered the camera with a couple of layers of black electrical tape. This method has worked perfectly for me. But I got the opportunity to try these stick-on camera slide covers and I can't give it more than 3 stars.

I haven't used the camera on the screen side of my old iPhone 6 plus so that also had a small sticker covering the camera. Aside from a protective case, I also have a screen protector in place. But I'm surprised that I was able to install one of these camera slide covers on the camera that's above the screen. I always keep my phone in the left front pocket of my pants. And the camera cover didn't stay for long before it disappeared.

I did had some difficulties installing these slide covers because they're small and need to be installed exactly over the barely visible camera of my MacBook Pro. And the slide cover I tried to install on my first attempt broke and was no longer usable. Glad I received more slide covers in my order so I had a replacement for the broken one.

The glue of these camera slide covers weaken if it needs to be repositioned. Best to use a new cover than try to reposition one. It was really hard to reposition them once they were stuck on a surface. It's good to have many of these slide covers because of the reasons mentioned above.

text: My daughter felt the need to upgrade to a new MacBook Pro Air.  I'm not a fan of Apple products (Microsoft/Google person), but I could tell from troubleshooting her old MacBook Pro (13" 2012 model) that there was basically nothing wrong with it that a new hard drive and battery wouldn't solve.  Sure enough, I put the 500GB SSD and a replacement battery in it for ~$100, and the thing now runs better and faster than it did new.  She's happy with her new MacBook Pro Air, and I'm learning how to use a MacBook Pro. Overall, I'm not very impressed with MacOS and the MacBook in general, but I can see how people who have other Apple products would like for their laptop to be the same eco system. The drive was an easy install, it was easy to restore the OS from the internet, and it's much faster than the original spinning hard drive, which had become REALLY slow (especially when booting) probably because it was failing. This is not my first SSD rodeo, as I upgraded my and my son's gaming laptops (Windows) to SSD drives, but this was my first experience at upgrading anything in a Mac.  It was relatively the same as a PC, but it was a much more significant improvement.
title: Replaced a hard drive in MacBook Pro 2012...

text:
I've mounted probably a dozen TVs and in brick and drywall (with and without studs) - each with a different mount bracket - and ECHOGEAR's is the best quality and easiest to mount I've ever used. Here's why:

- Comes with a mounting template (missing, strangely, from so many other brands) that makes hole positioning a breeze.
- Comes with every assortment of mounting bolt under the sun for attaching your television to the mount.
- Has tilt adjustment in the bracket (think "roll axis" of a plane) so, despite my OCD driving me to mount it as level as possible, I can still tweak it once mounted.
- Massive range of positioning for swiveling your TV to left or right, and very smooth articulation for repositioning once mounted (which with this one we do regularly).
- Large spacing in the mount plate so if you're running wires in the wall it can accommodate even double-sized panels sitting within the open spaces of the mount plate.
- Accommodates a crazy range of TV sizes, good for future-proofing!

Worth considering: the 42"-85" mount is quite heavy at just over 25 lbs. Combine this with it's size and it may be tough for some to install solo. In my case, as soon as I had one lag bolt partially in a stud it was like having a second helper (that bolt could support one side while I did the other) but you may want a hand for just the first bolt. That said, the weight is indicative of the build quality.

I'm pretty sure I'll never buy a different brand mount again. This one is just too good and was so easy to install, especially considering the sub-$100 price. Absolutely great product.
title: Best mount I've ever installed...well worth the $$

Now Sony did end up pushing an update that introduced the ability to adjust volume from either the left or right ear buds, but that is at the cost of sacrificing one of the more (in my opinion) more critical features. The taking one bud out feature to pause music can be spotty at times (having my finger accidentally touch the sensor on the ear bud will give a false positive that they are back in my ear, and my music or the video I'm watching will begin playing til I take my finger off. The case isn't too large and fits nicely in my pocket. The ear tips they sent with them are generous and have allowed me to fine tune how comfortablr these are in my ears. text: My hopes weren't real high for these cameras upon seeing the price.  However, I currently have 2 version 2's and they have had nothing but issues since I installed them over the past couple days.  The main issue I am having is the cameras keep going offline according to the app on my android phone.  The app will show they are just randomly offline on the app's overview screen, but when you actually click on the camera it is in fact online, not offline.  The issue with this is they do not record events during this time and Alexa cannot control them.  The weird thing is the continuous recording still captures everything.  So you can rewind back on the continuous recording off of the micro SD card and see everything during this, "Offline", period.  You can even see the little green boxes capturing and outlining motion on the screen, but it does not record it as an event and no notification is ever sent.  Apparently many others have had this issue as well.  I hope this is an issue that can be fixed via software or firmware updates.  As of now I cannot recommend these cameras as they are not reliable, but what do you expect for $25.

text:
Mine's been flaking for a while but I figured it was my ISP. By the time I figured out it was the modem I was a few days passed the 2 year warranty.

I bought a CM500 for $20 to replace it, as I don't need 3.1 yet and was assuming the Motorola would last longer.

Anyways, if you have the drop problem, or you can't get to the admin page at 192.168.100.1 (best indicator of an issue, AFAICT), try leaving the modem unplugged for 15 minutes or so and plug it back in. I had drops every 4 hours on the dot, but if the admin page was still accessible 1 hour after booting, it would be stable until the next power outage.

Seems that power cycling too quickly puts it into an unstable state. Don't waste your time with this, but if you have no other options, try the above. If 15 minutes doesn't work, try overnight. But really, just buy a used CM500 for 20 bucks unless you need 3.1.
title: Probably not worth the risk

What I don’t like: The battery life is short when using the LED backlight feature. I also don’t care for the texture of the vinyl the case is covered in. The keys on the keyboard sometimes make a plastic “scrunch” sound typical of cheaper keypads.
I needed a keyboard/case for my new iPad generation 7 tablet. I also did NOT want to spend the large sums of money that Apple asks for its keyboard/cases. I found this on amazon and immediately liked it because I’m NOT a touch typist and often am working in low light conditions, so the backlit keyboard is to me a godsend. Bluetooth setup was fairly easy. The main thing I don’t like about this keyboard is the battery doesn’t seem to last very long; likely I would get more battery life if I didn’t run the LEDs all the time ; ) The other pet peeve I have is the texture of the vinyl - it has tiny grooves that I don’t like the feel of and that tend to attract and hold dirt, food crumbs if I’m working at a dining table, etc. The keys have a cheap feel; I’m not sure how long this thing will last, though I have been using it solidly for about a month and so far it seems OK.

Despite the couple drawbacks I mentioned, I like the product so far and am glad I got it. I would recommend it to anyone with similar needs as I stated above.

text:
I only bought this because my Prolimatech Megahalems did not support AM4 and they had no updated mounting hardware for it. Decided to go with a company that appears to future support their coolers which Noctua does from what I have read. The box, packaging and instructions all are top notch quality. Once I read through the instructions I figured it would mount rather well being the price and quality of company behind it. Once I installed the support bars I placed the cooler down and prepared to tighten the last 2 main attachment screws. It took me a few minutes of pressing the screwdriver down trying for the threaded portion to catch. I simply tried to start the threads on one side with only a few turns to get it to catch but then on the other side I could not get it to grab on. I finally got the threads to start and it screwed down fine from there. My previous cooler is NIGHT AND DAY better mounting, it uses basically the same style of mount but the quality is SO much better on the Prolimatech. You simply place the cooler on the cpu just like the Noctua but then the two final screws easily hand thread into position without any force or stress to get them started. Then you take a screw driver and can easily and carefully tighten each side down a little by little till fully tight. Yes this Noctua worked but the mounting style is far inferior to what I have been using these last 8 or so years. The cooling performance in the benchmarks show the Noctua does cool a few degrees better than my previous cooler which is nice considering my disappointing view of the install. Yes the mount system works and sure plenty of people got theirs to thread in on the first try, that still does change my opinion on the much better designs out there. Last this Noctua 14 cooler keeps my stock AMD 2700x at around 40c-45c while gaming.

I bought better coolers for a few reasons.
1.) Keep the CPU cooler for ease of possible overclocking
2.) Less noise with better heatsink and lower fan speed
3.) Less force required in installation, easier to get the thermal compound the way you want when installation is simple. In the past heavy force had to be applied always risking damage to hardware. Some coolers really make on/off of the cooler a pleasant experience.

#3 is why this cooler got a 4 out of 5. It's a great cooler from appears to be a great cooler company. They need to look around and see what out premium cooler companies have done. I truly wish there would have been a adapter kit for my old Megahalems as not only was it very close in performance but mount is a 10 out of 10. I would rate the Noctua mount 7 out of 10.
title: Great performance, for a premium company the mounting could be improved.

text:
Pros:
Low price.
Room for full size components.
Clean, basic aesthetics.
Tempered glass side panel.
Room for cable management behind motherboard tray.
Full length power supply shroud.
Filters for front and top fan mounts and bottom power supply mount.
Excellent airflow.
Ample front I/O.

Cons:
Front panel connectors a bit short for full size ATX boards, depending on connector location.
Front fan filter clipped in to front panel, very difficult to remove for cleaning.
Bottom power supply fan filter very flimsy.
Power supply shroud cutouts for cables very small/awkwardly placed - a third cutout closer to the rear panel would have been a huge help.
CPU power connector cutout not large enough for 8 pin connectors with motherboard installed. Not an issue for 4+4 pin connectors.

Notes:
Sheet metal is fairly thin - rear panel is easily bent if force is applied.
PCIe slot covers are breakaway style, rather than replaceable.
Front of case has a 5.25" bay cutout, and another 5.25" breakaway cover below it, but the front panel only has room for one 5.25" bay, and the case only has mounting points for one bay. Seems to be re-used tooling from an older case.

Overall, this is clearly a budget case, and some corners were cut to get it down to this price point while including the glass side panel. I do not feel the cut corners take anything away from the overall appeal or value proposition of the case, but they should be noted. A couple basic changes could significantly improve this case in terms of compatibility with more hardware: a slightly larger EPS power cutout, a third cutout in the PSU shroud close to the rear panel, a front cutout running across the PSU shroud (and a [re]movable HDD cage) to allow for 360mm radiator mounting, and slightly longer front IO cables would make this a no-brainer in any build.

Overall, would highly recommend to anyone looking for a case under $50, intend to use it again for additional budget builds.
