text:
Although highly reviewed, for the price I'd rather stick with my Steiner military binoculars for the following reasons: Steiners have better night vision, they are more compact, the rubber coating is a thousand times tougher, the separate lens mounted diopters are stiff and therefore rarely get accidentally adjusted, the 60 feet to infinity auto adjust is a far superior technology, and a smaller magnification in the Steiners gives a clearer view of objects than a larger magnification and larger field of vision of similar Nikons.
Do yourself a favor and check out the Steiner line of binoculars.
Just as a side note: I just returned a pair of 8x30 police issue Steiners that were literally destroyed from 15 years of use at my outdoor work environment as a patrol ranger. Steiner sent me a brand new pair of military/marine 8x30 free of charge under their warranty. A $300 value. While they were in return, I used my Monarch 5 binoculars in the field for 3 weeks. In just that time the rubber coating has started to show extreme wear and I was constantly needing to adjust them because the center diopter moves so easily.
The Nikons might be okay for birding, which I do as a hobby, but the Steiners are by far the superior binoculars for field use such as hunting, camping, work, etc.
title: Pick Steiner brand over Nikon for extreme field use.

text:
There are only a few buttons on this camera, which would *seem* like a good idea for a child's camera, but the reality is it's really hard for anyone to figure out how to operate the simple basics (like switch between picture and video modes, view and/or delete files, scroll through and select settings, set date and time, switch to the selfie camera, etc.).

The other major problem is the SD card it came with malfunctioned and completely quit working within the first hour of use, making the camera unusable. Plus we lost all pictures and videos from Christmas morning.

Also overlooked by the manufacturer is how to delete files. You can only delete one at a time after two or three buttons pushed each time. We haven't found a way to delete them all at once. Our 3-year-old walks around taking pictures of everything and fills up the card in about 25 minutes, then just wants to be able to take more (not caring about saving what she's taken). But she can't use the camera at all until an adult goes through and deletes hundreds of pictures one by one. The deleting of pictures takes almost as long as it takes the child to fill up the SD card.

Lastly, the battery life is quite short--an hour or two at most--and you have to plug it in to recharge. You can't swap out batteries while the first ones charge.

Works perfectly on my 2012 Rav4 Limited with ONE caveat.
It's shown for use with a SVX100 or SVX200 tuner but CAN work just fine with the new SVX300 series tuners. If you do that, your stations will start at channel 130 with no ability to go lower. Luckily I know about electronics and what the dip switches' purposes are on what is basically just a relayed junction box circuit board so I checked everything was working correctly before I put everything back together (which is what I strongly recommend you do as well).
But it works as advertised and isn't that bad for the money.

I like backpacks as a means of carrying things either for the day or a few days. I like innovative high-quality backpacks that are constructed very well, are waterproof, and are completely utilitarian for my out of the ordinary uses.

My preference is toward form and function working well together to make my daily life better and more efficient. I don't like flashy backpacks and I have a bias toward plain and unnoticeable, unremarkable.

The reason is I don't want to make my carry possessions attractive to a thief. This bag is far from ordinary-looking or functioning. I am thoroughly impressed with the construction of this bag, the compartments, and the zippers. This bag is very comfortable to wear, even loaded with a weekend's worth of clothing and toiletries, my laptop and cords, etc.

This bag is much better looking than in the photos and to me, it appears to be a very long-wearing bag. I mean I STUFF this thing FULL and it still is easy to carry and still looks good. With all of my really important things inside this bag, being waterproof, sturdy, and very well-reinforced with steel cables to thwart slash and grab attempts, I feel secure putting my most important possessions in this bag and going about my life.

This is a way better bag than the price indicates.

The LINGANZH Smart Power Strip Can be very useful for multiple appliances or decorative holiday lights, provided that the electrical cord is long enough to connect with the power strip.

Installation isn’t a problem for tech saavy individuals, but for less tech saavy people, if there is a problem, it may be difficult to figure out trouble shooting in how to connect to WiFi or activate Alexa skills.

If I decide to manually turn on a device earlier than the start time, the device may not shut off on its scheduled time. The device stays on. You have to manually turn it off. Alexa skills for this device works very well. You just have to remember what you name each device you attach to the power strip.

I would recommend this WiFi power Strip for converting your home to a smart home.

text:
The motion detection on thses cams is very good and highly customizable. The night vision is much better than expected. The field of view is tremendous, only a little fish eye distortion in the very outer fringes. Clarity is good, wish the resolution was greater so one could read license plates when zooming in. The WiFi connection could use improvement. I had to purchase 2 WiFi extenders to get 2 cams I have in trees close to my house to connect, one of which is in my daughter's bedroom window ~25 feet away and the best the Cam will register is a RSSI of 68 and the other which is further away registers a RSSI of 57 - go figure. That being said, capturing "live" movement once a notification can be challenging as it takes several seconds to connect especially during the day with full color (more data, response time is much better on night vision.)

I have a wired Floodlight camera too and the video quality is indistinguishable from the three battery cams.

The battery life is quite good, once you configure your unit not to capture every squirrel sneeze - I had no idea my front stoop was a squirrel playground until I installed one of these cams.

I don't have any experience with all the other cams on the market but i have been in high tech for ~35 years and have to say that the Ring app and UI are both friendly and robust, there really hasn't been a time where I've said to myself "I wish I could ..."
title: Great cam, simple to install, robust app

This is a neat little camera and I like the quality of the picture for what they are. It's super light and easy to use. You do have to be careful framing the shot but they indicate that in the instructions so fair enough. BUT...

The picture button is seriously flawed and seems designed to waste film. I pressed it for a test picture. It played a little tune which I assume meant it took a picture. But there was no other indication and it didn't print for quite some time so I took another picture. It played a tune. And I waited. It eventually printed both pictures. I put the camera down. Picked it up, and fat fingered another picture.

Long story short, the button presses too easily and has no rim protection to prevent accidental shots. And although it's probably a pro that it can take multiple shots before waiting for printing to finish, it's a learning curve. I'd give it at least another star if they protected the shoot button (and power button) and added a couple second delay to prevent double shots.

Lastly, even for a simple camera with simple instructions, they are lacking. Does the camera auto power off? They don't say. What do the indicator lights on the back mean? Does red mean its charging or charged? Blinking versus non blinking. Simple things, overlooked, that I have to figure out through trial and error.
title: Good with a Couple of Irritating Flaws

text:
I bought this to replace my old laptop, I bought this laptop during a sale and got a great price on it. Overall the performance is acceptable, it can place most games I'm interested in on medium to high. The biggest downside is that the fan doesn't have a quiet profile, and anything you do at all causes the fans to run up to 100% for no perceivable reason.

For example:
You open chrome to check your email -> fan = 100% speed
You open a jpeg file -> fan = 100% speed
You watch a movie on netflix -> fan = 100% speed
You play a game -> fan = 100% speed

I dug through the BIOS for what felt like hours and came to the conclusion that there is simply nothing you can do about the fan noise, a bit of followup research on google determined that I'm not the only person who's a little upset by this.

If you don't mind constant fan noise and this is on sale definitely get it, but if you don't like to listen to constant fan ramping then I'd recommend avoiding this laptop. The fan is so loud that I've had coworkers ask what's wrong with my laptop, big f'in oof on Asus' part.
title: Fan is super loud, no cool'n'quiet or comparable bios functionality

text:
This thing isn't inherently bad, but it was a strikeout for me. I was hoping for something clean to use in the bathroom - I have 3 devices to plug in (razor, Alexa, and trimmer charger) - they all have big plugs, so I figured the big spacing would work out well, and the USB is a bonus for charging my phone while getting ready and having my phone on to control the music coming through Alexa. The price was great too.

Unfortunately, it struck out. No matter how I try to orient my 3 plugs, I can't make them all fit. The plugs just aren't quite far enough apart. It's a shame, because they were obviously spaced apart for something bigger than a standard plug.

Design-wise, I'd definitely give it a 3. The single plug that goes into the existing outlet is dead center - meaning when you install this, it'll cover both plugs, but it's not aligned with the outlet - it's off-center either towards the top or the bottom - so for anyone picky about aesthetics, it may bug you. Also, it does not have the screw that goes through the middle to secure it, so it'll be wobbly.

text:
Wow these are amazing!
My requirements that headphones are MUST have or else I'll return them are
- SUPER LOUD volume
- Heavy Bass
- Great sound quality
- Durability
- Battery life
- easy controls

Those requirements might seem common sense for all brands to follow and try to produce before putting a product for sale, but let me tell you, I've been buying the big brand popular headphones lately and have been returning them all after two days of testing them and getting disappointed.

The 950n1 I use it at the gym and am EXTREMELY rough on these headphones! I'm in the sauna for two 30min sessions, and they never stop working due to over heat, my phone will stop working until I leave the sauna and it cools down, but not the headphones. They get thrown around in my gym bag, have fallen down many times and they're still going strong after year and half! I know I'll keep going back on used markets and repurchasing these for many years to come when they do eventually break.
They're large, so if you're self conscious about the looks, then they might not be for you.
The controls on the side is by far the best on any headphones.
Incredibly loud, fantastic mids and AMAZING bass! I just don't understand why everyone doesn't try to copy these headphones?!
I'm writing this review now cause the past 3 months I've been on a hunt to find another great set of headphone just like these, not to replace, but to add as I like headphone.

The Skullcandy Skull crushers are bad! Their sound quality are of $30 headohones, they get all the attention due to their silly fake bass sliding gimik, please don't fall for it. But they do have excellent battery life and good built quality.

The V-moda Crossfade wireless were the closest ones that got to the Sony's. Excellent built quality, great looks and built quality, loud volume, good enough bass, but not Sony's level, Sony's level of bass is the maximum you can get while still have excellent mids. Vmoda has 75% of Sony's bass and excellent bass as well. The deal with the vmoda were that they're INCREDIBLY tight on your head and after 1hr your ears will be aching! The battery life was also very poor.
Keep in mind I listen to my music at high volume so the battery will not last as what it's advertised on the box, but the Sony will easily go two plus weeks if not three weeks without needing to be charged.
Unfortunately returned the vmodas. I think I'll buy them again in the future when they have folding ear cups, not as tight and better battery because their sound is excellent!

Now down the the Beats Studio 3s, these are pretty good, and I ended up keeping them, not because they're as good as the Sony's, but they do everything at B+ at least.
- Loud volume
- great bass
- great battery
- fast charging

Cheap built quality so I know it'll break soon, so I wear it at the office, not at the gym, Evey review warns you that it'll eventually break and I can see why, it's super thin and plasticy.
The mids not as good as the Sony's or vmodas, but they're very comfortable and have the best sound isolation compared to all others, which is why it's good for the office.

The most disappointing unfortunately has been the JBL Under Armour Sport Train Wireless( The Rock's Headohones)
They look and feel excellent, they have thought of many things synch as pass thru feature and fast charging but holy moly they get the major stuff wrong.
- no where loud enough with Bluetooth or wired
- when wired non of the headphones buttons commands work, you have to turn up the volume and change songs via phone(very inconvenient).
- heats up and stops working in the sauna.
- poor poor battery life, it's advertised at 16 hrs which with my high volume it'll give me like 10hrs at best.
- it has good mids, but not enough bass nor enough volume.
- they are very well built and fold the best out of all of them to be the most compact in your bags, washable ear cups is very cool.
I wish JBL had paid more attention to the high volume and bass cause its loud inside the gym and you're needing to get pumped up, these are the number one priorities of a gym headphone!

If I could make a baby out of all of these it would be
Vmodas mids, with Sony's bass and volume.
Sony's battery
Fast charging of Beats
The sound isolation of the Beats Studios 3s
Sporty looks of the JBL

I hope some manufacturers sees this and makes this.
Sony is the one with majority of the fields with a A+ in each category. Sony's really don't have any cons honestly.

text:
If you're trying to get a budget 5.1, this system is actually really fantastic when the price point is under $200. I did a lot of research before I bought these and needed something specific, these checked off the list perfectly.

The design is beautifully minimal with the satellites and speakers featuring all black details. The only branding is the ELAC logo on the metal grille, which you can barely see. The subwoofer matches the styling from ELAC’s Andrew Jones designed higher end line. This is probably the only piece in the set that has a clear brand name with its embossed ELAC branding in dark silver.

I tested the ELAC CINEMA 5 system running off a DENON S750H AVR in Surround with lots of different content. The system is setup in my living room that measures approx 10x12’ with high ceilings.

I tested the system with the following media:

Films and shows: Star Wars: The Force Awakens, The Witcher, Our Planet.

Video games on the PS4 such as God of War, Spider-man, Jedi: Fallen Order.

Music ranging from Latin, Jazz, trap, hip-hop, house, techno, and mid-range to bass heavy music.

It's a satellite based sound system, so you need to accept that the midrange and low-end of the satellites will not compare to the bookshelf-type speakers that most audiophile forums/posters/etc will recommend all the time...but that’s perfectly fine in this use case.

Everything coming out of the satellites is super clear and crisp, but as they don't have deep mids or lows the subwoofer picks up those frequencies. If you have your sound setup properly via your AVR this will be seamless and sound perfect.

The subwoofer is pretty beefy sound wise even at 100 watts PEAK RMS. Is it as powerful or detailed as a studio sub which can go down to 23hz? No, of course not. But you're not buying it for that. Yes it doesn't go below 40hz, but neither do a lot of subs at this price point (go look, you won't find any decent ones that do).

Footsteps from an alien in Star Wars: The Force Awakens sounded clear and defined. The hum of Thano's spaceship in Avengers: Endgame makes you feel like you're on board (I had a 250 watt sub from another HTIB before that didn't have this definition), and music bumps with clear definition between the kick and sub-bass. With that said, it's really good for the price point and will shake your apartment.

Here's the other thing, as I said before it also comes down to how you tweak your sound settings in your AVR. Nothing will sound amazing by default on any speaker unless you optimize. With the right settings on your AVR this system will sound great in your room.

Construction is solid, no rattling or vibration. The satellites and subwoofer have a hefty weight but are minimal and clean.

**Here's who should get the system:**

You have an apartment or small area with limited space but you want better sound than a sound bar

You want a 5.1 setup to use with an AVR and don't want to shell out a lot of money for absurdly oversized "bookshelf" speakers

You want small satellites for your surrounds

You can't convince yourself to pay 500+ for a Sound bar system

You don't want to pay 1500+ for a sound bar that has "virtual" Surround Sound and Atmos for your apartment.

You want something elegantly designed and discrete that doesn’t take a lot of space.

**Who shouldn't get this system:**

People with large spaces, specifically large dens or living rooms in a house where you need to cover a lot of space.

If you want full-range sound from your fronts. Small satellites will never give that to you, just a fact.

You want beefy big speakers. These are discrete and small.

Atmos Out of the box (you can add heights or Atmos enabled speakers later if you want and if you have an Atmos friendly AVR). You can even use these satellites for Atmos height speakers if you really wanted to.

You want really articulate bass that goes really, really deep. You'll need to shell out minimum $200 just for the Sub to get that.

**Bottom Line**

Time will tell how long these last and other factors, but out of the box, hooked up and tweaked to the right settings they sound amazing and exactly fit my needs.

Just understand that you are not going to get full-range sound from the satellites (you will with the whole system combined and optimized for your room). If that's what you're looking for then you simply need bigger speakers with a larger frequency range. At that point your fronts ALONE without a center channel will cost as much as this system (at the current price of $139).

If you want a compact and amazing sounding 5.1 surround system at a great price point, grab these when they’re under $200.

I've had a lot of trouble trying to find a headset that provides a good experience with my GXV3240, but this unit seems to have finally met the need. The biggest trouble I had with cheaper models was people complaining about me being too quiet or sounding strange, but with this model I haven't heard any complaints yet. It pairs just fine with my GXV3240, though to get it to work I had to disable handsfree mode, which was counter-intuitive. One thing that is very convenient is if you have it off your head, and you hear the phone ringing, the headset will sense somehow when you put it back on it and answer the call without you having to press the button. So I just leave it laying on the desk when I'm not on a call.

The only caveat is the GXV3240 driver only has partial support with this model, so that I can only use it receive calls, not to place them. So if I really want to use this for an outgoing call, rather than the handset, I have to call my customer on another company line, and transfer the call back to my SIP phone. But at my job about 95% of my calls are incoming, so it isn't much of an issue.

I haven't tried the ANC functionality yet, so I can't comment on that.
title: Having a good experience with my Grandstream SIP phone: one caveat

The completely wireless experience is liberating, especially when lying down or sitting in an over-sized chair reading.

So I'll be keeping them. I still can't get over the quality for the money. A very nice product!

text:
This H80i was my first foray into Corsair AIO's. I have a Ryzen 2600x in a small, "hot" case that would only allow a single radiator. Up until now the H80i has been "adaquate" but with no margin for handling any overclocking. This computer is a backup system and not actually on that often. Last week I turned it on and all fans came on full-blast and the CPU temp was hitting 108c+. I took the system apart, and installed the basic air cooler that comes from AMD with the 2600x. Temps with the air-cooler are back to "normal" (although I doubt it will have more "headroom" than a good AIO unit). Testing the H80i I could not hear any pump noise, so assume the pump had died. At least it died without leaking coolent. So far, Corsairs "RMA under Warranty" process has has not produced any non-automated response - time will tell. Pitty the person that has to unbuild and then rebuild their computer and not have a spare cooler: at this rate, if they actually respond, it would take a month (week to respond, the rest for shipping to/from, etc) for Corsair to replace the H80i (TBD). I have a Fractal Design AIO in another system that runs nearly 24/7 since July 2017 and has had no problems.

So, not impressed with the longevity of this H80i/pump and definitely would go with another brand in the future. On the plus side, it did not live long enough to leak.

[Update] Corsair received the unit on the 8th of January (2020). It is now nearly a MONTH later (Feb. 4) and I still do not even have an acknowledgment of shipment of a replacement, let alone an actually working unit in hand.
title: Pump died after 15 months...

text:
So my father lives in a literal log house with knotty pine walls and an addition that is the master bedroom. For those that don't know, wood is an amazing RF insulator, and once grounded it absolutely eats WiFi. These routers can blast through the knotty pine and hollow wooden doors no problem. Nothing makes it through the exterior walls though, so I had to place one node about 20 feet from the base where I still had line of sight with the base. Two of these were enough to cover his house. The third node will be used to get WiFi to the detached garage.

The power, speed, and performance of this system is great. I could not be happier with the system once it is set up.

I docked a star for the requirement of a mobile device, and the fact Linksys tries to keep users out of the web interface.
I should be able to use ethernet connections to configure a hub router and satellites, or log into each router independently and configure them for mesh much like how AI Mesh works.

For those wondering, navigate to your router, when you get the page that tells you to install the app, click the Velop symbol and log in.

This is the only tri-band mesh in a box system, at least as of the time I bought it, and I am very pleased with the performance.

text:
I purchased four "Echo show 5" units. One was for my personal use and the other three I gifted them to family members. The echo show 5 works great. It is user friendly and provides easy to follow instructions to connect it to the internet.
I am assuming that the developers' intentions were to use it as an entertainment piece. As such it works perfect. However reading about its features, I decided that I could use it as a tool to help aging family members.
The two units were used in the US to communicate with an elderly family member who is located about 65 miles away. She is using it as a clock (an expensive clock). Also, in the event that she needs assistance to contact a family member by asking Alexa to dial the family member's phone number.
We practiced a few times, so I hope that if it is needed, she will be able to use it.
The other two units were taken overseas with the hope that they could be used in a similar manner. Before I purchased the units I did not research the languages that the software is able to speak. When I was setting mine up, I scrolled through the language features and realized that Greek was not one of them. So, I set it up for English. The family member in the US speaks broken English so she can use it. The other family members in Greece speeks fluent English but the elder parent speaks no English.
Again, no complaints because the unit is not advertised as a medical allert aid or a product to be used for elderly people as a means of comunication. Although it has enough features that the developers could ensure that the software could be utilized for elderly or disabled individuals.
In case anyone is interested the Echo products in general do work great in Greece. You can get information about the local weather, the time and other local and international features in the same manner as if you were to use it in the United States.
I have not been able to set it up to use the "drop in" feature or the feature to call land lines or cell phones.
I hope that other developers look at the Echo Show 5 product and get inspired to develop a product that can be utilized by the elderly and disable populations.
title: Useful for entertainment

If i disconnect, she can reset it to work for her, but that's work we dont want to have to do everytime we get in and out of the car. We would be switching a few times everyday! Supposedly, theres a way to make this work through managing your household settings, but we both have student prime accounts so we cant add each other to our households and share any devices. So this is only great for someone who does not share their car. Secondly, it does take 30 seconds or so to connect to my phone and start working smoothly. It isnt a long time, but its annoying everytime i get in the car and ask for a song it tells me to wait. Lastly, its kind of bulky and annoying. The wires have a tendency to be annoyingly in my way, no matter how i cinch them. Amazon engineers do indeed try to curb this problem by including several sliders that keep the wires together and a place on the mount where the wires can be fed through, but it isnt quite enough to alleviate the problem. These few things aside, the echo auto is amazing. Its just as quick and effective as my home echos. Also, it allows me to control things in my home and use the intercom and announcement features while out on the go. I could feasibly do all these things with my phone, but not with my voice and certainly not while driving. If you can overlook the issues I listed above, this product will satisfy your smart car desires.

text:
Topline: Great room filling sound, but to avoid distortion and dropped connections, you have to use ethernet cables on every device in your console to avoid interference--to which the soundbar is obscenely susceptible. Out of box and with a bunch of wireless components nearby, you'll be banging your head against a wall. The sound quality *is* fantastic, but the documentation is either wrong, misleading, or incomplete. (I recommend you look at the manuals available on the website to see what I mean.) Additionally, the Vizio SmartCast app is incredibly finicky, particularly when it comes to recognizing your device. Which wouldn't be a problem if it weren't for the fact that the Vizio remotes are just difficult to use (why don't they backlight the VERY DARK, VERY SMALL LCD screen on them?). Finally, the Subwoofer is huge. HUGE. Doublecheck its measurements to make sure you can accommodate it in your space. (And make sure you have a power outlet near your couch.)

INTERFERENCE/SURROUND DISTORTED/DROPPED:

The problem with the SB46514-F6 is that the signal it sends to the subwoofer is prone to interference. I know this because it was plagued with "popping" distortion, disappearing voices, and dropped surround. Attempting to reproduce the effect was hit-or-miss. Sometimes I just needed to return to a menu and then re-start a video. Sometimes I needed to re-pair the subwoofer (a ridiculously laborious process). But the repair wouldn't last: Soon, the popping and dropping resurfaced.

On one forum, a user mentioned marginal improvement by *turning the subwoofer around* so its rear faced the soundbar (and away from the power strip it was close to). I tried it, and indeed, the sound cut out less frequently--it seems the receiving circuitry on the subwoofer is in the back.

So, I deactivated the wireless on pretty much all of my peripherals. I wired all the connections in the media console--from my TV, to my PS4, to my AppleTV--and deactivated all wifi components except the router. With that, I achieved seamless, uninterrupted surround sound.

I won't attempt a teardown of the soundbar to get into the details, but my theory is that the soundbar concentrates its antennae all together on the left side, away from the power supply to avoid electrical interference. But it has several antennae for a few purposes. You're bound to get interference. It appears to have Bluetooth, some variety of NFC antenna, a wifi antenna, and another radio antenna that carries the signal to the subwoofer. That's four, in one small enclosure. If it's under your wifi activated tv, and near your wifi activated (and bluetooth remote-controlled) apple tv, and all by your router, that's just a lot of potential for interference.

DOCUMENTATION:

The quick start guide is a decent walkthrough, and the manual has some useful tips, but the language is ambiguous about whether you can get ATMOS sound from any device routed through your TV, or if it needs to be plugged directly into your soundbar's ARC HDMI port. (My understanding: You need to be plugged directly into the ARC HDMI port, and it may work with a hub that passes 4k through as well.) Does HDMI-CEC need to be on? Yes! Kind of. But additional documentation is maddeningly hard to find: The distortion issue seems to be a crisis for Vizio, to the point they've attempted to roll out new firmware (enjoy updating it using the SmartCast app, which is awful in this venture). But nowhere do they acknowledge the reality of interference.

REMOTE:

Hard to see. No backlight. Dark screen.

SMARTCAST APP:

Takes a number of different approaches to identifying your soundbar, insists on putting your soundbar on wifi at first, requires you to place your phone on it for some reason, sometimes doesn't detect it, and once set up, doesn't detect the soundbar in subsequent uses. (Even after deleting and going through the process again.) Its most consistent reliability comes when the soundbar is hardwired into the router. Additionally, if you want to check settings, it *still* requires you to request them through the app, and then the speaker... says them to you. Out loud.

SOUND:

It's great. Really and truly: If you can get it to work properly, you'll love it, and your neighbors will hate you. My only complaint sound wise is that the sound doesn't seem to go very low before totally cutting out.
title: Surround Sound is Inconsistent: Here's How to Fix It

text: I purchased this product Sept. 2, 2018. After less than a year, flickering horizontal lines appeared on the screen. I sent it in to Amazon for repairs in June, 2019 and received it back within a week or so supposedly ‘fixed’. Less than 2 months later the flickering horizontal lines returned and to add to that annoying problem, the speaker quality began to fail. The speaker would sporadically crackle and/or skip (similar to playing a scratched record for those of you old enough to remember that sound) typically when playing music. I debated whether or not to send it in to be fixed and figured it wasn’t worth the trouble. I checked into the trade-in program and the most I’d get for it was $30, which was too ridiculous for me to bother with. I bought the Echo Show 2nd generation in a fit of insanity and returned it without even opening the box. I didn’t want to become disillusioned as I did with the ‘old’ Echo Show. The newest thing Alexa has decided to do is NOT respond to some commands. She lights up like she’s listening, but does not always obey simple commands such as “Alexa, pause music...skip song...stop...” etc. Yes, I rebooted, reset, checked wi-fi, all the things Amazon support tells you to do. text:
These are by far the best sounding true wireless earbuds I’ve ever owned. I have purchased at least 10 different sets to try within the past year. I even owned the first set of Tranya T1 when it first came out and I was impressed by the sound of those as well. However the battery life were just too short so I would have to have 2 sets of ear buds so that I could have continuous music during my travels. Well Tranya has improved hugely in that department with the their latest T3. I can say with confidence these lasted just about 6 hours because that’s how long my flight was from Nashville to San Jose before the battery died. The bass is deep and responsive and tremble is very clear. Also these don’t stick out as far as the T1 which makes it more aesthetically pleasing. The only negative thing I’ve experienced with the T3s is that occasionally the right and left do not sync with each other. So I’ve had to reset them several times. And I don’t always carry my little charging module with me when I’m working out or going shopping or eating. I never experienced this with the T1s. Perhaps I received a defective set. I’ve contacted Tranya regarding this issue so maybe they’ll send me a new set. I’ll keep you updated. Besides that you can’t beat these ear buds especially for under $50. Apple EarPods don’t even come close to these in sound quality and noise cancellation.

Pros:
Great Bass and Treble response
Very crisp and clear sound
Good noise cancellation
Long lasting 6 hrs battery life

Cons:
Trouble syncing to each other (left and right) on occasion
title: Best sounding ear buds with great battery life

Checked here and there, and found the solution (unfortunately not here), and sharing it with you as a New Year Gift ( if you decide to buy me a beer, I would accept :) )
So the solution of low sound coming form your new surround speakers is to install on your phones a Bose Mobile app.
There are few. "Bose Connect" and "Bose Music" will not work with soundbar 300, they do with 500/700.
For soundbar 300 model you need "Bose SoundTouch" app. It works using your home Wi-Fi to connect your phone/app with the soundbar. To prepare your soundbar for connection, press your soundtouch button on your remote, then press and hold 9.
Open the app and follow instructions. It will also check for updates ( I even didn't know this sound system could get updates, so did it for a first time in 2 years since I bought it. Update took a while, about 15 minutes).
When you are connected, on app under settings you could find "Audio Settings". There you can adjust the Central Level and your Surround Level, last one is what is bothering you, hit it to 10 :) Test your sound now.

text: I have a 7.1 system with 16 gauge wire running to all 7 of my speakers. The way these plugs clamp down on the bare wire requires fanning out the wire and then screwing the plug together. The problem is that 16 gauge wire and most certainly anything smaller than 16 gauge wire pulls right out of the plug after it's screwed together, there's just not enough thickness where the teeth of the plug clamp down on the wire. I overcame this by twisting the wire end like you normally would to put it into a binding post style connector, and just bending it over like that inside the banana plug. It still doesn't feel like a great connection, but it doesn't easily pull out, although it will with a moderate force tug. If you're using 14 gauge or larger wire I would buy these without hesitation, because them seem well made.
title: Best For 14 gauge Or Larger Wire. Stay Away For Smaller Wire.

I love the look and I was very impressed with the quality of this 4-in-1 hub. I can tell it will last a long time. This is great product at an amazing price it was money well spent.

I found out that I can run a desktop environment called Dex with my Samsung Galaxy 8 all that's needed was an adapter. So I bought this QGeeM USB C Hub 4-in-1 USB Adapter. This 4-in-1 configuration is perfect. I can plug a monitor or my 4k TV into the HDMI port. I use my mouse/keyboard USB dongle in the 2.0 port and a fast 3.0 256 GB flash Drive in the USB 3.0 port. Then I can keep my phone charging while I'm using Dex with this hub plugged in by plugging my charger into the Hubs USB-C port.

Now I can use my phone as a desktop computer which ends up being about the same thing as chromebook but better because now I can carry on my work with the computer in my pocket. The QGeeM USB C Hub 4-in-1 USB Adapter is small enough to comfortably fit in in my pocket with my phone and makes it easier than ever to have a computer on the go.

It doesn't lag and transfers amazing quality and the data throughput is phenomenal. I am 100% satisfied and I highly recommend this to anyone who is looking to use the Dex Desktop environment on their Samsung Galaxy phone.

I also recently got a laptop with a USB-C port and learned all what it can do and used this QGeeM USB C Hub 4-in-1 USB Adapter to try it out. On my PC it's great for doing USB-C to HDMI for a 2nd or 3rd Screen off my laptop beyond the HDMI and Display ports. I can leave my mouse/keyboard USB dongle in the 2.0 port and a flash Drive in the USB 3.0 port plugged into the adapter and leave it connected to my monitors HDMI cable to easily plug in and set up when setting up my laptop. This is great since I take my computer back and forth from my office and my home office I can just use this QGeeM USB C Hub and connect everything with just one plug in.

If you have a Dex capable phone or a USB-C port on your computer and want to try or take advantage of the USB-C port's features I highly recommend this Adapter as it is great quality affordable and has multiple use cases.

Hey Everyone and welcome back, and today we are reviewing the light that I have been using in past 3-4 recent videos, it’s full color RGB light panel and it also comes with many functions, we’ll see that as well and then we’ll see the use of it with different setup, lot to cover so let’s jump right into it.

INSIDE THE BOX
Ok, so first starting with package content, this light costs $63 and they also include one sony NP-F 550 style of battery, that is is smallest version of all and they also include NP-F Charger as well. And in the main box, it comes with LCD Panel itself and a small pouch and a small user manual if you need one. Next side we see a cold shoe mount that goes below light if you want to attach it straight on top of your camera. I am not a fan of keeping light on top of the camera and this mount is also made out of plastic and not of a good quality so I would rather use my own quarter inch adapter if I really have to use it on top of my camera.

CONSTRUCTION
As far as the construction of the light, it is completely made out of plastic on both sides accept the quarter inch screw in the bottom, and in the front we also have diffusion cover which is non-removable and on the back we have couple of keys and one knob to control and change the functions of the light. On the top we also have a small color LCD screen to see different modes and brightness and other stuff which we’ll talk next.

SEE DIFFERENT FUNCTIONS
Ok, so even though it’s a small panel, it does feature a lot of features. And before we jump into that, let’s take a minute to see the frontside panel of this LED. So basically, it has 5 types of different types LED lights, first is for bi-color regular LED use, so since this LED can also do different temperatures from 2500K To 8400K, there are led lights for each on the side, one warm and one cooler tone and then it mixes up together to give you a certain color. And then it also has 3 other pairs of light around and those are Red Green and BLUE and by combining all them together it will give you a any color you want.

Ok, so let’s see different modes of the light becuase as I said it has a lot of them, So first you turn on the panel with this on-off button and then let me clear out this key on the right side because it is pretty simple. So this key is basically for the adjustment on this knob, and it has two different modes, so if you put it into fine mode, it will gradually changes the settings with one percent at a time, So let’s say if I am changing the brightness then with each one click on this circles it will increase one percent, while if you put it on coarse mode then it will increase with 5% markup each time, so may be with just a quarter of a wheel circle from 1 to 100. And this will again apply to all the uses in different mode.

Ok, So let’s talk about modes now. There are four different main modes and that is CCT, HSI, RGB & different scenes. Let’s look et each one of them starting with CCT, correlated color temperature I believe, its pretty simple if you used any bi-color led panel before. So, once you are in this mode, you use use this wheel to change the brightness first and then if you click on it, you will see this arrow going to color temperature now which let’s you choose color temperature of your choice using this wheels. As I said earlier it goes from 2500K, 8500K by mixing two types of LED’s and you probably have figured out but the maximum brightness you will get is around 5600K which is good because it’s a daylight temperature.

Moving to the next mode is HSI, in this we have three different option, first one is the hue of your light which has value of 8 to 1518. The light also has a scale here on the back, so you can go near to the point of whichever color you want to select, next we have a brightness and the last one is the saturation. So let’s say if I want a magenta light, on the scale it is somewhere around 255, let’s keep the brightness to __ level and if I now start increasing my saturation, there you go we have a pink/magent color light. Its a little bit tricky though because if you see if I go below this level on saturation, it turns to cyan or little bluish so you’ll have to mix in between hue and saturation to get a color you want.

Next, let’s go to the other mode that is RGB, this mode let’s you color mix in between three colors of led lights, so let’s say if I go to red, it will simply increase the brightness of red lights. Same with green and then blue. What’s interesting in the same mode, you can also mix and match different colors if you know the mixtures, so let’s say if I know I can get cyan by mixing Green and blue, I can do that and get different shades and mixtures of them by going with different intensity, which is very handy and useful and little bit accurate to get compared to HSI mode.

And finally let’s come to the last mode, where it get most intersting is different modes. It has 10 different modes and you can change that by pressing this button and then yuo can simply increase the brightness. There aree couple of modes for lightning effect, one is for cinema or tv watching, police, ambulance, fire truck, and then couple of modes for changing RGB lights, SOS and lastly Candle light effect.

I bought this watch after owning a Vivomove HR for quite sometime until it the screen finally gave up the ghost on me. I bought this device obviously because it was newer so of course newer should be better. So far I've notice this watch is almost basically the same as the HR only difference now is the Pulse Ox which to be honest I think I'm better off without. My issue with Pulse Ox is battery life hit you take from 4 days down to about 3 days. I finally just disable the pulse ox so I will see what my battery life is looking like without it. Bigggggg issue for me right there because wasnt expecting it to have such an impact but in all fairness they did state it would decrease the battery life and I overlooked it. The older premium HR sells for $249 with basically the same features (I remember how bad I wanted the silver one too) The Amoled screen looks nice and is a wonderful improvement and the touchscreen works much better on this device as well. Definitely not liking the white tips on the clock hands, throws off the looks of the device.

But overall I think the device is pretty much overpriced especially the LUXE versions I mean for $499 and this device STILL doesn't track naps. Like come on Garmin this is very infuriating. I'm not sure yet but I am thinking about sending this watch back to get the older Premium HR and save myself a couple bucks, I don't need Pulse Ox.

Update: So after turning off the pulse ox I was able to get 4 days of battery life which is still less than the 5 days j was getting with the HR. I've since returned this device and purchased a Premium Vivomove HR along with a replacement band and extra charger and still cost less than this device. By about 90 bucks.

Pros:
-Touch screen has improved over previous version
-Amoled screen looks great and blends right in
-Once again very light, a plus for me.
-Pulse Ox is a good addition despite battery hit
-Very good app.

Cons:
-Doesn't track naps to add to sleep data
-The black style doesn't look like a premium device, looks more like a plastic dark grey.
-Battery life is worst than the previous version
-Price is too high

text: Bought 3 of these monitor arms to set up three 34" curved screen monitors for my son's gaming desk. The specs say they will handle from 4.4 to 33 lbs., but after handling and assembling these, I am convinced that they would handle 50 lbs. or more. These things are super quality and built like a tank. Nothing in the operating mechanism is left to chance - nothing but beautifully designed and heavy duty. The 34" Alienware monitors are about 16 lbs. each, so they are nothing for these arms to handle. I wound up having to completely bottom out the tension adjustment on them and then come back in 5 turns to get them just right. Now they float effortlessly and will assume most any angle or height - perfect! The ONLY complaint I have is the same as some of the other reviewers have noted and that's the wire cover on the lower part of the arms. After routing the wires, they simply click back in place via some small tabs at the bottom. Trouble is, these tabs are very thin and extended and will pop loose at the slightest pressure from the wires underneath that they are hiding. Two of the arms seem to have better tabs on the covers and have stayed in place, but one of them simply will not stay clicked in. I'm going to see if they will send me a couple of these covers to replace the bad one and to have a spare. Not a huge thing, but just an annoying little detail that detracts from an otherwise stellar product. I would absolutely, without hesitation, recommend these to anybody wanting a really heavy duty arm to suspend a larger monitor. The fit and finish is fabulous and they look awesome holding his 3 monitors either lined up or all over the place! It's hard to believe that they can sell this level of quality, design and function at this price. I would imagine that there are many other arms out there that are double or triple the price of these that wouldn't even be in the neighborhood of the same ballpark. Aside for the one cover, I couldn't be more pleased with this choice! They are 110% A+++ accessory components and I would buy them again with no reservation...

I got two of this for my wife's and my dash cam. It comes with the add-a-circuit kit and you don't need to buy anything else to hardwire your dash cam.

Recommended tools: plier, clean cloth, multi-meter, electrical tape

Workflow:

1. Check the fuse box, and figure out which fuse is hot (feeds power even when the engine is turned off) by using the multimeter.

2. Attach the black wire to the metal chassis first, secure it.

3. Attach the red wire to the always-hot fuse with the add-a-circuit one.

4. Plug the USB to your dash cam to make sure you get the power when the engine is off.

That's it. I managed to install the setup within 30 minutes the first car then 15 minutes the second one. I highly recommend this kit to everyone. :)

text: If you like Alexa automation and want something a bit more affordable to use with your own speaker system, this may be a good option.  But this is only as good as what you connect it to.  That being said, I have it connected to my Sony HT-NT5 sound-bar system with subwoofer which is a good sounding system, not an audiophile’s first choice but nonetheless a decent system.  I connected the Echo Link to the sound bar via an optical audio cable and turned the Echo Link volume all the way up.  I was not expecting anything great but what I get is really good.  Clear Hi-Fi audio with no distortion.  Much much better than what comes out of any Echo speaker or connecting an Echo speaker to external sound system via 3.5mm cable.  I control the volume through my sound-bar remote.  Or you can use Alexa for that too but she can only get the volume as high as what the sound-bar is set to.  So I tell my Alexa Echo-Dot to play Beats 1 on Apple music and she sends the music to the Link.  All I have to do is make sure my sound-bar is on and select the correct input.  I was skeptical at first because of some not-so-good reviews but I'm quite satisfied with the Link.  I’m sure there are much better high-end options and if I have it connected to a super high end system, the quality will be better.  Just don't think you're going to get great sounding audiophile standard Hi-Fi music with this Link especially if you connect it to a subpar speaker system.

This is my third Ryzen processor, I also have systems with the 2700x and 3900x. I picked this processor up at a great price on a Black Friday.

With a decent cooler this processor has never gone over 60 Celsius which was a pleasant surprise and that’s with the standard fan curve, not set to 100%.

As expected the processor performs well and is fast, especially as for the system this is in I’m running Linux. Not that it wouldn’t be fast with Windows, my other systems run Windows for gaming.

text:
My mom is pretty hard to buy for. But this last time I visited I knew this might be a great gift. Everytime I visit her we watch a little tv and the volume is always going up and down to accommodate her aging ears. I wasn't sure if it was a gimmick or not - but they have a 30 day return so I thought I'd give it a go. This was replacing an LG soundbar that didn't solve the her hearing issue. Setting it up was pretty easy - there is unfortunately no HDMI, I knew that before buying however. Once it was set up I could tell the difference instantly, the voices were much clearer and this was on the lowest boost (AC1) - My mom asked me what I thought and I stressed to her what matters is what she thinks. I was able to stay for a couple days after setting it up. We pretty quickly bumped it to AC2, and turned on the sound leveling. Right now it's on AC3. I don't know any other way to say this... each increase of the AC level makes it sound less hi-hi / theater like to my ears but again, that's not the point.

The first evening with AC set to one, Sound leveling Off, and Surround set to 1 (we never changed the surround level), We barely touched the volume, but she did mention how some things were loud - So I turned on the sound leveling, which definitely impacts the 'theater quality' and bumped the AC to level 2. My Brother came over and he too immediately noticed the difference, commenting that is sounded clear and much better than the old sound bar. Yet there where still a few times we played with the volume so I bumped the AC to level 3. and this is where it was when I left. This soundbar has 6 levels for accuvoice, Zvox makes soundbars with just AC on or off... I wonder what level the is equivalent to? In the end we watched TV with the sound on '11' which was *maybe* one level higher than I would have listened, certainly not as loud as my Mom used to listen at, and with her hearing more of the content.

The remote was quite a bit nicer than I expected, but Mom won't be needing it as the soundbar can learn your TVs Power, Volume up, Volume down, and Mute and respond to them. This is one spot where the documentation fails slightly - For one thing the directions for setting this up are not included I had to download them... Oh and a side note, they brag about the one page of directions - yes they are one page, one very large page printed on both sides and folded six times (yeah, marketing people) - Anyhow back to the programming the sound bar to respond to your TV - you need to download the directions from there website. and then the directions won't work, it simply will not enter 'learning' mode. Well the missing detail from the direction is the sound bar must be OFF at the beginning of the setup. It didn't take me long to figure that out, but it should have been clearly stated. (I did try it a few times using first the remote then the physical buttons before discovering it needed to be OFF first - at which point the remote or the physical buttons worked)

So in short - super happy - it sounds great, it does sound better with the AC lower and the sound leveling off, but it still sounds great as i configured it for my mom - and that was the whole point. Does my mom hear every word now? no - But we can watch tv quieter than we used to, and we adjust the volume significantly less then before (like 90% less)

We are thinking of getting this sound bar for my mother-in-law as well. And I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it for anyone that is looking at getting a sound bar in general. Personally, I have a Marantz AV receiver and lots of speakers - but for a sound bar this thing sounds great - and better than the $150ish sound bar we got from the big box store.

BTW I purchased https://www.amazon.com/dp/B01DW1XOCY/ref=cm_sw_r_tw_dp_U_x_F84cEb6F6FJF8 to mount it under my moms TV
title: Bought for my Mom

The only drawback for me is I found it tricky at times to tell if it was actually recording or not. While I did get the hang of it, there were times I wasn’t sure it was actually recording until I removed the memory card and was able to confirm whether or not that was the case.
title: Overall good cam

text:
This is a great body cam. I had bought 2 previous ones from other companies, but while sufficient for certain purposes, I right away realized they fell short in other crucial areas. Most importantly to me, the pros to this one is the lengthy battery life, night vision/IR, motion stability, loop recording, easy to tell if it’s actually recording, ability to set date/time on the cam itself without having to go thru a USB cord to a computer, and a screen to view the footage without having to put the memory card in a computer or device to view it.

However, the downsides which prevent this from being perfect/5* for me are these: mostly the fact that the clip/s, even the large sturdy one, isn’t sufficient in length and heft to enable the cam to remain in the right position/angle, as the weight of the cam pulls the clip down and I’m left with footage facing towards the ground/floor, and not at the higher level I need it to catch (a solution is to clip it horizontally where it stays out much better, only issue is the footage is now in portrait and not landscape). Other lesser cons are the clip/s lack the ability to rotate, the product pic does indicate otherwise but such is not the case, at least with the clips packaged with my cam. Also, the date/time is so tiny as to be unreadable when viewing footage on the cam, so when there’s a part I want to review, I’m unable to just skip to the time it happened and instead have to FF until I see it. Lastly, while it’s good that the clip stays firmly and securely in place, it’s a nightmare to remove!

Despite these issues, overall this is a great cam and I don’t feel the need to look further for another one. Do wish tho that there was the option of ordering replacement clips, just in case it should get damaged or accidentally misplaced.
title: Almost perfect, but not quite

text:
This is my first smart watch so I have nothing to compare it to. It tracks time...duh... So did my dumb watches.

Plays music that's stored in the watch, about 10 songs which were easy to load.
You can add pictures of the family as well.

Multiple watch faces to suit my every changing moods. I went crazy for about a month downloading and buying new watch faces only to settle on about 3 I use most of the time.

Sleep feature of my Fitbit is what made me look into a smart watch. This is better than Fitbit as there's no need to download to an app then open. I can do that if I want the data saved but it's accessible from the watch itself.

Heart rate in real time is great, I use it often and almost every day.
Like a Fitbit this thing is tracking everything I do including steps I take, lowest and highesr HR and average, and also activity logs... There's a lot it does.

The Watch.
Features state it still works and is worn like a watch, so if you use sleep mode and alarm it starts to make make on your wrist. Best to alternate wrists as you go along.

Clean the watch face as you would a phone face, it gets dirty.

Clean the HR monitor in the back of the watch as it gets dirty she interested with the watched shiny to track your HR.

Clean the inside of the straps with warm soapy water.

Clean the whole watch in warm soapy water, you won't kill it.

After 6 to 7 months I thought it broke as the face became very hard to turn. This is normal, to fix it run some very warm water and hold the watch under it while turning the bezel. You'll feel the grit start to go away and the bezel goes back to being easy to turn.

** Make sure you know what cell provider the phone is coded to if you intend to use it as a stand alone phone. I didn't check and got a Verizon coded phone though I'm on T mobile. So I can't use it as a stand alone phone.
However, connected to the phone via BT I can get messages and phonee calls through the watch. Range is about 15 feet so your sort of tethered to the phone. No big deal, I don't want to have a conversation on speakerphone in public anyway.

That's it. Coming up on a year and there's really nothing that's gone wrong.
Samsung's got the lockdown on my TV, Note 9 and Gear smart watch. If these guys ever decide to make cars, Honda is screwed... Lol

text:
For those using this MC7455 card in a Mini-PCIe to USB adapter, if you have issues with it passing data reliably, this information is for you.

* This MC7455 card can operate in two different interface modes: QMI or MBIM
* The card ships by default from SierraWireless in QMI mode, but most OS's ( Windows and Linux confirmed ) work much better with MBIM mode.
* While in QMI mode, I was able to establish a network connection, but outbound traffic basically didn't work for anything more than 'ping'.

To overcome this, you need to connect to the Modem's COM port for AT commands. Note that there are multiple COM ports assigned to the card, only one will work for AT commands. This is typically the highest COM port number which is associated with the card. You can find the right COM port by trial and error.. it won't hurt anything if you hit the wrong one.

NOTE: Proceeding below uses administrative config functions, which if not set properly can render the card useless. While I have completed this successfully on two cards and have not had any issues, proceed at your own risk.

In Windows, I recommend downloading 'putty'. When you run it, select 'Serial' under 'Connection type:', then change the 'Serial line' parameter to COM# (where # is the COM port you want to test), then leave the 'Speed' value set to 9600 and click 'Open'

In Linux, install 'screen', then use the command as follows:
# mmcli -m 0| grep ports
-- Look for the 'ttyUSB#' port associated with (at)
# screen /dev/ttyUSB2 9600
-- Note that 'ttyUSB2' is the port assigned to the (at) command interface.

Once connected to the port, you can proceed as follows:
1: Type the following command and press Enter (you will not see the letters as you type them):
ate1
- This turns on 'echo', meaning after this line is entered, you will see the keys you type as you type them.

2: Type the following and press Enter:
ati
- This should show the model, firmware and other details for the modem.

3: Type the following and press Enter:
at!entercnd="A710"
- This enabled administration configuration commands

4: Type the following and press Enter:
at!usbcomp=1,1,1009
- This changes the modem to MBIM mode

5: Type the following and press Enter:
at!reset
- This resets the modem so it will reboot into MBIM mode

At this point, if using putty, it will likely complain of a disconnection and close out. If using 'screen' in Linux, press:
Ctrl-a followed by k, then answer 'Yes' to kill this window.

Once the modem finishes its restart, you should be able to fully utilize the MC7455 for a solid, stable and FAST internet connection ( all other conditions being favorable, of course ).
title: Works great after changing modes to MBIM

text:
I recently "cut the cord" on my satellite TV service. My old satellite receiver had an optical Dolby 5.1 output, which I connected to my sound system amplifier. My amp is an older model, and doesn't have an HDMI input. I am now using an Amazon 4K FireTV Stick, so I needed an audio extractor to get the audio signal out from the Firestick, to my amp.

I found that this little unit works well for my application. Since this unit does not support Dolby Digital Plus (nor does my amp), I had to change the audio setting in the Firestick to "Always Dolby Digital", instead of "always Dolby Digital Plus". This works great, and now my amp always receives a Dolby 5.1 signal, regardless of the source encoding. The amp will downconvert to stereo if the source encoding is not Dolby Digital. The Dolby 5.1 sound quality is good.

My only complaint is that I wish it had a memory for the settings. If I enable ARC, and then power down the unit, it does not maintain the previous setting when powered up again.

text:
As soon as I inserted it into my Switch and turned it on, the Switch was non-responsive. I had done a system update prior to doing this, so my Switch was set up for using micro SD cards - no issue there. The screen stayed black and I had to do a hard reboot of it to make it cut back off. I let it sit for a while thinking it was just a coincidence, then I turned it back on and got the same thing. I turned it off again, took the card out, then turned it back on and luckily it still works. It DID, however, erase my saves during this ordeal. Luckily I have cloud saves enabled and was able to restore my save state.

I had done some research on this item prior to purchasing it for my Switch, and it seems to have some solid reviews. Having said that, the product that I personally received straight from Amazon seems to be a cheap knock-off of the real thing. Before today, I didn't know that "fake" SD cards were a thing.

The packaging seemed a bit "off" when it arrived in the mail. The front and back of the cardboard packaging was not lined up (pictured), and the imprints of the company logo are not lined up with the ink on the actual packaging. Looking at the plastic shell that it's in, you can tell that it wasn't pressed in a factory like other SD card holders. The last indicator, one that I didn't get a picture of before I opened it, was that the area over the SD card adaptor was "bulged out" and the lining around it was crinkled. You can still kind of tell from the fourth picture I included above - the top was like that before I opened it.

I reached out to Amazon customer service about the issue, but they did not assist me other than offering a refund without having to return the original item. Due to their response to my claim, I don't think they will be looking into this issue further and as a result, you run the risk of damaging your Switch or losing your save states by purchasing this item. I'm sure some of this product are the real deal, but obviously there are some fakes mixed in with their shipments. Very disappointing.

Update: Despite the agent I chatted with claiming he forwarded it to someone higher up and that they would be in touch with me to resolve the issue due to it almost bricking my system, no one ever contacted me. Do not trust a product because it is an "Amazon's Choice", and do not put your faith in their customer service. Product quality apparently doesn't matter to them.

text:
Looks like Amazon incorrectly labeled this item the 10920x which is only a 12 core cpu.

I managed to snag one off of Newegg. The 10980xe is an 18 core monster that is just a revision from the 7980xe and the 9980xe. This cpu still drops into x299 boards and behaves almost identically to the 7980xe and 9980xe with the exception of slightly higher stock clocks. The major selling point is the price with a massive 50% off of the original MSRP of the 9980xe.

The skylake-x mesh architecture suffers compared to coffeelake's(9900k) ringbus in gaming applications. You will actually lose performance in gaming compared to a 9900k. The 10980xe does bring more cores along with the features that come with the x299 platform making it a great workstation.

I consider the 18 core 10980xe a good core count in between the 12 from the 3900x and the 24 from threadripper 3. At the time of writing, I cannot consider the 3950x despite its incredible performance because of how unavailable they are. As of now, the 3950x is $999.99 on Newegg, $899 on B and H photo, $900-$1000 on ebay, and $929 from sellers on Amazon. Best Buy is the only one honoring the $749.00 MSRP...

The overclocking headroom on the 10980xe is incredible. With ambient water cooling(360 clc) I can hit 5ghz across all 18 cores. The heat is almost unmanageable at the moment for me so I will be looking into a custom loop in the future. As always with overclocking, your results may vary.

text:
These are very decent middle of the road kind of product, but suffer from some absoluty baffling design decisions. The comfort is fair. I can see out the bottom, so it doesn't block 100% light as it claims. But it blocks like 95% light. It cannot be worn too tightly either, as I found it really squeezes down on the nose / forehead if you tighten it, but it is indeed comfortable to wear on your side, or any position really.

The product info says these are machine washable, as long as you remove the electronics obviously. They are not, and this bold faced lie is why this product almost got 2 stars instead of 3. That right there is false advertising, folks. They may remove the picture after I leave this review, but it was there when I posted this. See my review pictures.

There is no noise cancelling for the headphones. Maybe they meant for the mic in call mode, but I took no calls on these, so I didn't rate it. But no these are just normal headphones and not noise cancelling. The sounds quality is surprisingly good honestly. Like some other reviewers, I use these for bedtime ASMR or moderation audio files, and they are quality enough to work for this purpose.

They posted over Bluetooth no problem at all, first time. However the operation of the device is where I have up nitpick. First of all, you should know that to skip a track you press forward or back and to adjust the volume, you hold forward or back. You read that right, and this is objectively wrong. Volume is something you want to adjust precisely, so a button push to lower or raise the volume 1 point would be the best implementation. Holding the buttons down should be for skipping tracks, as it's pretty clear when a new track is playing-- this does not require precision. It gets one star off for this insane control scheme.

And lastly, remember when I said that these are great for bedtime? That was a half-truth. When the headphones turn on, pair, unpair, or turn off, a super loud computer voice says "POWER ON," "PAIRING," "POWER OFF," etc. This is the second thing that someone must have been insane to implement considering this is a specialty product for sleep / nightime. If the unit shuts off while you are asleep, or loses it's Bluetooth connection, it will wake you up, so keep that in mind. There is no way to turn this voice off or make it quieter that I am aware of, it's not mentioned in the included instructions.

Only other weird thing is when it pairs, it always sets the the volume to a specific and pretty loud volume, but I couldn't tell if that was the player or the headphones. Pro-tip: adjust the playback volume on your device, not on these headphones awful control interface.

I like them enough to keep them, I'm not retuning mine and I use them still, but my advice is to search for a set without all of these horrible design oversights.

text:
This is the first WiFi Video Doorbell Camera I purchased for my home the past Christmas holiday. The instructions are easy to follow. The hardware installation went smoothly. The android app (I am using a Moto G5S Plus android phone) did not go well initially. It turned out that I had 2 issues on my part! The first one was that my old linksys WiFi router (WRT54G) was too far away from the doorbell. The 2nd one was that my old doorbell transformer was only 10V/5VA (this door bell camera requires 12~24V, 16VA transformer as labelled (see pictures attached)). After the two issues were corrected, the app ran smoothly. I was even able to update the firmware in a couple of minutes with the app. Over all, I am very happy with the purchase.

1. the product is small, feels solid, and looks nice at the door.

2. it is really smart to only identify moving human beings and dispatch alerts to the phone AND record the videos in the "history" which can be easily accessed from the app's UI.

3. The app UI is very simple and clean and functions well.

4. Night time, the camera will detect low light condition and turn on the infrared lights and the door bell camera becomes a night vision camera.

5. The mic can pick up human sound that maybe 100+ feet away. In fact, it can pick up anything I can hear from my porch my self (and maybe more). Similarly, the loud speaker can be heard 100+ feet away.

6. I can see and hear what's going on in front of my front door (~180 degrees left and right, up and down) any time and any where (with phone data connection of course) almost instantaneously (sounds almost no delay. picture frames about a fraction of a second).

7. By the way, the package came in with a couple of small hardware included. I now have one extra drill bit (for mason, it looks. I didn't have to use it since I have wood trim at my front door.).

As my name "picky" suggests, I am usually not an easy customer. After having used this product for 2 days, I was surprised at seeing how many smart and nice things this small door bell camera can do at my front door. It is a truly smart piece all around (even the "power kit").

text:
First off, the keyboard does feel really nice. I was looking for a backlit, low-travel chiclet keyboard to replace my Deathstalker (which is/was perfect for me outside of the fact that it would randomly repeat key presses upon restart), and this really fits the bill from a features perspective. Very comfortable to type on... only slightly less so than the Deathstalker. And the backlighting looks very nice when it works.

If you don't care about the backlighting, I highly recommend it. 5 stars.

But if, like me, you consider the backlighting one of the keys reasons you're buying this thing...

...why isn't this review 5 stars? All comes down to backlighting issues for me:
*Keyboard forgets my backlight settings regularly (defaults to off / no backlighting). Seems to mostly happen upon restarting my computer, though may also happen occasionally on long periods of inactivity. Absurd for a premium keyboard. -1 star.
*Backlighting sensors don't work at all when plugged in; it only comes on upon key press. Curious, since that would seem like a power-saving feature, except there's no need to save power when plugged in. No point deduction, but still odd/dumb.
*There's absolutely no way to customize how the lighting behaves. I would prefer to change the settings to leave it always on its dimmest level of backlighting, or at least extend the amount of time until it disables itself. -0.5 stars.
*There are multiple support threads on backlighting issues on Logitech's forums, and they don't particularly seem to care, or acknowledge the problems in any way. Support tickets don't get a response. -0.5 stars.
title: Good, comfortable keyboard with stupid backlighting issues Logitech refuses to acknowledge

text:
This is a great camera. I tried a few features and they have all worked fine for me.

Motion detection: The motion detection is pretty sensitive. Even when reducing the sensitivity threshold to a very low value, it picks up small things like rain, or moving plants with the wind. However, you can select a rectangular region of interest to trigger. I ended up making a very small region of interest in a small location where I'm guaranteed to have no swaying plants, and no rain dripping from rain gutters. I only wish we could create more than one region of interest for the motion detector for outdoor environments with lots of activity.

The saving to a local FTP server also works fine as well. I had to create a connection without a certificate (also make sure your firewalls will accept the traffic from this camera).

The email feature works fine. However, I noticed that when I click test, sometimes the software says the test failed, even though it actually succeeded (and I receive an email).

I like the alarm feature. It makes it very easy to review videos, if you set the motion detection right.

The video quality is decent. I can see what I need. You can select between two modes, SD and HD. I find that SD is generally enough for me.

I never use the pan tilt and zoom feature after setting it up. It is useful for setup, but if you have motion detection setup on a region of interest, you'll generally not want to move it. Still this is very useful to have.

There is one feature I have not tested yet. At some point, my SD card will run out of space. The camera should overwrite old videos. However, I have not run out of enough space to comment on that.

Overall, if you want an easy to setup camera that does not connect to any cloud services, this is a great camera. However, be prepare for some manual setup and tweaking.
title: Great non-cloud based camera

text:
Prerequisite: I daily drive Galaxy Buds, have tried Airpods, Airpods Pro and had a couple pairs of (2017) Anker SoundCore earbuds. I also use AKG K7XX's as my main over the ear headphones.

My review will focus mostly on sound quality, because build quality is just what you would expect from $50 earbuds: cheap plastics, but a solid build overall. Once they're in your ears, it doesn't make much of a difference.
They stick out of my ears more than I expected. The case is bigger than I expected, I'm not a fan of the shiny, fingerprint-magnet top of the case, and I would have preferred USB-C. But for $50 bucks, it's good enough, and NOT bad.

Now, the first and most important thing with sound quality: If you like the sound signature of Beats headphones, you'll love these.

They have INCREDIBLE fullness and reverberation to the bass. It seriously shocked me when I firs turned on a song. If you love bass, these are hands down the best value for money I've come across. They blow my Galaxy buds out of the water and Airpods/Pro don't come close, either. THAT SAID, the bass isn't incredibly detailed. It's definitely not muddy, but as I mentioned before, there's a lottt of reverberation. You can FEEL the bass. It was by FAR the main focus when the engineers designed these things. And unfortunately, I haven't found a way to tone it down. It's not my cup of tea, though if I were going for a run or working out, I MIGHT grab these over my Galaxy Buds, just for that extra pump.

That said, the mids are pretty dry. Listening to voices in podcasts or Youtube videos is actually great, but there's no dynamism to the mids. They're just there. Clean and clear on their own, but they easily get lost in the lows and highs when listening to music. But just voices alone, for podcasts, they're great, and you won't notice the lackluster mids in that case. With music, they definitely left me wanting for more.

On to the highs: I'm not a fan of sharp highs. Highs for me can easily be overdone and too sharp, and in this case, they are. They're very airy, a touch tinny, and pushed forward enough to the point where if I had an EQ I'd dial them down 3+dB. They're once again not very dynamic, very strong, and easily overpower the mids. They ARE somewhat detailed, but the tinny-ness and strong presence leave me really wishing I could use an EQ to drop them and raise the mids.

Overall, I'd give sound quality a C+

Soundstage is pretty wide for earbuds, and they're loud enough that I was afraid to turn them to max volume for fear of breaking my eardrums (lol).

The Airpods Pro are MUCH more dynamic, the Galaxy Buds are much more well rounded, and though lacking in bass, do a much better job in every other area. But they're anywhere from 2-5x as expensive.

Every video review I saw RAVED about these as the best earbuds under $100. And they MIGHT be right... But I'd be surprised.

In Conclusion:
I bought these for my wife, but I wish I would have jumped on the SoundCore Liberty Air 2's when they were $110 instead. I think SoundCore does a better job overall with balance and bass, and the pair I have only cost $26 almost 3 years ago, so I'm sure they've come a long way since then. I'd recommend checking out what they have in your price range over these, unless ALL you're after is MAD BUMPING bass.

This feature changed , it was previously available without subscription and I was never notified of the change. After a chat with support, I learned that without a Nest Aware subscription, I only have access to the last 3 hours of still images. That’s just not useful at all. The still images are blurry and sporadic. As a security measure, they’re useless.
