text:
Not sure how the hell Viltrox pulled this off, but they created a real gem with this lens. It's seemingly well made, being mostly metal (as far as I can tell) and quite substantial feeling. It's also quite heavy, but not enough to make an A7-series body feel unbalanced. AF is fast, generally quite accurate, and quiet. It does tend to hunt a bit in lower light situations, especially when stopped down a bit, but it's not a huge issue in most cases. Image quality is a lot better than I had expected, especially in terms of sharpness in the center of the frame. Wide open, it's acceptably sharp...but stopped down to f/2.8 it really gets super-sharp. Even f/2.2 is noticeably improved over f/1.8. Color rendition looks fine to me, but I don't pay a lot of attention to that sort of thing. Vignetting is noticeable up to about f/4 (or maybe 5.6), but it is not egregious and is easily corrected in post processing. Chromatic aberration is surprisingly well controlled, even at maximum aperture.

I bought this instead of the Sony 85mm, and I'm damn glad I did.
title: Amazing image quality at a stunning price point

text: I admit I like to play with audio gears... So I set up a pair of Yamaha NX-E100 for my desktop with a class D amp and a tube/valve buffer pre while I work for some good background music. I came across this and used my Amazon rebate.  It came this morning, so out the Yamaha (although they sound awfully good) under the desk and in the Covo.  I jury rigged a desktop stand/isolator with packaging materials and to my surprised, they were better than my Heos in mid.  The high roll off some but good enough and i will suggest to get a class D amp with a sub out and put a small sub under the table with crossover set at max.  Let's just say for the small package, I reclaimed my desktop and get some reasonable sound out of it.  For my application, it fits the bill.  I do think you need a small sub and a class D with sub out to add to it so instead of a 5, I give it a four. text: Bought these for my mom; she has a long driveway out in the country. When she is there by herself, she can't always tell when someone comes up to the house. We were thinking these might help in alerting her, giving her a heads up on visitors & deliveries. It did take some trial & error in finding the distance that we wanted them to be placed, but they work like a charm! There are different rings/chimes you can set for each sensor so you can tell how close a car is from your place. The packaging said the distance had to be line of sight, but we found the sensors could be spaced farther apart and still work. Bit of a heads up: these sensors will also pick up someone walking as well as some animals! (Figured that out when one of the sensors chimed 3 times; no car but three deer walked by! ) They came with a small charge (I'm assuming for set-up purposes), but I recommend charging them before use. This has definitely exceeded expectations.
title: Sensors = peace of mind

As for the brightness, its definitely not gonna light up your vaulted ceiling living room like it does in the photos. But I can see each individual star on the floor/ceiling/walls/furniture when it's in my sons 10'×12' room (AT NIGHT). And while I probably couldn't walk through the room without stubbing my toe because it doesnt illuminate the entire room, it is a gorgeous effect and works great as a night light for my son. So nooo.. it's not a table lamp that will brighten the entire room like a fireplace but it works for the exact purpose I bought it for. 100% would buy again.

[ For images please refer to other reviews, not much difference in what you would expect compared to their photos. ]

The Lepow 15.6 Inch Full HD 1080P (1920x1080 60hz) USB Type-C display comes with everything needed to plug and play. The unit also includes a flip cover/stand and power adaptor similar to that commonly found packaged with modern smartphones. The flip cover/stand is loose fitting and is attached to the device by magnets located within both the monitor and the screen. The adherence of the cover to the monitor leaves you wanting something more sturdy, such as a washable adhesive. The monitor also includes a screen protector. Using the utmost care, a roll of tape and a flat plastic card, I still received bubbles underneath the protector.

Using a 26800mAh portable battery bank, the monitor works well with Nintendo Switch, and Samsung Dex off of a Galaxy S10+, 512 GB, 8GB ram.

Audio from the monitor's 2 speakers is the quality better than an Amazon Echo (gen 3) and google home mini. I have not had much time playing music on it, but I would like to think it is on par with an S10+, below a Tab S6 speakers. As a portable device, the speakers work well for playing games and watching videos.

To utilize the device with my laptop (HP Spectre X360 15.6, intel i7-8705G CPU w/ AMD Radeon RX Vega, 16gb ram) I would have to plug the USB-C to USB-C first to power the portable monitor, then if I felt like charging the laptop I could plug in the (laptop) power adapter. If you are using this method, be sure to plug into the correct port of the monitor, as one can supply power and video, while another supplies only power. If the connection is attempted with the laptop plugged in, the monitor is not recognized and does not receive any power to turn on.

Currently using the portable monitor in conjunction with my desktop computer to stream videos while working/gaming. The video seems dull, but brightness is only set at 65 with the included screen protector. My desktop computer specs: with Intel i7-6800k 3.4GHz CPU, 32 GB ram, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 (2 in SLI).

Overall, the metallic exterior casing of the monitor feels premium and the lack of an internal batter assist in keeping the weight of the device to an acceptable weight for most people to carry around. The flip cover/stand works for the device because of the portable nature but leaves you wanting something more in the way it is secured to the monitor for transport. Image quality is smooth, moving through the built-in menu takes some getting used to and can be considered intuitive to average computer users.
title: Quality product at a affordable price

Love this Echo Show. It has a much larger screen and I can easily read it from across the room. The only issue I have is that I am disappointed with the Upgrade and Trade-in discount which offered me $30 instant credit if I sent in my old unit. My old unit sat untouched on a table for a year. It was like new out of the box when I sent it in. I wrapped it in bubble wrap and newspaper and dropped it off at UPS. Now they rejected the suggested $30 discount and have charged my credit card. The reason? Scratches. Absolutely no way there was a single scratch on that unit. I'll be interested in seeing the condition it's in when it is returned. I won't every use that Ugrade and Trade-in offer again.

Update: After a couple of weeks I just received my old unit back. I was anxious to see the "scratches" that they claimed were the reason they didn't accept it. Of course, there weren't ANY, not a single scratch. But the best part, wait for it... is that they returned it without the cord. So now, if I want to sell it I have to buy a $15 cord for it. This trade-in program is a scam and I am really surprised Amazon is okay with it. Basically, they lure you in with a higher amount and ask you to ok ahead if they feel it is worth less (which it always is, I'm sure). If like me you don't agree to take a lower value then they just ship it back to you. Beware!
title: Beware offer to Trade-In (updated 1/9/20)

text:
I tested the capacity of both of these batteries and they both rang in at around 3136 mWh or 847mAh. I measured this from the wall while charging the batteries which means that the actual capacity is much lower considering the fact that the little LCD screen on the charger is also using a decent amount of power. I get 62 mins of recording on my powershot elph 330HS with no zooming. Much less if I use the optical zoom at all.

The charger is nice. The screen lights up blue while charging and turns off when the battery is fully charged which is smart to prevent wasting energy. This is just the backlight, the lcd with the bar indicators is always on.

pros
-The charger I guess. Not any better than your OEM charger, but not a bad choice if you lost that or need another one. Still, a charger is just a charger, so I'm not awarding any stars for something so basic. Knowing how dead your battery is at a glance is actually pretty nice though. I will use this to justify the fact that I have to give this product 1 star instead of 0.
-I'm kind of grasping at straws here, but I guess the fact that the batteries actually work is a pro? Right? They didn't explode yet, which I'm grateful for. Unfortunately for grepro, you don't get stars for not burning my house down, this should be a standard feature.

Cons
-You get less than 70% of the advertised capacity. yuck

Neither, but good to know
-The charger is pretty tight the first few times you use it. I actually had to pry the battery out with a really cute fork. After a few times, it loosens and you can remove the battery with your soft hands.
-It's hard to tell from the picture I uploaded, but the battery icon in the lcd is very crooked. Beautiful job on that, guys.

I have very little faith in any of these dime-a-dozen companies selling this type of battery. I kept these batteries because I'm sure a large number of listings are lying about actual capacity and I don't want to go on a return spree. At the very least though, I can warn anyone reading this to go buy the other ones that I'm sure you have open in another tab. At least those ones "might" be better, all we know now is that these ones aren't very good. Ah, the excitement of buying niche batteries on amazon. Good luck.
title: Actual capacity isn't quite what is advertised

text:
I’m a hobbyist. I’ve had an Olympus EM 5 Mark 2 for about 3 years, using it for travel and to take photography classes. I love it! I also have a number of Olympus lenses, both Primes and Zooms. You could say I’m committed to the system. I upgraded to the EM 1 about a month ago for a number of reasons, including higher megapixel count, faster burst speed, and the larger size of the body to better match the 40-150 Pro Zoom.

So far, I’m amazed. This camera is a pleasure to use. It gives me the benefit of a compact system that produces all the quality I need. Prints in the sizes I want look great. I usually make 12x18 prints. I wouldn’t be afraid to go larger. Keep in mind that a matted, framed print this size ends up being around 20x26. That takes up a lot of wall space. Digital viewing is also wonderful.

Right now the EM 1 is also a great bargain. When 1st introduced, they were $1999. I paid $1199 on Amazon. I assume a Mark 3 may be right around the corner. I may get one. About 4 years from now. Maybe! I’m sure I’ll get some more lenses. I think camera technology for stills has gone about as far as it can. If you have been afraid to try MFT, don’t be. Buy one and go have fun, without straining your back.

I would like to thank some YouTube channels for their informative MFT videos, including Gordon Laing, Red35, David Thorpe, Robin Wong, Joe Edelman, Peter Forsgard, Sulantoblog, Rob Trek, James Popsys, Derek Forss, D Griff Gallery, Jamie Windsor and e6vlogs.
title: Buy one, go have fun, and don’t look back! Micro 4/3 rocks!

text:
This keyboard came on time, and feels premium. The top plate is metal, but I believe that the bottom is hard plastic. The color of the keyboard is awesome, and the side view letters are easy to see and light up real nice. I don't notice any real bleeding through with the light, there's some but it isn't bad. I really love the volume knob, so much better than a button, - and it doubles as a button if needed. The cord is nice and braided, wish it were a touch longer, but it is long enough. The cord is the length of any traditional keyboard cord.

There are a few small things that would have made this keyboard perfect:
1. The "free keycap puller" didn't come with the keyboard. The keys are easy to remove but still, its in the description it should come with the keyboard.

2. The keys are lightweight plastic - I think if they were a thicker plastic or a metal they'd be better. They are also smooth to the touch, a little texture feel them might be cool, then again maybe not lol. Still, this is subjective, I feel like they could feel better or more premium but they do feel good enough. It shows up the greasy fingerprint marks though, especially on the space bar, which I wish it didn't do.

3. While the light effect is nice, I am somewhat disappointed it isn't red to match the keyboard better. The pics show different light colors but so far I've only figured out different light modes. If there are indeed different light color modes instruction on changing them would make this keyboard better.

Overall I took a gamble on buying a keyboard with no review. So far I'm happy with it, but I only just got it. Last mechanical keyboard I got didn't make the year, and wouldn't you know it - it isn't found on amazon anymore. I'm hoping that this keyboard will last me many years. It has to last longer than a cheap membrane keyboard lol. I'll come back to update this review after I've used it a bit and see how it goes. But so far my overall verdict is it seems to me well worth the $80.

text: I've been using the Vantrue N2 Pro dual dash cam for the past two years. It's been a great cam. But I've wanted to get a 4K cam to see the difference in video quality. I ended up (finally) getting the Vantrue X4 and I can say the difference is definitely there. Both cams have good build quality though I'd say the N2 Pro is better in this regard. The X4 sort of has a plasticky feel to it. But in terms of actual video quality the X4 is amazing. Videos are super clear and the night videos are better too (than the N2 Pro). I also like having the larger 3" screen (over the 1.5" screen of the N2). Audio quality of both are very similar, maybe a slight edge to the N2. I love the mounting device of both units; they are top quality and allow for a more "professional" (or cleaner) look. So all in all, I give the build quality edge to the N2 Pro and maybe a little better audio quality too. But for pure images and videos, the X4 is quite a bit better. Both units cost similar in pricing so it really comes down to what you want most out of the dash cam. [Note: I've had really good customer service experience with Vantrue as well, which is why I went with their 4K unit. I had an issue with the suction cup mount on my N2 Pro and they sent me a free alternative mount that has worked out great.] Anyway really happy with the X4 so far.
title: My 2nd Vantrue and the 4K is Awesome

text: I don't need Cat6A speeds but I do like to have shielding in the house because I never know what interference I'll get in the walls and cables... I was using the Cable Matters Cat6a Tool Free terminators and love them.  But I decided to try the Ubiquiti UAP-AC-PRO AP's so I could manage everything in one location and view usages... But after receiving those I found that they were not designed well for those large connectors and there was no way to fit them into the ethernet port on the back. But I could squeeze in a normal terminated ethernet cable.  So I ordered these and a Klein VDV226-110.. mistake number one. As I am using Cat6a F/UTP it is some thick stuff and the Klein will not crimp the rear ground shield, These are not pull through so you have to try and fiddle the cable to the correct standard and length while removing the foil and then get the cable to fit into a tiny guide and into the connector, NOT easy on the F/UTP shielded sold strand cable.  Went through three connectors trying to do that.  The little plastic guide for these connectors expands in the middle and wont hold the individual strands in a good order to insert into the connectors.  Another problem I had was after crimping the connectors I didn't have a good way to compress the ground/shield support so I couldn't get the boot on all the way.  Then when I twisted the cable to get it to fit into the Ubiquity AP, the ethernet cable strand would twist away from the internal pin connection, causing the cable to go bad... I could straighten it out, it would work, twist it, and fail.  Definitely not good for solid cable and tight spaces.  These might be ok using a tool like the AMPCOM One-step RJ45 Ratcheting Crimper that will also crimp the ground/shield support and stranded cable but otherwise don't buy this for solid shielded cable.  I am really disappointed in these for the price and plastic quality.
title: Not good for solid shielded Cat6a

This hub is attractive and seems well-built at first, but frequently disconnects devices while plugging in another device. This may be because of the USB-C connector, which somehow doesn't manage to fit into the port very well. Also, when they say SD Card Reader, they really do mean READER, as in READ-ONLY. You cannot write to an SD or Micro-SD card. This means, for example, that you can't delete photos after importing them.

UPDATE: It's not a flaky plug. When plugging in a new device to the hub, any existing devices are momentarily disconnected. Not a big deal for a mouse, but a thumb drive in the middle of a write operation could be corrupted by this behavior. And it happens Every. Single. Time. you insert a new device.

I therefore conclude that this is junk and that nobody should buy it. Lowering my rating down to 1 star.

I re-set the CMOS with jumper as well as removing the battery no luck. Used the MSI bios flash with USB (by renaming the latest BIOS to MSI.ROM) and flashed the BIOS following the instructions - result no luck! All in all the board doesn't POST to BIOS at all. Thank god it is Amazon and I requested a replacement as I have this board with me only for last 2 days.

The board had all features I need to build my 3rd Ryzen based system, Unfortunately I lost half a day chasing this MB and BIOS issues. Unfortunately no where I can find what C6 means.

If anyone know what is the C6 error is I would like to know more about it. I have the MB packed to be returned to Amazon and waiting on replacement. May be I will return that too as I am not in faith with MSI. This is the first time MB giving me trouble in my last 23 plus years of building PC.

I own about 7 different echo devices, dots, spots, shows, etc. Along with 4 fire tv sticks.

I got this studio with the intention of replacing the built in speakers on my main living room tv, which is only really used with a Fire TV Stick.

Setting up the device was a breeze, just as all echo devices are. The real exciting part was when creating the Audio System for the Fire TV stick, which also was an incredibly easy process, and then I was up and running.

Overall, while I am not a sound engineer, I think the sound quality was pretty incredible. Granted, I’m moving from built in tv speakers, however, the bass was punchy and smooth, balance feels great. When playing music, it’s a fully immersive sound that fills the room. While it doesn’t compare to a full scale surround sound system for movies or watching TV, it does sound great and is a very easy solution.

As all echo devices do, this studio integrates perfectly with my existing ecosystem, multi-room music, etc. There do appear to be a couple bugs, biggest one I found was when asking this device to play Spotify, it won’t play it on that device but in an entirely different room. I’ve seen reports of this bug and assuming that it’ll be fixed soon, as Amazon doesn’t seem to let bugs like this hang around too long.

Overall, a great device and I’ll probably be getting another shortly to pair them in stereo.

Installation can be troublesome if you block access by MAC addresses to your network. On your home network, disable MAC access, review clients on your network, add the repeater's MAC (and/or devices) then re enable MAC address restrictions.

The MAC printed on the sticker attached to the product is NOT the MAC the repeater used to connect to my home network.

Devices connecting thru the repeater will NOT use their MAC address-they use the manufacturer's MAC prefixed to the device's MAC address.

Again - On your home network, disable MAC access, review clients on your network, add the repeater's MAC (and/or devices) then re enable MAC address restrictions.

Range seems to be adequate. Works well with 2 Roku TVs in upstairs bedrooms with repeater located in stairwell and home network router in basement.

Don't waste your time with WPS. Remember- access the repeater's interface on the IP address of the repeater. Better yet plug into the Ethernet port and configure the repeater from there.

Once you get past installation I think you will be satisfied.

text:
Just ordered my FOURTH HD10 tablet, and have been using Kindles since first day they shipped a kindle fire, I think that was 2011. I believe we are up to 10 readers and tablets over the years now, so I am mostly totally satisfied with the Kindle Fires. That rave review stated, the ONLY HD10 I have that still works is the one purchased in 2019, and hopefully the fourth one when it gets here. Ha. When the first one (gen 5 purchased 2015 i think went bad a couple of years ago, I thought it was the battery had gone bad, which I suppose can happen within a couple years of lots of use. When the gen 7 one purchased in 2017 went bad the same way, (won't charge), I researched and asked other people with them, and it seems the charging port is the weak link. The port goes back or makes a bad contact, or whatever happens to it, and then the HD10s wont charge at all. Amazon please address this... As a long time customer and a happy one, after buying four HD10s now in 4-5 years, and two of them already gone bad for the same problem, and others having the same problem, I am sure you are aware of the quality problem. I always use the Kindle charger that comes with the products, because I dont trust the quality of the USB cable, for my tablets, even the ones sold on Amazon. I see the new HD10 has a new type of charing USB 3, so I am hoping the connector on this one is already upgraded in the tablet. My only real complaint but it is a big one with tablet failure and you cant even get your tablet to come on any more. Otherwise it was working perfectly.
The display is great, the speed is good for most applications that I use, easy to use and a good value, if it lasts more than a couple years. For Golf Clash fans I do not recommend any HD10 I have had, not sure about this newest version yet... Golf Clash will tell you when you complain of glitches in the game of letting the ball go or disconnects that it is not optimized for the Fire tablets and they are working on it, but it does not change. Other than that, I have had no problems with any apps I have used. NOT a dedicated gamer, so don't consider my review for other games.
Would be nice to hear from Amazon about an upgraded charging connector in the tablet that does not go bad so easily. How about that Amazon? Ha!

text:
I bought this case as soon as I got my Acer Chromebook 11 C740-C4PE (fits great with this model!) Soon after, THUMP! WHUMP! Every time my Chromebook has slid off my bed, I've tentatively cracked it open, a lump in the pit of my stomach, only to find it running like nothing even happened. The case itself is near-indestructible. A year to the day (and countless 2 foot falls) a tiny bit of corner has finally chipped off, but it still fits fine. Speaking of fit, this case snaps on securely. You won't find it popping off at random, inopportune moments, yet it detaches easily enough if you apply enough pressure to the right area.
Whoever wrote in their review that the colored cases "make it look like a children's toy" are, at best, incredibly insecure, or suffering from some severe visual aesthetic disability. My purple case, especially when attached to my black C. book, makes it look chic, unique, and subtly yet elegantly feminine. In study groups or meetings, where everyone else's is grey or black, nobody's going to accidentally grab your laptop (nor vice-versa) and it's easy to find. The size and weight difference is negligible.
The only "con" is true for all these types of cases. If liquid is spilled, especially something sticky, remove the case immediately. Otherwise, you have liquid stuck between the case and the laptop -- seeping into important components. Imagine Mountain Dew drying on your CPU fan, congealing into a viscous, sticky, gel-like substance. The removal of such things (if your laptop survives!) demands either a high repairman's fee -- if they don't deem it too disgusting to work on -- or arduous component disassembly and grueling -- albeit delicate -- cleaning.
In summary, worth every penny! Go purple!
title: Has saved my Chromebook from falls time and time again!

text:
The Aumox PoE switch is a great value. I had been looking for a small PoE switch to replace the various POE injectors I am using for my access points. When I first opened the package, I was impressed by the small size of the switch. The power brick is about the same size as the switch, so I just used some dual-lock fastener to put the power brick on top of the switch to help with a cleaner installation. Granted it would look even better if the power brick was just a little bit smaller.

It was important that the switch had gigabit to maximize the AC wireless from my Access points. The Aumox provides a gigabit speeds. I have the switch powering 3 Ubiquiti AP ACPro. What is great is that this switch is almost the price of 1 their PoE injector, which again is great especially if you need to have more than 1 AP.

The Aumox quickly powered on the access points without any issues. I ran various speed tests and I was getting my advertised speed of 250/15Mbps on internet speed tests via the switch. No difference in speeds between using an injector and moving to the Aumox.

I plugged my laptop directly to the Aumox and performed a file transfer to another device on my other switch and confirmed getting speeds of 112MB/s which is approximately 0.896gbps. This is impressive considering the overhead and that I had my APs also plugged into the switch.

Another important item for me on a switch is that it is fanless with quiet operation. I know with POE switches they can get warm, however, after using my switch it seems to be passively cooled and feels the same temperature as my other devices.

Overall the switch seems sturdy with a good build quality. It’s a great value for the price and I highly recommend it to anyone needing a POE switch for their access points.
title: Great PoE Switch at a great value

text:
This dock is featured on the front page of the official DisplayLink website, and headlines a 2018 pamphlet alongside wireless VR. It's probably featured elsewhere on DisplayLink's website for good reason: it's probably the best solution a home user can get as a TRULY universal dock. And at a good hundred dollars less than other USB-C docks with Power Delivery. It's worked with most everything I've plugged it into, even older USB 2 devices. Just remember that you HAVE to install software from DisplayLink for this to work.
Also there are some hell devices that just won't work, no matter how excellent the DisplayLink standard is for universal compatibility. An old Nexbit Robin I tried using just refused to work. Had the software installed and all set up just like other phones I tried this on...no dice. I guess Nexbit was too garbage to implement the USB standard correctly, as that is the LITERAL only way it would fail to connect right. Last thing that wouldn't work is super-old systems; DisplayLink runs off of the CPU and can get intensive to run. So make sure to test it within the return window with everything you want to connect it to! That said, there isn't another dock at this price that supports DisplayLink and Power Delivery through USB-C. Get it!
title: Maybe the BEST DisplayLink dock. (at this price)

My decision was tied between these and the airpods pros. But after using these for close to a month, they're really amazing in close to all areas.

SOUND QUALITY: Top notch. I'm an audiophile and these sound amazing, especially compared to other brands at this price point ($150). EQ in the app is good and packs a clear, deep bass with rich mids and highs.

NC and Ambient Sound: Also very good, the eartip seals out noise and the NC drowns out white noise in the background. Ambient sound doesn't sound too artificial and useful when walking the streets. Earbuds can automatically detect what you're doing and adjust.

Fit: I thought these were gonna be a bad fit considering the size but if you find your right eartip, you'll be golden. I used them for jogging and working out (I sweat a lot) and they didn't fall off (surprising.) Tip: pull your ear back while inserting into the ear for a really good fit. Follow the instructions.

Product design: Clean and looks pretty. Durable.

Battery life: I applaud the amazing battery life. Will last me 7 hours of playback time on one charge with NC on at a cafe at high volumes. Combine this with USBC charging.

Product itself when shipped: Doesn't come in original packaging but was packed well and in new condition. No scratches whatsoever.
title: An amazing all rounder at this $150 price point.

From start to finish: This is an amazing buy, and great case. To address the most common question, my operating temp, running the same workload, has dropped from average of ~57c to currently ~36c. Switch between file transfer, web video playback, usb video playback, and retro pie psx emulation, no problems save for file manager needed to be reinstalled post update; open terminal and run "sudo apt-get install --reinstall pcmanfm -y && reboot" which will rebuild your file manager with permission "-y" and then "&&" reboot :).
Now for the case: sturdy as can be asked for unless you want solid aluminum. Smooth finish on top with hard acrylic base. The fan/gpio board works flawlessly and quietly partnered with amazing ventilation leaves a nice cool pi. Indicator lights in front with the ports in rear gives a sleek appearance with professional functional design. I went with the power supply option so I've incurred no issues on supplying power to multiple usb devices. The audio works without issue and the power button is an awesome feature, granted the time between soft shutdown and forced is o ly ~2sec of long press time so not ideal there(my only complaint so far). Over all I don't think I'll ever need another case for this pi, and look forward to the next iteration with the pi 4 which I'll be getting in a few months.

Overall: is it quiet: more than you'd expect
Is it good looking and high quality: couldn't ask for much better
Does it have all instructions and support needed: plenty plus extra features not yet discussed in the main advert(infrared for those feeling froggy).
Does it meet power reqs. And still function okay while gaming: yuppers
Will it get you a girlfriend?: no but my non-tech artist of a wife think it looks like a legit mini pc and loves the magnetic gpio cover.

When I plugged it in, something happened to my PC in regards to the startup page when turning the system on. It wouldn't load past the Gigabyte Screen, and BIOS couldn't solve the issue. After 8 hours of digging, a friend and I found a way to get the PC to boot with the card (we didn't know it was the card at the time).
Several days later, I updated my Radeon RX 5700 driver and the PC automatically restarted and refused to boot. It was very frustrating, and it also happened several other times (all with other drivers in the system) after I rebooted the PC back to before updating the driver. We had done a speed/practice build of the same PC a week earlier-without the Wifi Card due to late shipping. So, I went ahead and updated the drivers and waited for the boot error, turned off the PC and unplugged the Wifi Card, and turned it back on.
Voila, it worked.
For some reason, the card didn't like the AMD build of my PC. It did have all of it's driver installed, so there was no reason for the strange issue. It was easy to install, got great signal, but the product itself had major problems while working inside the PC-earning it a 2 rating.
I hope this troubleshoot helps and warns people who are considering on buying this product. Maybe it'll work for you, or it might be your worst nightmare for 2 weeks straight.

text:
I bought these hoping they would be better for transfering bass sound than the silicone ear tips that came with my Sennheiser M2 Iei IEMs. I was also hoping they would be more comfortable because the silicone ear tips are fairly sharp at the edge (side closest to the earbud, not the one in my ear) causing a scratchy uncomfortable feel. Unfortunately the sound to my ear is more muddy and less bassy in the foam tips for sure. The comfort I find worse than the silicon ones because when they expand in your ear after you place them in, they have a fair amount of pressure in your ear canal, but it doesn't have the same scratchy feel as the silicon ones which is a plus.

There are two advantages that I can find to the foam tips. One is that they stay in my ear much better, so if you were using them while exercising they should stay in better, and the second is that they are a fair bit more isolating than the silicon tips I have.

Something I would be careful of if you want to order these, is that the sizing isn't exactly the same as silicone ear tips. I wear the medium sized silicon tip, but I find the large foam tip fits my ear the best, so if your ordering these for your first time I would advise buying the multi sized pack.

text:
I ordered two of these cases to go with two rasberry pi 4's for different projects. I don't know if the case, the pi, or both were out of tolerance; however, the first case I opened would not allow the USB C port to clear. When I tried that pi board with the second case it fit and the second pi fit with the first board. With the first pair I probably could plug it in but was not going to be able to align the single post with the screw hole on the pi.

This brings me to my second issue, the pi has 4 holes for mounting screws, this case uses one of them and the ports are used for the remaining points of contact. I would have been much happier with 4 posts to screw the pi onto rather than relying on the ports for support.

Finally, the cases have different sized fans. One allows for all four screws to be attached and one will not align with more than two screws attached. This is a minor annoyance to me but seems to continue the pattern of poor quality control. Of note, the case that had tolerance issues with the first pi was also the one with the misaligned fan. The fan came preattached while the directions indicated it would not.

Having gotten the cases assembled I am happy enough with them to keep them, they seem solid, despite the single hard point of contact.
title: Decent case once assembled, tolerance issues and a design flaw

I remember first seeing the articles about these and getting excited about them, Then radio silence for months. Obviously there was a lot of anticipation for these, as I kept seeing people around the internet asking when they would be released.
I bought them pretty much as soon as they were released, and they were great for the first few weeks. Then the connection issues began. One earpiece will randomly lose sync, or it just won't pair at all. Seems to happen most when I'm moving around. I've had to reseat them in the case, in hopes they reconnect (another inconsistency), repeating the process several times in some instances. I thought maybe I had a bad pair, and klipsch's customer service was outstanding in getting me a replacement set. But the replacement set has the same issues.
Then there's the app. I think most people have just given up on it because it seems like every month, they'll release the app next month. Just go look at the twitter page.

As much as I want to love these for their sound quality and battery life, I'm honestly about ready to toss these in a drawer and revisit them in a year or two in hopes that klipsch will have the issues sorted. Btw, these issues have persisted across two sets of headphones with two different phones (LG G7 and galaxy note 8).

And good luck getting them to stay in your ears. I constantly have to adjust them when I'm wearing them, which also affects sound quality.
title: Definitely released before they were ready.

Unfortunately, that never happened for me. The sound (mainly dialogue) coming out of the center channel is horrendous. It sounds like the sound is coming through a tin can. The rear speakers and subwoofers rarely - if ever - give off any output. I spoke with technical support initially and they just e-mailed me the steps to walk through with my Samsung TV and how to upgrade the firmware (all of which I had already done). That still didn't work, so I contacted tech support again. They advised me to disconnect the HDMI cable and go purchase an optical cable (was not too happy about having to purchase an additional cable, based on the money I already shelled out for the system). That still didn't rectify the problem. So I've had a useless surround sound system sitting in my den for months that I don't even have powered on. I've been using the sound coming from the TV, which is far superior to the awful sound I have coming out of the the Nakamichi system. This is not what I spent hundreds of dollars for. After several back and forths with the tech support team again, they are finally offering to replace the system with a new one. Unfortunately, they asked me to e-mail my purchasing invoice to them - which I attempted to do - only to have all of my e-mails returned, saying they are undeliverable. Now I can't get them back on the phone, either. This has been a terrible experience all around!

**UPDATE ON FEBRUARY 11, 2020

After waiting over a month for my replacement, I finally inquired to see what the delay was. "Customer service manager" Alberto told me he needed to set up another call with me, which I didn't understand why. Certainly seemed like they were reneging on their offer to replace the broken system. I arranged a time to speak with Alberto and even left work early to get home for the call. Wouldn't you know, Alberto never bothered to call. I even gave him three more days, in case there was an emergency that prevented him from calling me. Nadda....zilch. Talk about the ultimate disrespect for a customer! I've now had a non-functioning unit in my home for 7 months and am DONE trying to deal with this company. They are an absolute joke! I've now filed an official complaint with the Better Business Bureau to return and get a complete refund for my unit. I want NOTHING with the brand name Nakamichi in my home. text:
Ok, so this isn't made to be used for extreme overclocking or anything like liquid nitro cooling.

BUT. It works amazing if you are a gamer who owns a stock or cheap cooler, you pop this on and can most likely get a decent overclock at stable temps, as I was able to with my AMD Ryzen 2400g, went from 3.9 to 4.5GHz and get about 50 degrees at max use, and 20 at idle, gonna get another to try to cool the RX 570 in my build.

Overall, cooling is amazing with a lapped IHS, and maybe even a lapped cooler if possible, overclocks are easier to manage due to the graphite, and is very useful for part testers and component resellers who test CPU's but don't want to shell out 100's a year in thermal paste. Plus you can pop it back in its box, and save it for later if you upgrade your PC.

Now, the big shortcoming of this pad though, is that it can ONLY fit basic Intel/AMD CPU's with a basic square IHS, meaning Threadrippers and certain Intel CPU's will not have fun when trying to stay cool with this pad.

But after all the key points, it's a nice thing to have, certainly worth the cheddar.

text:
Sure, it's on the lower end of the Thunderbolt 3 dock pricing spectrum - but it's still $200 and for that much I expect a product that does what it's supposed to do without having to think about it. It's a dock. It should just sit there and connect my computer to things. It does not. Here are some of the problems I've experienced since purchasing this dock about 1 month ago (none have been resolved despite dealing with CalDigit tech support and going to the trouble of installing 3rd party beta drivers):
• First and foremost, when my computer goes to sleep with the ethernet cable plugged into the dock it brings my entire LAN down with it. The whole house and anything connected to WiFi included. This is completely unacceptable and makes one of the primary uses for me (hardwired network connection) very frustrating to use.
• When waking my computer from sleep the external display (connected via DisplayPort) is not recognized about 75% of the time. I have to unplug the thunderbolt cable and plug it back in. Then wait. Then unplug it again and wait. Then plug it back in. This is not why I bought a dock. If I wanted to plug and unplug cables all day long I would have saved my $200 and bought adapters.
• There's an obnoxious blue light on the front of this dock that can not be turned off. If you plan to work past sunset you'll have to find some black electrical tape like I did.
• There's no micro SD card slot, only standard SD. I knew this before purchasing but really should have thought more about it because those micro->standard adapters are yet another step I have to go through when I want to get something done. If it weren't for the other issues I probably wouldn't mind that much, but it's just one more annoyance I have with this dock.
That's all I can think of at the moment. When something else goes wrong I'll try to remember to update this review.
title: Major Software Flaws

text:
I purchased these to replace a waterproof mp3 with the in-ear earbuds for lap swimming. I tried two of the most highly rated in-ear earbuds, but never was able to get them to work comfortably and consistently with water leaking into my ear and cutting off the sound. The Aftershoks are a much better solution for swimming. They stay in place (without swim cap) in turns and the sound is very good and consistent underwater and are very comfortable to wear.

I use these primarily for swimming and since Bluetooth does not work underwater, having the built in MP3 player is the only real way to get music in the pool unless you want to swim with wired earbuds and your smart phone. The sound quality is good with or without the ear plugs. With the ear plugs I did not notice much of a difference between pool and normal mode. Without the ear plugs, the sound is much more bassy and would recommend pool mode. Whether or not to use ear plugs is mostly personal preference on sound and comfort. I am on the fence. One complaint was would be nice if the volume could get louder, but the volume is definitely adequate for lap swimming.

Copying music over was straight forward, but formats are limited, so you may have to convert some music files (that are not format protected) to acceptable file types. Of course, you have to own the songs and can’t just download from one of the subscription music services.

While the xtrainerz are the best music delivery device for swimming and would highly recommend them, I am sticking with the in-ear wireless ear buds and my smartphone for non-water activities as the sound quality is superior and I have more options for music.
title: Great solution for music while lap swimming!

text:
Ok I bought this unit about a year ago and have been using it ever since so figured with a year use I will have decent enough feedback for a review. First off since it's being advertised as a usb mining hub. With the current miners on the market in 2019, this hub is NOT really designed to handle them. The Sapphire Block Erupter back in 2013 and Bitmain's Antminer U1 for example were ideal for this hub. However today's USB miners being Gekkoscience Newpacs and Futurebit's Moonlander 2 are not ideal. As they need minimum 2.5 to 3 amps per port to run these miners correctly. And this hub does not deliver if you are going to use more than 3 of any of these types of usb miners. I currently have 3 Moonlander 2's running on this hub and that is maxing the hubs usage. If I put a 4th Moonlander on this hub then it starts resetting the Asic's due to power issues.

With Newpacs it is worse. You can only run 2 newpacs on this hub. Anything more than that and you will run into power issues for the asic miners.

So final break down on what I gave it 3 stars. Mainly the build of the unit and quality as it is pretty solid and has been dependable for what I've used it for. I deducted 2 stars for 1: Advertising is outdated. This product is no longer suited for usb miners. It is now more of a data hub / charging station only. And 2: which backs up the outdated advertising is not being able to run more than 2 (newpacs) or 3 (moonlanders) usb miners on this hub.
title: Decent USB Hub however outdated as a USB Miner hub

text:
In recently lost my longtime earbuds that I have been using for two years. Saw these on sale and thought I'd give them a go.
Let's break this review into categories; sound, ergonomics, connectivity, and usability

I'll start with,
Ergonomics:
These are tiny, and super lightweight. I used the large ear tips, and they feel like they are in there to stay, no falling out or anything like that.
I kind of wish they went in a little deeper though. I find myself pushing them in trying to get a better seal in my ear.
I was able to sit through hours of watching the Witcher on my IPad very comfortably though.
Other than wishing they were a little deeper, my only other complaint is that the hard plastic body, gets uncomfortable if you push them all the way in, but I think that would be an issue with any earbuds with this design.

Usability:
I'm not a fan of the button controls, they "click" which is a bit uncomfortable in the ear. The aside of that is that there are no accidental button presses. Once you learn what button combination does what it's fairly intuitive (except volume control) triple clicking on an earbuds sucks, and often times results in a track change.
But pausing Netflix when walking away from the iPad or when someone is talking to you works well.
Also the charging case is fun to play with, satisfying clamp on the lid. The earbuds are definitely in there and will not easily fall out. I typically have to use a thumbnail to get them out.

Connectivity:
Seems great overall, but I have had times where (in the first day) the right earbud will lose sound for a quick half second. It's very jarring when it happens. I was Within 2- 3 feet of the iPad when this happened. I can listen to them in different rooms and overall connectivity to my IPad pro, and my Moto z2 force seemed good
Speaking of which, these can only connect to one device at a time. You have to manually disconnect to change devices, not a deal breaker for me.
There are significant delays in audio from YouTube, and more pressingly gaming. Played call of duty mobile... Sound comes a bit after the gun shot.

SOUND
Very clear sound, these are great for watching videos and all the words are super clear. The highs are absolutely perfect.... Maybe I got a defective pair though, because other reviews mention bass, there is none on the pair I received, bass was completely absent. I tried Spotify, Netflix the epic orchestral track of the Witcher
sounds awesome, just sans bass. This may be the deal breaker for me. I turned them up tried some bass heavy tracks, and nothing. Again, they are very clear, but don't expect to hear the bass drop.
Outside of that one gripe I actually really dig these, I cannot recommend them with that flaw though, I used the largest eartips to try and hear that bass, but it skipped these buds.
Oh, and these do not sound isolate, let alone noise cancel. Good in some cases for situational awareness. I would probably wear these to the gym, because of the comfort, you really can almost forget they're there.
title: Comfortable, clear sounding earbuds

text: I have the ML Motion 4i as a full 5.1 surround system with a Motion 8 as the Center and a Dynamo 700W Sub. I decided to buy the Motion LX16 for the front channels as an upgrade. After listening to them right out the box I was about to return them as I could't hear a big perceptible difference. I decided to wait for the break in period before making a decision. Its been about 20Hrs of break-in and the difference is huge. I read a lot of reviews about the bass being weak on these but sense I already had a good matching sub that fact didn't worry me much. After some break-in time I have to say that I have been very surprised by the bass on these, it is night and day compared to the motion 4i. The biggest improvements have been mids and lower mids and now there is a big difference between these and the Motion 4i. They really have gotten better by the day and have come alive. I 'll be honest and say that I did not truly believed the whole speaker break-in talk until now. Martin Logan speakers have a distinct sound signature and are best for jazz, blues, classical, vocals and best with acoustic music especially guitar (which is my kind of music). If your are into pop, hip hop ect.. there are other speakers that might be better (Elac, Klipsch). Not to say they are not enjoyable with all genre of music, is just that they are very revealing, detailed and dynamic but might lack a bit of punch. Maybe adding a second sub will make them even better.

text:
I actually had a different printer half setup when I saw this at Best Buy, did a ton of research and then took that down and bought this instead. I read through most of the reviews here, went on Consumer Reports. Some of the bad reviews were from people basically not using it as directed.

What sold me on it was the following:
1. It will scan up to 8 4x6 photos at a time (and save them separately), as well as any artwork I create up to 11x17.
2. It will print in wide formats, up to 13"x19" which gives me a lot of options.
3. The 7720 also has OCR (Optical Character Recognition), which will convert scanned text as live editable text.

So far? Amazing! Contrary to some reviews, setup and network connection was a breeze, wireless printing was so fast, and scanning has been high-quality and richly balanced in color. The large touchscreen is enjoyably responsive and laid out very clearly. I have plain paper in one tray and photo paper in another. Spending 15min flipping through the online manual gave valuable info (what paper goes where, presets, etc.) and I was off and running.

As for being an ink hog, it will use less ink on the correct photo paper than on any non-photo paper. Make sure the print settings match what you're printing on, and you'll be in good shape. Plus, there's enough options to dial in the settings and save them to presets. If it uses more ink in maintenance, I'll gladly buy an extra cartridge a year to have this kind of power at my disposal.

This is a versatile machine that gives you options not many all-in-one printers can, and none other that can match it's scanning ability, a huge plus in my studio. Print quality here is damn good, certainly good enough for my presentations, projects, and display artwork & photos. The speed in the video is actually how fast it prints, incredible.

Highly recommend!

And if you are still struggling, invest in an attic or roof antenna. The difference in capabilities is exponential. text:
This review is for the GNV34DB which I believe is the newer model of the GN34CB. The major difference between the two are a sharper curve on the GNV34DB (1500r vs 1800r) . Also the manuals on Viotek website seem to indicate that the GNV34DB has better RGB coverage (99% vs 96%) not sure how accurate this is but the GNV34DB appears to be the superior and newer product and its also weirdly cheaper.

First off the monitor needs to be calibrated, calibrating this monitor drastically improved the color and contrast. Make sure you go into the setting on the monitor and check that everything is currently set. I used lagom website's calibration test to calibrate gamma and contrast and ended up with 100 brightness and 70 contrast for around 2.2 gamma, using the contrast test color banding looks excellent after adjusting each rgb channel gamma using windows calibration. Calibrating the display using just your eyesight should produce a decent result , but if you need more accuracy you will need to buy a calibration tool.

tldr: This is a great router. It is very cheap for what you get. If it lasts a year it will have paid for itself by not renting one from an ISP. Signal is ok, could be stronger. Don't buy unless your wifi can already take advantage of at least 802.11ac, and preferably ax to get the most out of it.

Buying our own router instead renting from the ISP saves about $10 to $15 per month, so they have a tendency to pay for themselves if you choose wisely. We had an Archer C7 router for about 6 years that I paid about $100 for and although it worked great overall it was starting to show its age a little too much. When the time came to upgrade I looked for an ax router to future proof our home network for a while and was hoping to find something in the same price band.

For an ax router in this price band the pickings were slim. I ultimately chose this one because (a) it was the cheapest option, and (b) it had good reviews. So far I am very happy with the selection.

It was very easy to set up out of the box. In a ~2600 sq ft three level townhouse with the router on the middle floor we get signal throughout, although the 5 ghz band is weak upstairs and on the far side from the router. The Archer C7 5 ghz band didn't reach there consistently, though, so at least now there's access. Previously, I had to use the 2.4 ghz band and was getting about 2 Mb/s over usb wifi using 802.11n. A combination of this router, an ax-capable PCI-E wifi card, and being able to get a 5 ghz signal means I now get about 80 Mb/s on the same computer, which caps out what the ISP will give me. The difference is night and day.

So far, any issues I have would be nitpicking. I wish the 5 ghz signal were just a little stronger and the router's interface is merely functional which means it could be cooler to interact with. I personally am very happy that it just has one small LED indicator light on the front instead of the nearly dozen flashing icons on the Archer, but I guess some other people might prefer it the other way. I had to get a new wifi receiver for the computer to take advantage of the 802.11ax standard, but that was something I knew going into this. Do not buy this router unless you (a) already have a wifi receiver that can use at least 802.11ac, or (b) plan to buy a new one that can use the 802.11ax standard. If you don't do that then just get an even cheaper one that still uses 802.11n because the extra bandwidth will never be used.

Overall, I was very pleased with the resolution and ease of color adjustments with this monitor. It was easy to setup and didn't require much image tweaking before I was looking at a bright, vibrant picture that just popped off the screen. I played a bunch of YT videos on it, all of which looked great. But I don't play computer games, so I really can't comment on that, but the impressive specs seem to suggest many gamers should be happy with this monitor.

Unfortunately, the deal breaker for me was the lack of any window snap software. I know this is a feature with Windows 10, but it was less than intuitive and requires memorizing various keyboard commands to move just a few windows into place. I also tried a couple of third party screen snap applications and they, too, required heavy keyboard command mastery as well as endless "enable/"disable" settings for terms that required numerous online lookups just to understand what they meant. On the other hand, the screen snap software that came with a top brand monitor was real easy to work with - merely point and click for a large variety of screen snap formats. That's what I needed. So, with much regret, I returned this monitor, but the company was very good about it and quick. So, I thought the least I could do is write a nice review for them. So, in summary, my guess is this monitor would be well suited to gamers but not so much to business application users like me that need an easy screen snap application. But if the company were to include that, it would probably outsell it's generic brand competition.

You can ask Alexa what's playing or to play a song on Sonos, but oddly you can't do the same via the touch screen. What a waste.

text:
There is a handful of radiator selections for the corsair water cooling line with some thin, some thick, and then different measurements.

I recommend making sure which size will fit your case as I originally got this one, the 240mm one and a 360mm thick one. Turned out the way I wanted to put stuff in my case there was no way the 360 would fit so I ended up getting a second 240mm thin one which allowed me to put one on the top of my case and on the bottom. Both of them got two fans to cool them.

In the icue software you can make your own profiles or in the setup if you have the hydro x pump it will go through a wizard and ask which ports on your commander pro (sold separately but definitely needed for the corsair setup) has the pump and which ones have the fans.

I found even during heavy graphics everything stayed nice and cool. The radiators can get hot which is the idea.

As far as the radiator itself? I found it solid and really unless you are doing some serious overclocking, the 240mm radiators I found did the job just fine.

I think this is a good time to get into corsair's line of water cooling if you are thinking about it as early on the icue software was buggy and difficult to manage. Now I find it is very stable and while there is a learning curve, once you learn it you really do have complete control of the Temps in your computer.
title: Solid 240mm radiator that just works.

text:
This is a really great and affordable drawing tablet, especially for people who have yet to get far into digital art. It's cheap, comes with multiple bonus art programs, and has helped me become a better artist myself. Know however that if you get this product, and find difficulty with it, more often than not, it's not the fault of the tablet. I know there was a time where i couldn't use my tablet and it wouldn't register my inputs. I thought i did something to break it, but in the end, it was actually my computer denying me the inputs because it didn't recognise the tablet after some update. All you have to do to fix that issue is to reinstall the driver, and the customer support really helped out with that.

I love the life out of my tablet, but know that if you decide to buy it, it doesn't mean that you'll immediatly become a great artist. It takes time and practice for anyone to use, skilled or not skilled in art. If you can't immediatly create something awesome don't blame the tools for it. Best thing i've ever bought on amazon by far
title: It's a great way into doing digital art

text: I got this as a way to put stickers on my laptop's back without ruining it or leaving any little paper tears on it if i wanted to fix it. When it came, i snapped it onto the top and bottom part with a little difficulty. It had some trouble getting a grip on my computer on for the first day, but eventually it was snug. Now, this is affordable, and pretty cheap for a laptop cover, and though it still "technically" works today, it's not what it used to be. After about a year of use (and i've heard this from some other college students who got this brand too) the laptop cover starts to break. For me, after about 6 months, the little nibs on the bottom part came off first. I replaced them since then but after another 6 months, they all came off again aswell. One of the more annoying issues is the "cracking". The case will eventually (bottom part) crack at it's corners, and this sometimes can lead to a cut on your wrist if you're not careful. Overall though, it was cheap, and the part I actually needed it for (the textured part that goes over the top) does do it's job very well. For me, it passes as an ok product, though just be aware of this stuff before buying.

text:
I've held off writing this for a few days so I could make sure my review includes at least a few days worth of pretty heavy use. So far, it has performed very well and met pretty much all of my expectations after several hours of use.

First of all, I was careful to follow the instructions for first use, including charging the unit fully (at least 2 hours) before using.

Once fully charged, I followed the instructions for powering on and pairing. The instructions were clear and simple and the unit paired successfully with my Bose QC35 headphones in seconds. It reconnects to the headphones without trouble every time I turn it on.

So far I have only used it as a transmitter, not a receiver, but it has worked great transmitting from my PC, my audio interface (home recording studio gear) and my stereo receiver for my home entertainment system. In all cases, the audio is clear, powerful and nearly free of lag.

I say "nearly free of lag" because there does appear to be a few milliseconds of lag for video (YouTube, TV, etc.), but it's almost imperceptible unless you're really fixating on it and I find that my brain seems to compensate for it quickly to the point that I don't even really notice it anymore. It is not distracting for me and has no effect on my enjoyment of whatever it is I'm watching. Naturally, lag has no effect on listening to music or other audio only sources.

I have also noticed the sound cut out once or twice at very low volumes, but it was really quite low and even then it only cut for a second. It's not something I would consider to be a problem or a defect.

As far as build quality, the unit is very small and very light, not much heft to it, but it does not feel "cheap." It feels very tight and sturdy, the button feels substantial enough that I'm not afraid of it breaking under my thumb. The unit has a really cool almost velvety surface texture to it as well, which lends an air of quality to it. For its size and for the price, I have to admit to being rather impressed with the look and feel of it.

So far, I'm very pleased. I'll give it a bit more time and use to be sure, but I will likely end up buying a few more.

text: I just got back from a 4-day event that I executive produced.  We bought the Hollyland Mars 300 hoping to simplify our roaming stage camera setup so we didn't need a cable puller and weren't limited in movement.  The one thing I was reading with these was that there was enough noticeable delay that it wouldn't be real time enough to want to show someone speaking or singing.  To that end, we took a gamble on it anyway and told the roaming camera operator to avoid faces and focus on giving us color shots.  What surprised us was that when he got some faces we noticed that the video was perfectly in sync with the audio.  I think the thing that we didn't consider is that there is delay/lag in the entire system, including audio, and from a live audience view, your brain is just more forgiving with small delays.  We ended up lifting the restriction on our roamer and got some really great angles on live speakers and musicians.  I can't recommend this product enough, it worked flawlessly for all 4 days!

Important points

-Update the machine's software and drivers before you do anything else,it will be a lengthy process so don't plan on any immediate gaming. Don't neglect the dragon center either, because that can be helpful if used right, this is not a novice's computer, but it is good for a novice.

-The system needs to be configured for gaming so that means setting fan speeds to loud and cold, Also I would highly recommend a cooling station for the lap because it will need it, they do get hot without one.

My last semester of school, I was able to wake up naturally with the sunrise & found I was much happier that way. Now I have to wake up around 5:45 and at first found that I was having a very hard time waking up and had a tendency to be in a bad mood. This has genuinely made a huge difference in my mornings. I’m able to wake up feeling rested & not like I’ve been abruptly shaken awake. I have an easier time being cheery & getting myself going quickly. I forgot to set it one morning and definitely noticed a huge difference.

Two things worth noting:

I don’t rely on the alarm function to wake me up. I use the alarm strictly to schedule a sunrise, so to speak then I rely on my phone’s alarm to wake up about 20 minutes after the “sunrise.”

I also found that the sunrise is incredibly bright. Of course, it’s meant to be that way but it is not very pleasant if you have the clock on your nightstand facing you. So I actually turn the clock away from me. It’s a much gentler sunrise and arguably a better way of simulating a sunrise since you never look directly at the sun during an actual sunrise.

I would purchase this again, no question & recommend it to people all the time.

I collect Bluetooth headphones as an expensive hobby.. these are some of my favorite! They look great, feel natural when wearing, and pair without any issues. Out of all the different pairs I own (probably 10+) these are the only ones that feel as if the audio is just being “played in my head”, like I’m not wearing headphones and have some kind of receiver implanted or something. It’s nice and feels futuristic! The case lighting is a really nice touch too, it doubles as a conversational piece too when I open it in front of others.

My only critique is that they pair when you open the case. They would be better off pairing when you remove them as you may only want a single earbud in. text: Don’t buy this. It is way too cheap & does not spin evenly, causing anything you play on it to sound warped. In addition, possibly the worst of all, some of the components occasionally rub against the record as it is playing, ruining your vinyl. The combination of these factors is unbearable. I had to give it two stars instead of one because it does *technically* spin and play music, has stereo out ports, and has multiple RPMs, but it is just bad quality. You are better off purchasing a higher quality turntable unit to avoid warping & deteriorating you vinyl. You should only buy this if you absolutely must play your vinyls & have no other choice, even then get cables and run the sound through anything else, (TV, laptop, etc.) The wobble on this unit alone makes it basically unusable regardless of anything else.

text:
EXCELLENT MP3 SHUFFLE PLAYING SPEAKER. Plays all mp3s on a microSD card in random order. FM is good, Short wave is good, I guess. AM radio play is noise, noise, noise. Otherwise, its a great radio overall. Shortwave is pretty much dead. Nothing but a waste of time. Back to mp3 play. Added.... also plays .wma files in addition to .mp3 files.
-
Copied five thousand (5,000) mp3 files on a 32GB microsd card and decided to test out the Retekess TR102. ran it non-stop for three weeks with no problem. Six months later and its a mp3 playing beast. Playing 5,000 mp3 files randomly (shuffle). This is a shuffling mofo!
-
Basically, hundreds of folders. Each folder filled with songs from an album. A folder full of miscellaneous classical music. folder of miscellaneous classic country. folder full of religious music. 3 folders of gunsmoke seasons 2, 3, 4 free from archive.org, 3 free dragnet season folders. six-shooter folder. Folder with 20 free This American Life episodes. Folder with Bullseye with Jesse Thorne. ETC. This is a shuffling mofo!

- You can only select play modes when Mp3 files are being played from microSd Card. See A,R,F, or 1 in upper left of display.
A=Play all songs in folder order, R= Random play all songs on Sd card, 1=repeat playing current song, F=Play songs in current folder
Shuffle play mode (R), folder play mode (F) and play all mode (A). This radio has a MENU button that lets you set/adjust the sleep timer, contrast, backlight on time, language and the mp3 recording quality. When you are playing mp3 files, the menu button allows you to choose. A-mode or F-mode or 1-mode or R-mode. In A-mode, plays all mp3 files in current folder, then plays all mp3s in next folder, etc. In F mode, plays all mp3s in current folder, then repeats playing the mp3s in the same folder again and again. In the 1 mode, plays the current song repeatedly, again and again. In the R mode, plays all mp3 files on the microsd card in random order.
....... ADDED... Above shuffle info also applies to Retekess v-115 and the Tivdio v-115 .
Unfortunately the tivdio v-115 has a fatal software problem that cant be fixed. Freezes. Must remove battery to restart.
-
DISPLAY: the big display shows the title of the song playing . current song number and total number on microSD card. and many, many more details.

.....ADDED... MP3 File NAVIGATION
... Two ways to navigate the songs on the MicroSD Card.
Navigation Method #1: Direct number input. If you know the order files and folders were written to MicroSD card. Say you have 100 files on card, if you type 51, you will land near the middle song. Type 99, you land near the end song. ETC.
Navigation Method #2: [ROOT] With MP3 playing, Press and Hold ENTER (>||) button . then Press and HOLD word "ROOT". Will take you to the mp3 currently playing (Rolling Stone) and the folder the mp3 sits in (Highway 61). use << or >> navigation buttons to move through files in folder. At end you will see [UP LEVEL] to folder contain your folder or the ROOT level (Dylan Albums). Play with it and you'll come to understand how to navigate.

-
How to play continuous music. I discovered that this radio will run forever on a simple 5 Volts 1/2 amp cellphone charger with microUsb connector. Yes, you can even remove the battery and power the TR102 on the charger power alone. Its a beast! External speaker play. The tr102 has a 3.5mm headphone jack. So i can be plugged into external self powered speakers.
-
If you are just looking for a great AM radio, stop reading and look elsewhere. AM radio play on the TR102 is crap. Too noisy! FM radio play is good. Shortwave is dead. Nothing on shortwave. Don't waste your time.
-
At twice the price, the Radiwow R-108 is a really great AM budget radio. Especially after dark when the massive 50 watt stations start transmitting across the country. Radiwow R-108 is a Great and Magical Radio. The Radiwow R-108 is a Great AM, FM, and Aviation bands radio. It plays showtwave too, but SW is dead in the US. Automatic time off. Automatic turn on and back off. and much more. However, the Radiwow R-108 has no mp3 player. No mp3 play.
-
The sleep timer is not automatic. Has to be set each time. At bedtime, choose Menu > Auto Power > Hit Select Button > use the << and >> buttons to choose 10 to 90 minutes > hit select button > Done. Radio will power off after time selected.
-
TIP: FM and shortwave uses the long extended antenna. AM uses a coil antenna built into the case. So, no need to extend antenna for AM reception. Extended FM antenna may distort AM radio reception.
-
CON: The Retekess TR102 has a serious AM noise problem. The retekess tr102 is marketed as as an upgrade to the retekess v115. While it is an overall improvement, it is a real downgrade in AM performance. AM Noise, noise, noise. Why would anyone release an radio with such a major defect? If Retekess finds a way to eliminate the AM radio noise, it will be a really great device.
-
Finally. If you are OK with good FM, good Shortwave, and excellent MP3 Shuffle Play, Run and get this Radio/MP3 Player speaker. If you need good AM reception, keep looking.
---
Not a Prime Member? Add a $5 microUSB 5volt, 1/2 amp (500 milliamp) cellphone charger. to meet the $25 free shipping minimum. OR $8 32GB microSD card. Retekess TR102 take a maximum 32GB MicroSD card.
-
DISPLAY: the big display shows the title of the song playing. shows length of mp3 and elapsed mp3 playing time. mp3 bit rate. 32kb, 64kb, 128kb, 256kb. battery level. Mp3 playing order mode: A,F,1 or R. shows total number of mp3s in current folder F (folder) mode. Or number of mp3s on microSD card if in R (shuffle) mode or A (play all in order) mode.
-

The backlight goes off at a set time. The Display is always visible in a lighted room. In the dark, backlight is needed.

Why not just use an old smartphone to play mp3s? True, a smartphone can do many of the functions of the Retekess TR102. But a smartphone does not have that big 2 inch diameter speaker. A Smartphone's thin speaker slot can not compete against the TR102's bit speaker. It sounds much richer and clearer than any phone speaker slot. Also, most smartphones can not be used a an external self-powered speaker either.

3.5mm Line In Port: You can plug an external audio device (mp3 player, cd player, computer) in to the Line in Port. Makes the Retekess TR102 a portable self powered external speaker.

My personal gripe with Retekess. My first Retekess device was the Tivdio v-115. It was a good AM/FM/SW radio and mp3 player until the software went crazy. The whole system would just freeze-up or show Chinese characters only. I later discovered I was sent version V1.3 well after newer versions were issues. A dirty deal, indeed. I can't find a way to update the firmware to fix the Tivdio v-115 problems. I guess that's why the Retekess TR102 was made.

text:
I got these for Christmas. Ive been using them for a week now and I’m not impressed. The product Leaves much to be desired. The tech definitely seems rushed. The Alexa feature works half the time if you’re lucky. They also disconnect from my iPhone foo frequently. The tap gestures don’t work in an efficient manner. There’s no volume or pause gesture. In order to pause music you have to take the bud out of your ear completely. This is very Inconvenient. There’s a way to change the gesture settings but I shouldn’t have to do that just pause. Once you remove the Bud the touch gestures still trigger and action.... it’s frustrating especially if you are trying to have a conversation.
Echo products and nothing new to me. I’m very familiar with how the platform works. My issues are not user error.
Also that pass through is a joke. They need to work on that too.
All in all these headphones are no good. I feel like Amazon has rush this product to get it to market to compete with AirPods Pro and sacrificed actual functional ability. I’m going to continue to use them for another week but as of right now I’m planning to return them.

Update (6 days later)
I really tried to give these a second chance. I think my frustration grows day-by-day. It's just a bad product. They are a constant disappointment.
when I use the buds on a phone phone call, they start going crazy --- audio (the person on the other end of the call) goes in and out while noise canceling/passthrough function toggles on and off sporadically. This happens almost every phone call.
If you want to use the alexa feature you have to give the command twice, sometimes 3 times. This is every time I try to access alexa. connected to wi-fi or not.
The touch gestures do not work. Even after adjusting the settings in the alexa app. Its extremely frustrating. You can't even adjust the volume on the actual buds... WTF?
Also, if you are only using one bud, and holding the other (because the only way to pause is to remove the bud... dumb) the touch gestures still trigger a command. So you can accidentally make calls, access siri/alexa, toggle passthrough. this needs to be fixed. Its extremely annoying while having conversation.
Buds do not stay connected to my iPhone --- triggering media to play through my phone speaker LOUDLY --- I haven't had to deal with headphones doing that in years!
These are just a few of the problems I've had with the echo buds. I could keep going.
Did Amazon even test this product before releasing? apparently not!

I LOVE echo products and really, really wanted these to work. I've been using them for about a month and am so disappointed. I can't wait to return these.
Take these back to the drawing board.... you have more work to do...

P.S. I hope this review doesn't disappear like my original review did...
title: ONE WEEK UPDATE Rushed tech. Don’t expect much... keep looking

Review of Ubit Wifi 6 Bluetooth 5.0 EIDE Card:

As a user of the former Ubit Wifi 5 Bluetooth Card, this Installation was a breeze. I installed it in place of my Wifi 5 card and shut up my system and booted it up. There were no drivers to install or software changes to be made.

Further testing was done in order to see how much faster the Wifi 6 card really in a Wifi 5 LAN environment. After 10 or 12 tests, I was very impressed. Got more speed that I thought I would since the receiver was a Surface Pro 4 laptop that was obviously Wifi 5.

First I tested with the old Wifi5 card for a base measurement. My test file was a 341,270 K file in all cases.

Wifi 5 to Wifi 5 Average 66.3 seconds to send file = 5147 KB/second

Wifi 6 to Wifi 5 Average 52 seconds to send file = 6563 KB/second (27% faster)

GB Ethernet to Wifi 5 Average 30 seconds to send file = 11,375 KB/second

I didn't test the Bluetooth performance since both cards were Bluetooth 5.0.

I'd really like to see the difference if BOTH ends were Wifi 6 but I don't have another Desktop and card to test with. I'm very sure the tests would be better than all of the above.
