text:
Firstly, any new headphones will take a good few hours of listening for your ears to "adjust" to them, so keep that in mind. I love their neutral audio balance. The bass is definitely there and you hear it clearly and audibly, but it's not going to kick you in the head. The neutral balance is unique to Bowers & Wilkins in the way that you can hear the entire range of audio, no matter what style of music you listen to (and trust me, I listen to a healthy amount of rock, metal, and electronic styles).

Next, along with the neutral audio balance, the positioning of the sound stage is superior to the competition. The drivers are pointed forward at about 30-45 degrees, so it sounds like your face is right in front of a speaker and the sound comes from right in front of you, then forms around your head and into your ears. At least, that's what it sounds like to me after my ears adjusted.

The only set-back is the microphone on these. Yes, you can take phone calls using the Bluetooth features, but good luck trying to get your friends to understand what you're saying. It's best to use these strictly as an audio listening device, forget the phone call features.

Apart from the lack of microphone functionality, the REST OF THE FUNCTIONS ARE INCREDIBLE for these headphones. They know (most of the time) when they're being taken off or onto your head and over your years, they'll pause the music when one or both of the ear cups are not on your ears. They come with a USB cable that serves not only as a charger, but also WORKS ON PS4 (and maybe other gaming consoles?) AS A USB AUDIO DEVICE! Furthermore, my favorite part, they come with a 3.5mm-3.5.mm cable to use as direct line-in audio for those of you that want to hear it through your fancy Quad-HD HiFi DAC device.

Noise-cancellation is pretty darn good, but could use a little improvement. I work in a noisy office and when I put these on High ANC I can barely hear the loud chatter and clicking of keyboards & mice. However, I think the Active Noise Cancellation is still not up-to-par to completely cancel-out the decibels of walking down a busy city sidewalk.

Lastly, but equally important to the rest of why this got a 4-star review, the BUILD QUALITY IS A HUGE IMPROVEMENT FROM PREVIOUS GENERATIONS. The leather material on the ear cups is soft, comfortable, and doesn't press against the top of my jaw line like the P9 headphones. The leather ear cups are removable and replaceable if they wear-out or get damaged. The PX7s are durable, made with brushed carbon fiber (same material that you'll see on Ferrari or Lambourghini cars in some cases). Despite their weight/mass, they feel lighter than they are, which gives a boost to their comfortability rating.
title: Better than previous versions, worth the price!

Installed the Samsung 970 NVMe SSD 1TB in my Macbook A1398 yesterday. So far, so good – haven’t had a chance to test it hard in the real world, but my before and after read/write stats show an impressive improvement. Apple SSD - 1876/1255 vs. Samsung 970 - 3028/2572 (MB/Sec).

Here’s a checklist of the main parts/steps you’ll need.

1. Backup to TimeMachine
2. Build a bootable USB stick (check Apple's website for info specific to your OS)
3. Install new SSD – photos attached
4. You’ll also need:
- A Sintec NGFF M.2 nVME SSD Adapter Card for the SSD to interface with the Mac - available from Amazon
- An oGoDeal which includes a Pentalobe P5 1.2x50 for the case screws AND the Torx T5 to remove the SSD - available from Amazon
5. Boot your Mac from the USB drive created in step 2.
6. “Erase” the new SSD using the Disk Utility. Format with APFS (best for SSD) and GUID Partition Table
7. Restore system from Time Machine backup. (May take an hour or so…)
8. Enable TRIM - you'll find plenty of search results on how to enable

text:
I previously reviewed this product, and said that it was a really good buy. But in fact, I've changed my mind with time. The problem, I've found, was that once power is actually pulled, they don't hold up voltage levels. This morning, power flickered here. We're talking < 2 secs. No big deal, but my computer was off when I came down to use it. This was not the first time. As long as it was down, I took a few minutes to test the battery. I unplugged everything else from the battery ports, and connected a voltmeter. Power output registered at about 120V, which is perfectly fine. Then I pulled the power plug from it, and watched as the voltage level dropped down to a variable output of between 98V and 105V. And that's why my computer is losing power. But that's not why I wanted a battery backup unit. I've had this unit since March. Didn't expect it to last forever, but also didn't expect it to never quite have worked properly. Serves me right for not testing it right early.

In any event, if you're looking for a surge protector, this one is fine, but you can get cheaper ones that'll work just as well. If you're actually looking for a battery backup that will keep your devices up during brief power events, don't rely on it.
title: Don't rely on this

text:
This mp3 player will pair with a bluetooth device, but it can't compare with the SOULCKER mp3 I bought in May of 2019 for about the same price. This device has a small speaker that will play music without earbuds, but the sound quality is a bit "tinny". See below for specific comments on observations/performance.

Pros:
1. The mp3 body is boxy and solid.
2. The charging port is sturdy and doesn't wiggle when plugging in the Micro B charging cable. (Note: the connector does not go in very far. This is not a problem. The device charges fine.)
3. It has a retro ON/OFF switch with buttons for volume control and "waking" the device screen when it goes black.
4. The screen has minimal black borders.
5. Adding songs to the MYMAHDI playlists is simple. The user taps the list wanted on the song's screen. (Click the "folder +" icon then choose...Collector 1, Collector 2, or Collector 3. Click the "heart" icon to add to favorite music...list is named "favs").

Cons:
1. The touchscreen is slow to respond to the user's touch.
2. The charging indicator is a static image of a USB connector. The user has to guess when the mp3 player is charged.
3. The bluetooth battery life is roughly 8-10 hours. The battery life is longer with wired earbuds.
4. There is electronic noise (chittering) when connecting/connected to bluetooth earbuds.
5. The instruction booklet's font size is too small to comfortably read without magnification. (The MYMAHDI instruction booklet is compared to another product's pamphlet for font size comparison in the image.)

Suggestions:
*Add an alarm clock function.
*Add a better search function for songs/artists/albums (searching by initial letter would be nice).
*Allow users' to transfer their playlists from their computer or device to the mp3 player intact (with playlist name and songs).
*Update the charging indicator to display another image or color when the mp3 player is finished charging.

Obviously fixing the problems listed above is also required to make this mp3 player worthy of the current price. I did not include the small, on-board speaker in my rating. I will be returning this device, but I will consider purchasing the MYMAHDI mp3 player in the future if the company significantly upgrades a newer version.
title: Not worth $50 for this mp3 player.

text:
I originally purchased a Celestron LCM80 for a family Christmas gift at a hobby shop about an hour from where we live. We got it out of the box and it was missing the software download and the finderscope. It was disappointing seeing how our kids went from being excited over their new Christmas gift to being sad that it didnt work. I took it back to the hobby shop and got my money back as they didn't have a replacement and we didn't want to wait on getting the parts from Celestron. I went to order a replacement on Amazon and the price we paid at the hobby shop was slightly less than the Nexstar 4Se offered by Amazon. I did some research and the Nexstar 4Se seemed to be a better telescope than the LCM80 and it also included the rs232 cable to connect to our laptop for additional control. This really sweetened the deal since the LCM80 did not include a rs232 computer cable. We just had to purchase a rs232 to USB converter cable for $15.

About a week later we were excited to get our new NexStar 4SE. We got it out of the box and inventoried the parts. We got the finderscope and software download this time but there was no rs232 cable. The getting started manual showed the rs232 cable should be included. I contacted Celestron and they said the new on-board computer doesn't require an rs232 but does require a straight through USB cable so they quit including them. So now we are short of a computer communications cable and we purchased a USB converter cable for the rs232 that is now useless. After looking at some other amazon reviews for this product it is apparent Amazon knows this cable is not included yet they still advertise that it is included. This is deceptive and they should change the description of the included items.

We got the scope mounted on the base and went to align the finderscope with the telescope and couldn't see any light being reflected into the eyepiece. We followed the quick start guide and rotated the flip mirror control and still no light coming into the eye piece. I looked inside the OTA and was unable to see a mirror. I contacted Celestron and was told that this is very rare but the mirror is only held in place by a piece of double sided tape and something might have damaged it during the manufacturing process. It doesn't sound like the mirror is loose in the OTA but instead may have never got installed (there is no visible tape residue on the plastic piece that supports the mirror) at the factory. They suggested I send it back to Amazon as it was clearly defective. After reviewing other Amazon posts for this telescope it looks like this problem might be a frequent occurrence. I am sending this one back and am hoping we get a working telescope that includes all the parts listed on Amazon's site. I will post an update after getting a working unit.
title: Defective telescope out of the box. 2nd Celestron with missing parts advertised as included

I had high hopes for this product. Sadly I was very disappointed. Here's everything that was wrong with it:

- Screen has no adhesive. I was willing to overlook all the other negatives but not this one. If I had figured that out earlier I would've returned this; unfortunately I found out too late. What's the point of a replacement screen if there's no way to stick it back on? I had to use Krazy Glue.

- The suction cups don't work. Besides the fact that they were deformed, you have to apply force to make it stick. Applying force to an already broken screen increases the cracks, which reduces the ability to stick. Get one with the suction cup where you flip a "switch" or something.

- The wet cleaning pad was dry. So there were two dry pads. And they were small: 1"x1". Would've been nice if they were at least 2"x2".

Everything else was fine: the other tools were pretty good, the screen itself works great, the fit was great. It was a cheap way to extend the life of an already obsolete product for kid usage. And definitely watch videos, more than one so you can figure out what works the best.

I had to write this Ring review because I am extraordinary disappointed with this camera.

This camera, by far, is the worst camera I have had after trying Wyze, Blink, and Canary. I thought because of some of the reviews on Amazon as well as some of the reviews on websites through Google that the camera would meet an average expectation of security. However, it has not!

I own a medical business that requires security and surveillance at all times. Ring is limited in its ability to pick up on traffic going through my hallway because of its inability to pick up on motion from a distance. A lot of the people coming in and out of my practice were not picked up on by this camera because of the short distance that it records. The other issue with ring is that I had a 60-day subscription free trial and after it ended I lost ALL of my footage that I had wanted to save and transfer to a USB drive.

Most of the surveillance is extraordinarily important in my practice and if I don't have it that poses an issue.

Ring's unsophisticated subscription service disposed of all of my videos because it wasn't on the cloud when the subscription ended. I don't see this as a good product because if there were hardcore evidence on that camera that I needed to prove something or to protect my business, I would not have it any longer.

I should not be forced to purchase a subscription (and purchase it immediately before my free trial ends so I don't lose my video storage) after paying $100 for a camera that I believe should provide recorded "copies" of all videos for free.

I returned this unsophisticated device to the store and I will NOT be purchasing or recommending another Ring device. The device claims that it can be used for businesses but I HIGHLY discourage this.

I have five Canary cameras and I went and bought the sixth one after I return Ring. Although not perfect, I feel that Canary at least provides the security that I need in my business.

Highly dissatisfied with the Ring product.

text:
I'm not far enough into use to leave a thorough review but I did have some issues right out of the gate and have had no support at all. The printer came with a prominent sticker touting attentive support and an email address but email sent to the provided address bounces as non-deliverable. I sought support through Amazon and was told I'd get a call from a representative but never did. I'm on my own, it seems, and was able to work through some initial problems by trial and error. Beyond setup, prints are having issues with adhesion to the build plate, despite my using the included glue stick and the hair spray recommended by another reviewer.

The printer itself seems well designed and I'm very encouraged by my first attempts, time will tell. It's a little lost and lonely at the moment though.

==== UPDATE: A COUPLE WEEKS LATER ====

After about 75 hours of printing, my problems got a lot worse and was unable to print anything, nothing would stick to the build plate at all. I tried switching to a new filament and went from bad to worse.

I finally reached Tang for support and he was very responsive and helpful. As a 3D printing novice I needed some help assessing the issues and Tang provided that and more. Most helpful was a video demonstrating disassembly of the extruder which helped me identify a rookie mistake I made unloading the filament, resulting in a completely blocked filament tube.

As to my print quality and adhesion issues, those were maintenance related. I had not kept the print nozzle clean enough and (worse) had cleaned it in a way that damaged it. I ordered two nickle plated replacement nozzles (recommended) and a PLA solvent (Ethyl Acetate) for gentle cleaning.

Presently, I am printing again with eSUN PLA Pro filament which is fantastic and am very pleased with the prints. The printer is simple to use and, once you get familiar with its needs, performs very well hour after hour. I used to order prints through an online service and this printer has already paid for itself.

text:
This Television was a holiday gift for the family - an upgrade from an older, smaller set that was starting to show its age. For its size, this set was very reasonably priced - not the best deal out there, but the cheaper options all had fatal flaws. The feature set is solid, the picture quality quite good and with an effective 120 Hz refresh rate, it's bright and responsive. Color saturation is good with minimal or no bleedover, even when contrast is high. Audio quality is surprisingly good for a flat screen, and can be very loud. There is some distortion at high volume, but not anything really noticeable at any volume you might consider comfortable. Set-up is easy, if somewhat tedious as the unit had to download and install three iterations of updates before it declared itself ready. It's currently connected to our network using its built in wifi, but it also has an ethernet port for a faster, more robust connection if desired.

Ports are plentiful - there are four HDMI inputs, one USB Type A port and the above mentioned ethernet. You can also connect coax or conventional Composite video sources, though I don't know anyone that uses such things anymore. The set is Alexa compatible, though you will require an Alexa device to use that feature. This was important to me - the set has neither Alexa nor Google Assistant built in - if it had, I would not have bought it. The set is also compatible with Apple's Home Kit - a somewhat harder feature to find, but one that appealed to me since our family is invested in the Apple ecosystem. Whatever your choice of digital assistants, though, this TV will likely work with it.

The remote is fairly comprehensive - but somewhat awkwardly laid out. The most common controls used in our household (most notably the input select) are not as well placed as they might be, but that is a small complaint. Build quality seems good - the supplied feet are metal, easy to install and fasten securely. The set is also VESA mount compatible for those that wish to wall mount it. Good cable management is a must to keep things tidy and the various connections easy to trace.

A few caveats - be sure to check the packaging - the first unit that I ordered arrived damaged - the box had been struck fairly hard and the frame of the set was bent and the screen badly cracked. A return/exchange was easily set up on the web - the new set arrived just a few days later, and was in perfect condition.

As for the set itself, the on board software required updating during set up - it took while but was a straightforward procedure. The Netflix app on the set crashed a few times, and getting it to operate correctly required a reboot of the TV. Apple Airplay works well, but again, we had a lock up that required a reboot to correct. That has only happened once so far, though so I do not consider it to be serious issue - if that changes, I'll update my review.

Bottom line - for the money, this set is hard to beat. You can get a much better set, of course, but you'll pay correspondingly higher prices - and this unit does everything I want a TV set to do, and does it well. If you're in the market for a good TV set and you haven't got a lot to spend, you'd have a hard time finding better.
title: Feature Rich, Budget Friendly

I have not used the motion sensor activation feature. I did contact Andoer tech support via email, but received a response in Chinese that translated to a mailer auto message saying the mail was undeliverable because the recipient's mailbox was full. text:
This is a well designed push-pull power amplifier. Going with the a dual rail 45Volt supply will yield the 100 Watts as advertised. The power transistors are top notch and the drivers are on a nice size heat sink. Make sure you use a decent size heat sink for the power transistors, say at least a 5" x 5", per pair. I am going to mount them on a 12" x 5" x 1.3" Wakefield Vette aluminum fined Heat Sink, about $35 bucks from "Mo***er" Design a nice power supply or buy a
good linear one that will deliver at least 4 amps. Stay away from switching supplies for audio stuff. I know that sounds old school, but it is correct. I am an EE. Also you should shield the power supply from the amp proper, or even better put it into its own steel enclosure. Then use a circular Amphenol connector to run the cables to the amp enclosure. Amphenol part PT02E-10-6P(072) and Amphenol part PT06A-10-6P(072) will do. These are 6 pin, you only really need 3, but this way you have extra conductors for fans and such that would reside in the amp proper enclosure. Use the 5th and 6th wire for the fan drive and use the 6th as the ground, that is attached to the chassis of the power supply enclosure with a wire connecting the power supply enclosure to the amp proper enclosure. This way each of the amp supply rails will have a floating supply. If you do it this way, use some good 6 conductor sheilded cable, with 18 AWG stranded wire and tie the sheilding on the Power supply end to the chassis. I make my own cables using good Mil spec PTFE insulated wire and a metal braided sleeve capturing the ends where the connectors attach with heat shrink.

Also use a stand by switch that goes in the center tap line of the transformer ( a good toroid), and place a 450R, 5 Watt resistor (Ohmite 45F450E) across the switch with a 0.1/630V Cap in parallel to reduce in rush current. When you first turn to power supply on, wait for about 30 seconds before you close the stand by. This will give the amp and power supply components a little bit to heat up, and reduce the inrush current. When these components are cold, they have much lower resistance than when hot, on the order of a magnitude. The 450R resistors allows approx. 100mA of current to be delivered; heating things up a bit. This will increase longevity of all the components especially the toroid and power supply devices. Also I would use fast diodes in the rectifier or use a bridge and then place one fast diode on each power rail right after the bridge; user a 30ns device that is say 600V at 10 amps
(ROHM RFN10TF6SFHC9).
I would cut the Wakefield Vette HS 125403 in half midway and mount each board to one the orient them so the fins face each other in the middle with about 2 inches betwen them. Place a fan on the under side of the top of the enclosure, one at each end, and two in the middle; that have at least 100 cfm capacity. When designing your supply, you can add a L7824CV 3 terminal regulator with a TO-220 clip on HS to the output of the positive side, with a 0.1uF/250V PP Cap on either side of it and a 100uF/100V eCap after the one on the output side. Each fan will draw at most 150mA if you select them right and use the 24Volts to drive them. Use 12V fans and pair them wired in series and you will have a nice rig. If you need anymore help comment and I will reply.

text: Okay so I bought this computer a while ago and I just got the hard drive replaced. If you do buy this computer, I would highly recommend changing the hard drive immediately. The Toshiba hard drive in any Toshiba product is as reliable as a Chrysler. It worked fine the first day, until I tried using it the next day. It couldn't find the hard drive even though it was inserted correctly. When I eventually got a replacement, the guy who fixed it told me about the reliability of Toshibas hard drives and showed me a large stack of 20 broken ones that he had stored over 4 months just to show as an example. So I wouldn't store anything on the computer until you replace the hard drive. But this computer is powerful, and handles great with games. I use FL Studio and play games on it and I had no issues with the speed of the computer. It can also be upgraded if you want more power out of it. If you can look past the (very possible) hard drive issue, then it's a great computer. But I put 3 stars on the value because of the issues with the hard drive.

text: This was a gift for my husband.  When he turned it on the was really pleased with the sound quality and the buttons you can pre-set stations with.  It also has a nice feature where you get several choices on how bright you want the display to be.  The biggest issue we had was with the time set-up.  The radio comes with the ability to have the time automatically pick up the time from the FM station you are playing on the radio.  At least in our area, the radio stations clocks are all over the place and the time confusedly shifted from minutes off to hours off as you changed stations.  This seems to be the default mode, but you can change it to manual time, but read the owners manual carefully to do this.  The first two times he tried to reset the time, he just reset the radio station time which didn't solve the problem.  You need to click on the radio-control icon and then move to Manual to turn the radio-control time off. Once we did that we were able to set the time accurately.
title: Nice Radio but pay attention to the manual

text:
I received this monitor as a Christmas gift this year - I specifically asked for it. I have not been disappointed so far!
The main reason I wanted the monitor was to maximize my efficiency and productivity when working from home. I run multiple displays at work, so it's always been difficult to transition to a single laptop screen when working from home. With this portable monitor I can just plug a single cord into my laptop and then I'm off to the races!

The picture quality is better than expected. It's definitely a HD screen. The images are crisp, everything is very readable, and the colors are vibrant. I have been primarily using this with my Surface Pro X, so the screen size is almost the same size as my Surface's. This is ideal and makes everything look very deliberate. Additionally, the smaller screen size of this monitor is great for its' portability. It very easily fits into a small laptop bag right alongside my Surface.

The folding stand/cover that it comes with is also great. It protects the monitor's screen from possible scratches/debris. It also functions properly as a stand. It has two slots for different viewing angles The stand works as intended, steadily holding up the monitor in either position. One of the big bonuses for the cover is how thin it is. It adds a negligible amount of width to the monitor itself, and essentially no additional weight.
Another bonus is the cover is easily removed by unscrewing the two hand screws on the back. It's also very easy to put it back on.

I've also been using the monitor as a small, portable Dex station. To do this all I need is a USB-C Dex compatible HDMI converter. All I have to do is plug the HDMI cord into the monitor, use a USB-C cord plugged into a wall adapter for power, and plug the Dex converter into my phone. It's incredibly easy to do.
It's been great to actually be able to utilize the Dex capabilities of my phone with this monitor. It basically lets me have a laptop at the tip of my fingers. It's something I'd never really had the opportunity to explore until I got this monitor.

Overall this is a fantastic little gadget. It's something I'd easily buy for myself, and am actually considering buying a second one. I put a lot of thought into which portable monitor I asked for for Christmas, and price for quality this one is truly hard to beat. I would heavily recommend this monitor to anyone who has a need for small second monitor that won't remain stationary.
title: Fantastic addition to a mobile work station
